Weekly Family Update – 
02.10.26 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters Most 
What a fantastic week it has been at Abbey College. I continue to be impressed by our 
students’ positive attitude, hard work and commitment to making a difference to both 
themselves and those around them. 
A particular highlight was our Year 6 Open Evening, where we welcomed over 300 families to 
the college. It was wonderful to see so many prospective students and parents exploring our 
school. Our students were exceptional ambassadors, proudly sharing their experiences and 
helping visitors see what makes Abbey College such a special place. 
A special mention must go to Evie in Year 7, who spoke brilliantly about her first four weeks 
at Abbey College. Her confidence, warmth and engaging delivery captivated the audience, 
and she represented the school exceptionally well. She should be incredibly proud of herself 
and has a very bright future ahead. 
I would also like to thank our Parents' Forum for the outstanding support they provide to our 
school community. Their fundraising and commitment have helped us introduce initiatives 
such as our mobile phone pouches and pre-loved uniform shop, both of which have made a 
real difference to families and students. 
The first Parents' Forum meeting of the year will take place on Wednesday 7 October, 
5.00pm-6.00pm, and all parents and carers are warmly invited to attend. Whether you 
would like to get involved regularly or simply find out more, you will be very welcome. The 
Forum's first fundraising event, a Family Quiz Night, will take place on Thursday 12 
November. We hope many families will be able to join us for what promises to be a fun 
evening. 
Have a wonderful weekend. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher 

 
Please read on for essential updates. 
Vacancies at Abbey College and across the Meridian Trust 
https://www.abbey.college/vacancies  
Celebration of Spirit - Recognition 
Year 7 Spirit Lunch 
For the first time ever, Year 7 have a 'Spirit Lunch' built into their 
curriculum. Once a fortnight, students come together to build 
their sense of community by sharing lunch, serving one another, 
and engaging in interesting discussion topics. 
This week's question for discussion was: "If you were elected to rule the world for a day, 
what rule would you change?" 

The answers focused on ending discrimination and caring for those less fortunate, responses 
that truly embodied the Abbey College Spirit. 
Headteacher Commendations w/c 28/09/26 
The following students have been awarded with Headteacher's Commendations this week 
for going above and beyond in an area of school life.  They will receive 10 Spirit points and a 
special postcard home. 
 

 
Staff member of the week 
Mr Valentine: Intuition: For taking on a completely different challenge and making a real 
difference with the students. Every day is different in New Horizons, and you just go with it 
and have shown a calm and caring nature towards the students they really respond to. 
Thank you for all your hard work and support to help support them. 
Tell us about something brilliant! 
If you would like to nominate someone for an Abbey College Spirit Award for any out of 
school success stories, then please follow this link or email the Office office@abbey.college. 
Strong Partnerships 
Parent's Forum 
Date for your diary! 
The date of the next Parent's Forum meeting is Wednesday 
7th October 5-6pm. You can either join in person in the 
Boardroom or online via Teams. 
Parent Questionnaire 
Please complete our parent questionnaire to raise any questions you have prior to the next 
meeting. The questionnaire closes on Monday 5th 
October:  https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/ParentsForum26-27 
• Please email ParentsForum@abbey.college any questions.  
• Please find our minutes here: https://www.abbey.college/parents-forum  
• If you would like further information on the Parent's Forum, please email: 
ParentsForum@abbey.college   
Genevieve Wardle - Chair of Parent's Forum 

Uniform Update: Optional Plain Black V-Neck Jumper 
To provide greater flexibility for families whilst maintaining our high uniform standards, 
students may now wear a plain black V-neck jumper under their blazer. 
Please note that: 
• The jumper must be plain black, with no logos, branding, patterns, or 
embellishments. 
• It must be V-necked to allow the school tie and shirt collar to remain visible. 
• Hoodies, sweatshirts, crew-neck jumpers, or knitwear in other colours are not 
permitted. 
• The jumper must be worn underneath the blazer, not as an alternative to it. 
Family Quiz Night! 
The Abbey College Parents' Forum invites families to a fun-filled Family Quiz Night on 
Thursday 12th November in the South Hall. 
Gather a team of up to six people, test your knowledge, and compete for prizes, all while 
supporting a great cause. Every penny raised will go towards exciting new opportunities and 
resources for Abbey College students. 
 

Up-to-date MCAS details 
Please ensure that your contact details are kept up to date on MCAS (MyChildAtSchool). 
Having the correct information helps us contact you quickly if needed and ensures you 
receive important school communications. 
You can update your details yourself at any time through the MCAS app or website. 
Alternatively, if you need assistance, please email office@abbey.college with your updated 
information. 
Zebra Crossing location Survey 
The County Council would like feedback on a proposed Zebra Crossing location near the 
school. Please complete the survey here: https://yourvoice.cambridgeshire.gov.uk/place-
and-sustainability/ramsey-zebra-crossing-feedback/ 
Any queries, please contact Hanane Rouadi, Assistant Project Manager, Local Improvements 
Team, Hanane.Rouadi@cambridgeshire.gov.uk 
Diary Dates  
 
Everything You Need to Know About Assessments 
 

Ensuring Pupils Feel Safe and Behave Well 
Safety First 
Worries 
Students discussed emotional wellbeing and the importance of talking about worries early. 
They were reminded of the support available in school and encouraged to seek help if they 
are struggling. 
Useful Resources 
• YoungMinds: https://www.youngminds.org.uk/parent 
• Anna Freud: https://www.annafreud.org/parents-and-carers 
• Place2Be: https://parentingsmart.place2be.org.uk 
• NHS Every Mind Matters: https://www.nhs.uk/every-mind-matters 
If you need support or have any concerns about your child's wellbeing or safety, please 
contact welfare@abbey.college 
Promoting Positive Behaviour Every Day 
Student attendance  
Week 4 – Impact on Wellbeing  
Being in school supports more than just your learning—it supports your wellbeing too.  
Routine, friendships, and feeling part of your community all help you feel positive and 
confident.  
Coming in matters for your mind as well as your grades.  

Supporting Your Child’s Wider Development 
Offer & Opportunity Programme (OOPs) - Autumn Term 
 
 

 
Student curriculum 
How can I find out what my child is learning in each subject? 
Discover Our Curriculum 
At Abbey College, we want every student to feel challenged, supported and inspired to 
achieve their best. Our broad and balanced curriculum combines excellent teaching, rich 
experiences and strong careers guidance to help young people thrive both in school and 
beyond. 
Our curriculum is designed around three simple aims: helping students understand the 
wider world, providing an ambitious education for all, and ensuring that every learner has 
the opportunity to succeed. Parents can explore what is taught across Key Stages 3, 4 and 5, 
along with information about homework, higher-attaining students and relationships 
education. 
Find out more: View our Curriculum Overview 
Communicating with us and raising concerns 
Click here to access this Communication Flowchart on our website. 
Parent Friendly Policy Guide: 
https://www.abbey.college/key-policies--reports  
Other news updates can be found here: 
• Our news page: https://www.abbey.college/school-communications  
• Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/pg/RamseyAbbeyCollege/posts/  
• Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/abbeycollege_ramsey/

Weekly Family Update - 09.10.26 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters 
Most 
Thank you for your continued support in helping your child attend school every day. Regular 
attendance is one of the most important factors in a young person's success, wellbeing and 
sense of belonging at school. 
Every lesson matters. Being in school each day helps students build strong relationships, 
develop confidence, keep up with learning and make the most of the opportunities available 
to them. Even missing occasional days can make it harder for students to stay connected to 
their learning. 
As we approach the half-term break, we would be grateful for your support in ensuring 
students attend every day until the end of term. Students finish for half term on Thursday 22 
October. 
Please note that the following are Meridian Trust INSET days, when students are not in 
school: 
• Friday 23 October 
• Monday 2 November 
This means students will have an extended break before returning to school on Tuesday 3 
November, giving plenty of time to rest and recharge. 
Thank you for working with us to ensure students are in school, on time, every day. Your 
support makes a real difference. 
Every day in school is a day of learning, friendship and opportunity. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher 

 
Please read on for essential updates. 
Vacancies at Abbey College and across the Meridian Trust 
https://www.abbey.college/vacancies  
Celebration of Spirit - Recognition 
 

Headteacher Commendations w/c 05/10/26 
The following students have been awarded with Headteacher's Commendations this week 
for going above and beyond in an area of school life.  They will receive 10 Spirit points and a 
special postcard home. 

 

 
Staff member of the week 
Miss Andrew-Martin: Passion - Your love for creative writing is infectious. To have 30 
students regularly attending an OOP and being so proud of the work they produce there is 
wonderful to see. Thank you for being so willing to give up your time to allow students to 
feel such a sense of pride and belonging. 
Tell us about something brilliant! 

If you would like to nominate someone for an Abbey College Spirit Award for any out of 
school success stories, then please follow this link or email the Office office@abbey.college . 
Strong Partnerships 
Parent's Forum 
Parent's Forum Update 
At last night’s Parent's Forum meeting, Mrs Noble provided an overview of the changes to 
the Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) guidance and invited feedback from parents. If 
you would like to contribute, please submit any comments here:  
• Relationships, Sex and Health Education: Parent Consultation – Fill in form.  
We look forward to using your feedback to help shape our updated policy, which will be 
published next year. 
We also continued planning for our exciting fundraising quiz on 12th November, and 
preparations are well underway. 
At our next Parent's Forum meeting, Miss Lane will provide an update on how our new Year 
7 students are settling into life at Abbey College and we will look at some projects to donate 
funds to. 
• Please email ParentsForum@abbey.college any questions.  
• Please find our minutes here: https://www.abbey.college/parents-forum  
• If you would like further information on the Parent's Forum, please email: 
ParentsForum@abbey.college   
Genevieve Wardle - Chair of Parent's Forum 
Family Quiz Night! 
The Abbey College Parents' Forum invites families to a fun-filled Family Quiz Night on 
Thursday 12th November in the South Hall. 
Gather a team of up to six people for £6 per team, test your knowledge, and compete for 
prizes, all while supporting a great cause.  
There are prizes which have been donated for a raffle on the night.    

The sixth form will be running the quiz so any support would be much appreciated! 
Every penny raised will go towards exciting new opportunities and resources for Abbey 
College students. 
 
Up-to-date MCAS details 
Please ensure that your contact details are kept up to date on MCAS (MyChildAtSchool). 
Having the correct information helps us contact you quickly if needed and ensures you 
receive important school communications. 

You can update your details yourself at any time through the MCAS app or website. 
Alternatively, if you need assistance, please email office@abbey.college with your updated 
information. 
Road Safety 
 
Zebra Crossing location Survey 
The County Council would like feedback on a proposed Zebra Crossing location near the 
school. Please complete the survey here: https://yourvoice.cambridgeshire.gov.uk/place-
and-sustainability/ramsey-zebra-crossing-feedback/ 
Any queries, please contact Hanane Rouadi, Assistant Project Manager, Local Improvements 
Team, Hanane.Rouadi@cambridgeshire.gov.uk 
Diary Dates  
 
��� Inset Days Coming Up 
Please note that the following are Meridian Trust-wide Inset Days. All Meridian Trust 
schools, including Abbey College, will be closed to students on these dates: 
������������ Friday 23 October 
������������Monday 2 November 

������������Friday 27 November 
���� Please add these dates to your family calendar. 
These training days allow staff from across Meridian Trust to work together, share best 
practice and continue to improve the education we provide for all students. 
Everything You Need to Know About Assessments 
 
Ensuring Pupils Feel Safe and Behave Well 
Safety First 
Healthy Habits 
This week students discussed healthy habits, hygiene, hydration, sleep and self-care. 
We encouraged students to consider how everyday health habits support both wellbeing 
and school attendance. 
Useful Resources 
• NHS Live Well: https://www.nhs.uk/live-well 
• NHS Better Health: https://www.nhs.uk/better-health 
• The Sleep Charity: https://thesleepcharity.org.uk 
If you need support or have any concerns about your child's wellbeing or safety, please 
contact welfare@abbey.college 
Promoting Positive Behaviour Every Day 
Student attendance  
Week 5 – Coughs & Colds  

It’s okay to feel under the weather sometimes—but most coughs and colds don’t need days 
off school.  
If you’re well enough, being in school helps you stay on track.  
Don’t let a small illness lead to big gaps in learning.  
Ms Davis – Attendance Officer 
Supporting Your Child’s Wider Development 
Offer & Opportunity Programme (OOPs) - Autumn Term 
 

 
 
 
Click here 
Student curriculum 
How can I find out what my child is learning in each subject? 
Learning outside the classroom (LoTC) 
At Abbey College, we believe learning should extend beyond the classroom. Through a wide 
range of opportunities, students can experience art, culture, heritage, adventure and the 
natural world, helping to broaden their horizons and build confidence. These enriching 
experiences are offered through our curriculum and our Offer and Opportunity Programme 
(OOP), alongside trips, visits and activities such as the Combined Cadet Force (CCF). The aim 
is to give every student access to memorable experiences that support their personal growth 
and development.  
Find out more: Learning Outside the Classroom 
Communicating with us and raising concerns 
Click here to access this Communication Flowchart on our website. 

Parent Friendly Policy Guide: 
https://www.abbey.college/key-policies--reports  
Other news updates can be found here: 
• Our news page: https://www.abbey.college/school-communications  
• Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/pg/RamseyAbbeyCollege/posts/  
• Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/abbeycollege_ramsey/

metadata.title: BBC licence fee could change as Government makes major announcement on future plans
metadata.contentSnippet: A petition calling for the BBC licence fee not to be extended to subscribers of rival streaming services has received a Government response, amid growing questions over how the broadcaster will be funded in future.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: BBC licence fee could change as Government makes major announcement on future plans
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A petition calling for the BBC licence fee not to be extended to subscribers of rival streaming services has received a Government response, amid growing questions over how the broadcaster will be funded in future. The petition, which has attracted 18,418 signatures, warns that households could face extra costs if ministers decide to extend the licence fee to people who subscribe to streaming platforms not owned or operated by the BBC. Campaigner Alec Burns, who created the petition, argues the move would be "wholly unacceptable", particularly during the cost-of-living crisis. The petition, which can still be signed, states: "Amid a cost-of-living crisis, we believe the Government should be finding ways to save the public money, not expanding their means of taxation." It also claims the BBC already has a "tarnished reputation" and warns that extending the charge could further damage public confidence in the broadcaster. The Government has now responded, confirming it is considering a range of options for the BBC's future funding but stressing that no final decisions have been taken. In its response, published on November 2, the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport said ministers were considering feedback from a public consultation on the BBC Charter Review Green Paper. It said: "The Government is keeping an open mind on the future funding of the BBC and no decisions have been taken at this stage." The response added that ongoing policy development was looking at the potential impact of different funding arrangements on households, consumers, investment and the wider creative economy. Ministers said the BBC remained a "vital national institution" which informs, educates and entertains audiences across the UK. The Government also highlighted the broadcaster's contribution to the UK's creative industries, saying it supports jobs and growth across the nations and regions. It pointed to research from the Reuters Institute, which found that 59% of UK respondents trusted BBC News in 2026, making it one of the country's most trusted news brands. However, ministers acknowledged that viewing habits have changed significantly as more people turn to streaming services and other ways of watching television. The Government said: "The changing media market and audience viewing habits mean the Charter Review needs to consider whether the current funding model remains suitable for the future." It also revealed that the total number of TV licences in force has fallen by three million since 2017/18. The Government confirmed it is looking at several options to ensure the BBC has sustainable funding in the years ahead. These include making the broadcaster operate more efficiently, generating more commercial revenue and potentially reforming the licence fee itself. Ministers also acknowledged concerns about the cost of the charge for households already struggling with their finances. The response said: "We understand that ensuring the licence fee is affordable is important." It added that the Government wanted to keep costs as low as possible for households while ensuring the BBC had the resources it needed to continue providing its services. The response did not confirm whether people subscribing to non-BBC streaming platforms could eventually be required to pay the licence fee. Instead, ministers stressed that they were still considering consultation responses and engaging with stakeholders. A White Paper setting out the Government's plans for the BBC's future is expected before the end of 2026. Recommended reading: The Government also highlighted existing support for households struggling to pay the annual licence fee. Since February 2025, more households have been eligible for the Simple Payment Plan, allowing them to spread the cost through weekly, fortnightly or monthly instalments. Other support includes: Ministers said the Charter Review was also considering whether further concessions or alternative payment schedules could better reflect different household circumstances.

metadata.title: Shoppers at Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Lidl and more risking £100 parking fines
metadata.contentSnippet: Drivers are urged to check supermarket parking signs after a warning that some car parks charge for parking outside opening hours.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Shoppers at Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Lidl and more risking £100 parking fines
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Drivers could face a £100 charge for parking outside a supermarket's opening hours. Some supermarket car parks restrict when vehicles can be left there, even if the car park is empty. Select Car Leasing highlighted the issue. Graham Conway, managing director of Select Car Leasing, urged drivers to read signs before deciding whether to park. He said: “Check the signage as you enter the car park carefully before making a decision about whether to stay or not. “Not all store car parks punish after or before-hours parking, but many do, and it’s an issue that’s causing real confusion among motorists.” Mr Conway said the company had seen cases where people were charged after leaving a vehicle for a matter of minutes. Supermarket car parks can be managed by private operators, which issue Parking Charge Notices when they believe conditions have been broken. Some use automatic number plate recognition cameras, with notices sent by post. Other conditions can include limits on the length of a stay, parking within marked bays and restrictions on who can use disabled or parent and child spaces. A private Parking Charge Notice is different from a penalty charge notice issued by a council. In England and Wales, Citizens Advice says drivers should check whether the parking company belongs to an accredited trade association when considering an appeal. It advises that if a non-member puts a ticket on a vehicle, the driver should not contact the company unless it writes to them first. In Scotland, Citizens Advice says someone who wants to challenge a private ticket should first contact the operator, explain their reasons and ask for it to be withdrawn. It says they could also approach the landowner, such as the supermarket, and provide the operator with evidence including photographs of unclear signs. In Northern Ireland, the Consumer Council says a driver who believes a private notice was issued incorrectly may be able to appeal, using evidence such as photographs of damaged signs. It says registered keepers in Northern Ireland cannot automatically be held liable for private parking charges, unlike in England and Wales, and that the driver is liable. An independent appeal may be possible if an operator rejects a challenge, depending on the company and the relevant appeal service.

metadata.title: Rare Cadbury chocolate returns to UK supermarket shelves after months away
metadata.contentSnippet: The Cadbury Twirl Crispy Wafer, a bar originally from Australia, has been spotted in B&M stores.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Rare Cadbury chocolate returns to UK supermarket shelves after months away
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A rare Cadbury chocolate bar has returned to UK shelves after months away. The Cadbury Twirl Crispy Wafer, a bar originally from Australia, has been spotted in B&M stores. The bar features two fingers of flaky chocolate swirls and curls, layered with crispy wafer and coated in Cadbury Dairy Milk milk chocolate. The Twirl Crispy Wafer is still sold in Australia, and B&M has imported the 40g and 150g packs from the country. It was first released in June 2025 but remains uncommon in the UK. The bar followed the earlier Twirl Breakaway style variant, effectively acting as a modern reimagining of the classic Cadbury Time Out style bar. Its return to UK supermarket shelves was shared by the New Food Spotters UK social media page. One person replied: "Hungry now." Another said: "That's what Timeout used to be like." It is not the only rare Cadbury treat that has returned to shelves in the UK. Astros, space-themed chocolate and candy balls with a biscuit centre, are also available at B&M stores. The popular chocolate brand first launched the treat in the UK in 1997 as a competitor to Smarties and M&Ms. They were discontinued in 2008, but are back in the UK and are exciting shoppers. The Cadbury Dairy Milk Winter Mint Crisp bar is also back in UK supermarkets for the festive period. The 350g bar, which combines classic Dairy Milk chocolate with crunchy mint pieces. Other rare Cadbury chocolate spotted in supermarkets include the Dairy Milk PB&J flavour, Cadbury's mint-flavoured Twirl, and the Cadbury Dream white chocolate bar. Cadbury launched Dream White Chocolate bars in the UK back in 2001. However, the popular chocolate was discontinued just a year later (in 2002), with Cadbury citing the changing tastes of customers as the reason for its decision. Cadbury's Dream chocolate has made several appearances on UK shelves in recent years. But it is now back again at B&M for £2.99, having been imported from Australia. In other food news, rare Walkers crisps have returned to supermarket shelves in the UK, with one flavour back for the first time in five years. The crisp brand has reintroduced its Roast Potatoes, Pigs in Blankets and Sensations Honey Glazed Roast Ham flavours as part of its 2026 Christmas range. The Roast Potatoes flavour last appeared on shelves for Christmas in 2021, with the Pigs in Blankets flavour not being seen since 2023. All the festive crisps are wrapped in limited-edition Christmas packaging. Recommended reading: Rob Pothier, marketing director at PepsiCo, which owns Walkers, said: "Christmas is a huge opportunity for savoury snacking, with shoppers stocking up for every occasion, from family get-togethers and parties to nights in and the days between Christmas and New Year. "Our Christmas portfolio is designed to stand out in store and make it easy for shoppers to find what they need, whether that’s a familiar favourite or a seasonal flavour." What is your favourite Cadbury chocolate product? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Popular ITV show to return after 7 years away with 'glamorous' star set to host
metadata.contentSnippet: Take Me Out is reportedly set to return to screens nearly seven years after it was axed from ITV.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Popular ITV show to return after 7 years away with 'glamorous' star set to host
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A popular ITV series is reportedly making a comeback after nearly years away. Take Me Out is set to return to screens nearly seven years after it was axed from ITV. The reboot of the popular dating show, originally hosted by Paddy McGuinness, will not feature him as host. Producers are reportedly seeking a “glamorous female” presenter to attract new audiences. A source told The Sun: "Take Me Out was absolutely huge in the 2010s and was a stalwart of the primetime light entertainment schedule. "Execs at Fremantle, the production company behind the reboot, want to ensure it has the same cheeky tone as the original. "That’s what set it apart from more serious dating formats which rely on beef and drama – and made it such a fun watch." Presenters Olivia Attwood and Emily Atack are among those being considered, with model Leomie Anderson also reportedly in the running. The source added: "Emily and Olivia’s quick wit and timing make them favourites and Maya Jama was also considered perfect, but her links to Love Island make that tricky." The original Take Me Out ran for 11 series from 2010 to 2019, with McGuinness at the helm. The show featured a single man trying to impress a panel of 30 women, who could turn off their podium light if they weren’t interested. If any lights remained on at the end, the bachelor would choose one of the women to join him on a date to the fictional “Isle of Fernando’s” – filmed in Tenerife. The source said: "The fact Take Me Out had the females in control and it was delivered with such a gentle, comedic touch makes it a very future-friendly format – little would need to be changed." The reboot is currently in development, with Fremantle in talks with streamers including Netflix. Another classic show is also set to return to TV screens in the UK. ITV is reviving Name That Tune for the first time in 29 years, with presenter Alison Hammond set to host the brand-new series. The music quiz show originally began in the United States in the 1950s before launching in the UK in 1976, and becoming a weekly half-hour show in 1983. It was transformed into its own show in 1983 due to its widespread popularity. The original UK series was hosted by comedian Tom O’Connor until 1983, with Lionel Blair taking over until 1988. The show last appeared on UK television in 1998, when it was briefly revived by Channel 5 and presented by Jools Holland. ITV’s new version will challenge contestants to identify famous songs in a series of high-energy rounds. Tracks will span generations and genres, all leading up to a dramatic finale. The show's band will also be performing in the new UK version, made up of a group of elite musicians who have performed with some of the world’s biggest stars, including Adele and the Spice Girls. The rebooted game show Name That Tune will air in the first quarter of 2027, according to TV Zone. It will consist of nine episodes. Alison Hammond said: "As a massive music lover, my biggest challenge as a host will be trying not to grab the mic and start singing along when one of my all-time favourite tunes comes on! "And trust me… that will take serious self-control! "I grew up absolutely loving the original show, so being part of this now feels like a real full-circle moment. Recommended reading: "I cannot wait to get into the studio, put the contestants through their paces, and see who really knows their music. "And let me tell you, being joined by the super-talented Name That Tune band, who’ll be belting out some of the biggest songs on the planet in their own unique, electric style… oh, it’s going to be next-level. "Bigger, louder, and more feel-good than ever, this is going to be EPIC!" What classic TV show would you like to see return? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Emmerdale star confirms exit from ITV soap but promises to return in the future
metadata.contentSnippet: Bradley Riches has confirmed he will be leaving Emmerdale for the festive period but will return to play Lewis Barton in the new year.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Emmerdale star confirms exit from ITV soap but promises to return in the future
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An Emmerdale star has confirmed his exit from the show and has revealed what his next role will be. The popular ITV soap has seen a few stars leave over the past year with Bradley Riches being the next actor to be taking time off. However, the 24-year-old has reassured fans that his character is only taking a break from Emmerdale rather than leaving the show forever. Bradley joined the cast in May 2025 to play Lewis Barton, the long-lost son of Emma Barton, played by Gillian Kearney. It was later revealed on the show that Kev Townsend, played by Chris Coghill, was Lewis’s biological father. The pair worked through many challenges on the soap to build a strong relationship that ended with Kev adopting his son’s surname. Lewis also built a friendship with Nicola King, played by Nicola Wheeler. The actor is also known for his role on Netflix’s show Heartstopper where he played James McEwan in 2023. He went on to feature on the 2024 series of Celebrity Big Brother alongside Love Island’s Ekin-Su and Coronation Street’s Colson Smith. Bradley has confirmed that he will be taking a break from the show to star as Peter Pan in a panto at the Sunderland Empire. The actor shared a story on Instagram confirming his new role. He said: “That’s a wrap at Emmerdale for now! “A little time off before heading to pantoland. “So excited for what’s ahead for Lewis in 2027. “Feeling very lucky and grateful, as always. “See you on your screens soon!” The theatre has announced that Bradley would be joining the cast back in March on social media by saying: “Bradley Riches from Netflix’s Heartstopper, Emmerdale and Big Brother is flying into Sunderland this Christmas as our thrill-seeking hero, Peter Pan!” Fans took to the comments to share their thoughts on the announcement with one person saying: “This is so exciting.” Another person said: “Bradley is an absolute joy.” A third person wrote: “Absolutely brilliant casting.” Are you excited to see how Lewis’s story develops on Emmerdale next year? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: BT shutting off decades-old service with households given warning to switch over
metadata.contentSnippet: BT is shutting off its analogue landline service with customers being told to either switch providers or use its new digital service.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: BT shutting off decades-old service with households given warning to switch over
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Households are being warned of an upcoming date that will see a BT service being switched off forever. BT and Openreach are set to be ending the Public Switched Telephone Network by the start of next year. The service has been available for decades but is coming to an end in a few weeks' time. The analogue technology that has been used to support the phone and broadband services over the years is being shut off. This is because it no longer meets "connectivity standards". The new digital landlines are set to deliver "a more reliable and resilient service" for customers. The switch over is currently taking place and is set to be finished by January 31, 2027, with customers being told to change their service. Customers can either move to a digital landline or to another phone service that will allow them to keep using their landline in the same way. You should be able to keep using your landlines and phone numbers after the switch off, but they will need to be plugged into a broadband router. BT's new home phone service is called Digital Voice and switching over is described as being "simple". Over 99% of home phones are compatible with the new service. Customers are set to be contacted about the changes at least four weeks before the digital switch to make sure they are ready. Customers that might need some extra support when changing their landline service can book a free in-home engineer visit. The BT website says: "Customers are advised to wait until they are contacted by their provider, but to take prompt action when they are. "Failing to respond to messages from your provider may result in disruption to your phone or broadband services as the switchover deadline approaches." Recommended reading Digital Voice will not cost customers anything and they will continue to pay the same as their current home phone plan states unless they have decided to upgrade to Digital Voice while recontracting a home broadband plan. The new service will use screening to help block scam calls and has a caller display to let you know who is calling before you answer the phone. Will you be switching over your landline to Digital Voice? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: James Norton is unrecognisable as Santa in M&S's star-studded Christmas advert
metadata.contentSnippet: M&S has launched its 2026 Christmas advert starring James Norton as Santa, Lucy Punch as Mrs Claus and Katherine Jenkins singing Heaven Is a Place on Earth.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: James Norton is unrecognisable as Santa in M&S's star-studded Christmas advert
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: This article contains affiliate links. We may receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more. M&S has unveiled its star-studded Christmas advert, with Happy Valley actor James Norton making a rather unexpected appearance as Father Christmas – including a scene in which he is wearing just a towel. The actor gets a very different Santa makeover, shaving off his famous beard and ditching the traditional red suit as he goes undercover to experience Christmas without being recognised. He is joined by Amandaland star Lucy Punch as Mrs Claus, who encourages him to leave the North Pole behind, while Katherine Jenkins OBE provides a special reworking of Belinda Carlisle's classic hit Heaven Is a Place on Earth for the soundtrack. The campaign, titled The Home of Christmas, brings together M&S Food, Fashion, Home and Beauty in one festive advert for the first time since 2017. The advert will be available on social media from 8am and will make its television debut during ITV's This Morning at 10.15am. James Norton appears in just a towel in M&S Christmas advert as he plays Santa (Image: M&S) The advert follows Santa as he leaves the North Pole behind after Mrs Claus encourages him to go undercover and experience Christmas for himself. Played by Norton, Santa shaves off his beard, swaps his traditional red suit for a festive jumper and heads out into the world. His adventure takes him through the moments that make Christmas special, from getting dressed up and choosing presents to enjoying festive food and transforming the home for the big day. Rather than discovering that Christmas magic comes from the North Pole, he finds it in the homes, traditions and celebrations happening across the country. James Norton said: "It's not every day you get asked to play Santa, let alone a Santa who immediately shaves off his beard! M&S has been such a familiar part of Christmas for as long as I can remember, so getting to be part of its Christmas campaign feels really special. "I loved that this story takes such an iconic character and lets us see him differently. He gets to experience Christmas like the rest of us, discovering that the real magic is in the food, traditions and moments we share with the people we love. "It's warm, funny and full of Christmas spirit, and I'm very happy to have been briefly trusted with the red suit." James Norton is joined by Amandaland star Lucy Punch as Mrs Claus (Image: M&S) Mrs Claus, played by Lucy Punch, is the one who sets Santa's Christmas adventure in motion. The actress, known for Amandaland and Motherland, encourages her husband to lose the beard and leave the North Pole so he can discover the festive magic happening in homes across Britain. Lucy said: "M&S and Christmas just go hand in hand, so it was an absolute joy to become part of that tradition this year. "I loved that Mrs Claus is the one who gets this story moving. She gives him the nudge so he can get out there incognito and experience the magic of Christmas for himself. "There's something very sweet and fun about their dynamic, and something quite lovely about the idea behind it: this idea that the magic you're looking for is actually happening all around you." The soundtrack is another big name addition, with Katherine Jenkins providing a special reworking of Belinda Carlisle's 1987 hit Heaven Is a Place on Earth. (Image: M&S) The soundtrack is another big name addition, with Katherine Jenkins providing a special reworking of Belinda Carlisle's 1987 hit Heaven Is a Place on Earth. The Welsh singer, who is the voice of M&S Christmas this year, has teamed up with producer Fraser T Smith, known for his work with Adele, and Ted Lasso composer Tom Howe. The new recording will be released on Friday, November 6, so shoppers can listen to the song beyond the advert. Katherine said: "For me, Christmas has always been about coming home. It's about family, traditions and creating memories with the people you love most, and music is such a big part of that. "Certain songs instantly become part of the soundtrack to our celebrations, so I was thrilled to record a new version of Heaven Is a Place on Earth for this campaign. "I love how beautifully it complements the story, reminding us that the real magic of Christmas isn't found in grand gestures, but in the moments we share together at home." Alongside the advert, M&S has shared a selection of the festive food, fashion, beauty and homeware it expects shoppers to snap up this Christmas. The retailer's Christmas picks include: Food and drink - see the full range here Fashion and gifts - see the full range here Home and beauty - see the full range here Products are available at selected M&S stores and online, subject to availability. The campaign comes as M&S shares new research into how people across Britain are preparing for Christmas. Its Customer Pulse research found that 81% of customers want a special Christmas with the people they love, while 57% plan to spend as much time as possible with family and friends. Food remains a major part of the celebrations, with 73% saying it is worth spending more on quality food at Christmas and 68% saying food is what makes the season feel special. More than four in ten (42%) plan to host a gathering this year, rising to 51% among M&S customers. The research also suggests festive planning is starting earlier, with 53% saying Christmas preparations begin earlier every year. Recommended reading: Sharry Cramond, Marketing Director at M&S, said: "Customers don't think about Christmas as one meal, one gift or one outfit. They think about all the moments that make the season special. "As the only retailer with a truly cross-category offer spanning Food, Fashion, Beauty, Gifting and Home, M&S plays a unique role in helping customers create Christmas from start to finish. "Bringing those categories together allows us to tell one connected Christmas story and celebrate all the ways our customers make the season their own. That's why we're proud that customers call M&S The Home of Christmas."

metadata.title: Town vision includes river moorings, pedestrianisation and bus station revamp
metadata.contentSnippet: Ambitious ideas to transform St Ives with new riverside moorings, pedestrianised streets, an enhanced market area and a regenerated bus station have been unveiled.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Town vision includes river moorings, pedestrianisation and bus station revamp
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Ambitious ideas to transform St Ives with new riverside moorings, pedestrianised streets, an enhanced market area and a regenerated bus station have been unveiled. The St Ives Town Team has published an updated 'A Vision of St Ives', setting out ideas to boost the town while protecting its historic character. Town Team spokesman John Souter said the document is a starting point for discussion, with businesses, organisations and other interested parties due to meet next month. MP Ben Obese-Jecty (centre) with John Souter and Sheila Stones of the St Ives Town Team, which has created an updated Vision for St Ives document. (Image: Ben Obese-Jecty) The meeting will be closed to the public, but people will have a chance to give their views later, he said. "We want to discuss what is feasible, and come up with some sort of plan that we can take to the public for people to discuss and then add their views on," said John. "The plan will include some short-term goals that are easily achievable because they won't require a lot of funding. "Longer-term projects where we would need to find funding, and then schemes that we know will take some time to realise, such as regenerating Hyperion corner, alongside the bus station, making them more attractive." Hyperion corner could be completely transformed with new buildings. (Image: Town Team) He said the owners of the buildings were on board with the idea. Among the most striking suggestions are additional mooring pontoons at The Quay, designed to encourage more people travelling on the Great Ouse to stop and spend time in the town. The Town Team says extra visitor berths could bring more people to shops and other amenities, accommodate more boats and create opportunities for river events. It believes pontoons could also improve safety along the water's edge. The bus station could be given a makeover to make it more appealing to look at. (Image: Town Team) Another major idea would see part of Market Hill pedestrianised, particularly around the Oliver Cromwell statue, Town Hall, Free Church and Corn Exchange, and local MP Ben Obese-Jecty has launched a poll on the St Ives Serious Discussion Facebook page asking people for their views on potential pedestrianisation. John said: "This project is about far more than pedestrianisation; we want a vision for St Ives that will make it more attractive, while helping it to prosper." He said he has been pushing for various improvements in the town since 1996, when he was a town councillor. He believes the time is now right for progress. The Octagon could become a venue for daily farmers' markets. (Image: Town Team) "There has not been the political will before, but I believe it is there now, and so this is our chance to do something good for St Ives, and it's probably my last chance to see my ambitions for the town realised in my lifetime," said John. The Town Team's vision suggests reducing parking in Market Hill to create more community space, potentially featuring trees for shade and a covered area inspired by traditional market halls. Changes could also be made to Crown Street, Bridge Street and Merryland, with the Town Team suggesting pedestrianisation while retaining access for residents and delivery vehicles. Public transport is another key part of the vision. One idea is to reroute Cambridge buses through The Broadway, Crown Street and Market Hill, bringing passengers closer to shops and boosting footfall. The document also suggests the existing bus stop in Station Road could be relocated to the Sheep Market. Meanwhile, the area around the bus station is identified as a potential regeneration opportunity, including the historic Octagon. The document envisages a development featuring shops, an improved antiques centre, flats and an historic auction room. The Octagon itself could potentially become a daily indoor produce or farmers' market, while also being used for antique auctions and as a tourist information point because of its proximity to the bus station and main car park. The vision also calls for efforts to revive the town's markets, improve cleanliness, tackle commercial waste and wheelie bins in sensitive historic areas, and boost tourism. It also suggests creating an innovation hub, using vacant properties for pop-up businesses and conference facilities. The Town Team says the updated document aims to spark debate about what could be achieved and inform the Town Council's Neighbourhood Plan. It says St Ives should build on its independent shops, historic streets and riverside setting rather than copy other town centres. The document says some major projects will take time, while others could improve the town quickly. It says: "We understand that no town can stand still and rest on its laurels, and every community needs to assess and reassess itself to ensure it is taking advantage of all the opportunities that exist."

metadata.title: Shoplifter who threatened to stab staff with drill bit jailed
metadata.contentSnippet: A shoplifter has been jailed after threatening staff at Smyths Toys in Peterborough with a drill bit.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Shoplifter who threatened to stab staff with drill bit jailed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A shoplifter has been jailed after threatening to stab staff with a drill bit at a Peterborough toy shop. Stephen Foot, 29, was confronted by staff at Smyths Toys in Boongate on November 3 when he was caught stealing a toy truck. He pulled out a pointed drill bit and threatened to stab staff if they approached him before fleeing the scene with the stolen item. Foot, of no fixed address, was arrested less than 30 minutes later by the spree offender team in Dickens Street, Eastfield. PC Lily Norman, who investigated the case, said: "Foot’s behaviour towards the shop staff was completely unacceptable, and no one should face these threats while trying to do their job." At Peterborough Magistrates' Court on November 4, he was charged with possession of a bladed article and three counts of theft from a shop. Foot was also found to have stolen from H&M in Queensgate on October 23 and Home Bargains in Bourges Boulevard on November 1. He was sentenced to six months in prison.

metadata.title: Four EV charging bays approved at Hunts shopping centre despite parking concerns
metadata.contentSnippet: Four electric vehicle charging stations have been approved at a Godmanchester shopping centre despite concerns about parking and safety near a school.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Four EV charging bays approved at Hunts shopping centre despite parking concerns
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Four electric vehicle charging stations have been approved at a Godmanchester shopping centre despite concerns about parking and safety near a school. The proposals will see four rapid EV charging bays and associated equipment installed at the King James Retail Centre in Ermine Street. Huntingdonshire District Council planning officers recommended approval despite strong objections from Godmanchester Town Council. Application 26/01647/FUL revised an earlier scheme, cutting the proposed charging spaces from six to four. Plans to install four electric vehicle charging stations at a Godmanchester shopping centre have been approved despite concerns over parking and safety near a school. (Image: Google Maps / Street View) Six existing parking bays will be replaced by four EV charging spaces. Planning officers said the scheme would improve access to rapid EV charging and encourage greener transport. They concluded that it would provide sufficient parking and vehicle movement and would not cause significant harm to neighbours, highway safety or biodiversity. However, Godmanchester Town Council strongly recommended the plans be refused, arguing that dedicating four spaces to EV charging had not been adequately justified given demand for parking at the site. The town council said the car park is frequently at or close to capacity and warned that removing general short-stay spaces could push vehicles onto surrounding roads. It was especially concerned because the site is used for primary school drop-offs, saying displaced parking could make it less safe for children, parents and pedestrians. The town authority also pointed to publicly accessible charging facilities at a nearby Shell service station and called for evidence about the demand for four additional charging spaces. The council also raised concerns about the impact on deliveries to neighbouring businesses. But Cambridgeshire County Council, the highways authority, did not object because the equipment would sit inside the car park, away from the public highway. Environmental health officers also raised no objections after the number of dedicated spaces was cut. Planning officers said the loss of two parking spaces would not create significant highway safety concerns given the number of spaces remaining. They also noted a “fallback position”: the charging points are permitted development, but the associated substation needs planning permission. The applicant, Ashwin Eapen of Instavolt Ltd, submitted planning documents in support of the proposal which argued the infrastructure was small-scale and was designed to provide safe, accessible and convenient charging within the existing car park. The documents described the equipment as modern, functional InstaVolt infrastructure. Officers said the development was suitably scaled and designed and recommended approval. A decision notice to that effect was issued on Wednesday (4). The approved layout includes one fully accessible charging bay, along with charging units, CCTV, cabling and a feeder pillar, across about 122 square metres of the existing car park.

metadata.title: Beloved African lion Ghana dies aged 16 after declining health at Cambs zoo
metadata.contentSnippet: Johnson’s of Old Hurst zoo, near Huntingdon, is in mourning today following the death of one of its beloved lions.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Beloved African lion Ghana dies aged 16 after declining health at Cambs zoo
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire zoo is in mourning today following the death of one of its beloved lions at the age of 16. Ghana, an African lion at Johnson’s of Old Hurst, near Huntingdon, was put to sleep due to declining health and age-related arthritis. Posting on their Facebook page the zoo said: "We are devastated to announce the passing of our male African lion, Ghana. Majestic Ghana and his companion Lydia have proved a huge hit with visitors to Johnson's since their arrival at the zoo three years ago. (Image: Johnson's) "Ghana lived an amazing 16 years, and was not just a lion to us but a huge part of our family here at Johnson’s and the start of our zoo story. "He will forever be remembered for his incredible roar that could be heard miles over the zoo, his magnificent mane and his infectious character that we all adored." "Our zoo team will continue to give Ghana’s companion Lydia all of the attention and love she needs as she navigates through this confusing time without her bestest friend by her side." Johnson's zoo said they will remember Ghana's incredible roar, mane, and character. (Image: Johnson's) Ghana moved to the zoo in August 2023 with Lydia, when their previous owner decided he wanted to cut back on his animals, and he has proved a huge hit with visitors, who have loved seeing the majestic male and his mate over the past three years. Ghana has previously enjoyed some TV stardom after appearing in an advert for Ford Transit vans in the past. Johnson's of Oldhurst is home to more than 100 animals, including crocodiles, pumas, alligators, and bears.

metadata.title: Zombie Fest transforms Cambridge Junction with six stages and 90 acts
metadata.contentSnippet: Zombie Fest brought Halloween costumes, rave culture and 90 acts including Jaguar Skills and Ultrabeat to the Cambridge Junction.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Zombie Fest transforms Cambridge Junction with six stages and 90 acts
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Amid a sea of zombies, ghouls and impressively crafted costumes, Zombie Fest has carved out a unique place on the region's festival calendar. Mixing rave culture, Halloween spectacle and a strong sense of community, it is easy to see why it has developed such a loyal following. The festival transformed every available inch of the Cambridge Junction into a vibrant celebration of music and alternative culture. Stages were spread throughout the J1 and J2 arenas, as well as outdoor space, creating an impressive multi-stage experience with something always happening around the next corner. The atmosphere was warm, welcoming and relentlessly upbeat, with festivalgoers throwing themselves wholeheartedly into the Halloween spirit. Some of those who attended the event (Image: Sham Hussain) From elaborate costumes to impromptu dance-offs, there was a genuine sense that everyone was there for the same reason: to celebrate great music, creativity and unapologetic fun. Musically, highlights were undoubtedly Jaguar Skills and also the brilliant BCXD vs DJ Gumbar hardstyle set which featured lookalikes of Vladimir Putin, Kim Jong Un and Donald Trump. It was impossible not to get swept up in the fun. I laughed hard, danced even harder, and loved every minute – it was one of those performances that perfectly captured the anything-goes spirit of the festival. Across six stages organisers say there were more than 90 live performers and acts across the entire venue with a wide range of styles. There was 90s & 00s classics and anthems featuring acts such as Ultrabeat and N-Trance, drum and bass and jungle featuring Jaguar Skills, Logan D plus Harry Shotta with Triple Threat, house and classics from Grooverider and Alex P. Hardcore and hardstyle fans were catered for by Slipmatt and Dougal, breaks were in abundance from Dub Pistols and Jay Cunning, while hard house and trance heads were treated to sets from Rob Tissera, Lisa Pin-Up. What stood out most was the sheer ambition of the event. The organisers squeezed every ounce of potential from the venue, transforming Cambridge Junction into a fully immersive, multi-room festival experience. For anyone looking for a Halloween night out with great music, plenty of energy and a welcoming crowd, Zombie Fest delivered in style and already it has a date set for next year. Put it in your calendars! Zombie Fest X · The 10th Edition · Cambridge · 30 Oct 2027

metadata.title: Officers seize huge stash of illegal fireworks from Peterborough shop
metadata.contentSnippet: A large stash of illegal fireworks has been seized from a shop on Lincoln Road in Peterborough.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Officers seize huge stash of illegal fireworks from Peterborough shop
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A large stash of illegal fireworks has been seized from a shop in Peterborough. Officers found unlicensed fireworks at a Lincoln Road shop on November 6 during a joint operation involving Peterborough City Council’s trading standards team, Cambridgeshire Constabulary and Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service. The inspection followed intelligence that fireworks were being sold there without a licence. Councillor Zameer Ali, cabinet member for communities and public safety, said: "In the lead up to Bonfire Night, the community in this area has been disturbed by several firework-related incidents, which have been widely reported on. "While we don't know if these are linked, I am relieved that this sizeable quantity of fireworks has been removed from this address, as it was clearly presenting a hazard to those who lived nearby. "There are obvious serious safety risks in buying, storing, and selling fireworks in an unlicensed premises. "Fireworks are explosives and those sold by unlicensed sellers may not meet safety standards. "They could be improperly stored, incorrectly labelled, damaged and unsafe to use, increasing the risk of injury, property damage and fire." During the visit, officers found more than 21kg of fireworks with net explosive content (NEC). NEC is the total mass of explosive substances, excluding packaging, outer casings, containers, or inert components. These fireworks were subsequently seized. Sam Tucker, Peterborough neighbourhoods inspector, said: "Our officers joined partners in visiting this premises as part of our ongoing efforts to tackle issues involving inappropriate use of fireworks in the city. "Additional patrols will take place in the area tonight and this weekend, and we would strongly urge anyone with any concerns to report this to us, so we can build an accurate picture of anti-social behaviour in the area and work to combat this." Anyone who believes fireworks are being sold illegally can contact the Citizens Advice Consumer Service on 0808 223 1133. If someone is in immediate danger always call 999.

metadata.title: Hail Weston Halloween trail draws more than 300 visitors and supports NSPCC
metadata.contentSnippet: More than 300 people enjoyed a "spook-tacular" Halloween trail in Hail Weston.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hail Weston Halloween trail draws more than 300 visitors and supports NSPCC
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: More than 300 people enjoyed a "spook-tacular" Halloween trail in Hail Weston. The Trick or Treat Monster Trail, held in the village, featured over 10,000 lights and raised awareness and donations for the NSPCC. Families and friends explored the route, which was filled with colourful Halloween surprises, larger-than-life monster displays, moving animatronics, and projections. A highlight was the illuminated pumpkin patch, creating a picture-perfect Halloween scene. The trail provided a blend of excitement and family-friendly fun, with visitors able to spot their favourite Halloween creatures around every corner. One of the attendees said: "The combination of thousands of colourful lights, animated monsters, and magical projections created a wonderful Halloween atmosphere, bringing a little extra sparkle to the spooky season." The event, while focused on Halloween fun, also had a special purpose. The Trick or Treat Monster Trail supported the NSPCC, with visitors encouraged to donate via text to back the charity's work in protecting children. The event organiser said: "The event brought together the magic of Halloween and the kindness of the local community, showing that even the cheekiest little monsters can help make a big difference." The evening was a blend of family fun, community spirit, and fundraising. With more than 300 visitors, over 10,000 lights, and a collection of monsters, pumpkins, and special effects, the Trick or Treat Monster Trail was a celebration of Halloween. The event organiser added: "The event demonstrated just how much fun can be created with a little imagination, plenty of creativity, and a whole lot of Halloween magic. "As the lights twinkled, the pumpkins glowed, and the monsters entertained their visitors, Hail Weston’s Trick or Treat Monster Trail delivered a Halloween experience full of smiles, surprises, and happy memories." To learn more about the NSPCC and its work, visit nspcc.org.uk.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire PC praised after cutting deliberate fires at landfill by 81 per cent
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire police officers, staff, and volunteers were celebrated at an awards ceremony.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire PC praised after cutting deliberate fires at landfill by 81 per cent
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire police officers, staff, and volunteers were celebrated at an awards ceremony. They were praised for their outstanding contributions to public safety and community service. The ceremony, held at the new Milton Police Station, was led by South Area Commander Superintendent Paul Rogerson. The awards acknowledged acts of bravery, professionalism, and dedication, including officers rescuing vulnerable people from rivers and fires, and a special constable supporting domestic violence victims. Superintendent Rogerson expressed his pride in the recipients, stating: "We have recognised acts of bravery, compassion, professionalism and determination that have made a genuine difference to people's lives and to the communities we serve." Members of the Southern Business Support Team, Antonia Early, Susana El Din Ruiz, and Josie McFarlane, were commended for ensuring a smooth transition from Parkside to Milton Police Station, minimising disruption to frontline policing. Special Constable Sophie Trippett received recognition for her more than 80 hours of service to the Domestic Violence Disclosure Scheme, supporting victims through difficult situations. Police Constable Janine Hagger was praised for her efforts in reducing deliberate fires at Grunty Fen landfill site by 81 per cent, significantly easing pressure on emergency services. Detention Officers Katie-Louise White and David Foy were celebrated for their commitment to detainee welfare in custody. Volunteer Police Cadet leader Patrick Kadewere received recognition for his dedication to supporting young cadets. Several awards highlighted acts of bravery in life-threatening situations. Police Constables Will Carr, Alexander Manning, and Liam Wells were commended for evacuating a retirement complex during a rapidly spreading grass fire. Police Constables Jonathan Moesbauer and Kacper Czerenkiewicz were praised for rescuing a woman from a river in crisis. The awards also recognised the contribution of local resident Cheryl Boaz, who helped officers support a vulnerable woman in Cambridge. The commendations highlighted the diverse ways people contribute to community safety, from emergency responses to long-term problem-solving and public service.

metadata.title: Memorial appeal for heroic World War II 'Ghost Patrol' soldiers
metadata.contentSnippet: They were known as the ‘Ghost Patrol’ by opposing Italian forces because the unit often appeared suddenly out of nowhere in the deep desert

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Memorial appeal for heroic World War II 'Ghost Patrol' soldiers
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The families of men who served in one of the Second World War’s most remarkable special forces units are launching a £150,000 appeal to create a permanent memorial to their courage and achievements. The Long Range Desert Group (LRDG), nicknamed ‘Ghost Patrol’ by opposing Italian forces, was formed in Cairo in 1940 and often operated in secret behind enemy lines. The appeal follows the death in August of Jack Mann, the last surviving veteran of the LRDG, at the age of 100. Born Zacharia Zuckerman in Cairo in 1925, he altered his age to enlist while still a teenager and was recruited by the LRDG as a radio operator. A talented linguist and wireless operator, he was recruited into the LRDG and subsequently served with other wartime special forces units.  He later served with 21 SAS. The LDRG were founded after explorer and British Army officer Major Ralph Bagnold proposed the creation of a small, fast-moving reconnaissance force capable of travelling vast distances behind enemy lines in the deserts of Egypt and Libya. The unit became renowned for its ability to navigate across apparently featureless desert and operate hundreds of miles from conventional forces, gathering vital intelligence on enemy movements and carrying out raids and other operations. Its expertise also made the LRDG an important partner to the newly formed SAS, transporting and guiding its men across the desert on some of their early operations. After the North African campaign, the LRDG continued to operate across the Aegean, Adriatic, Albania, Italy, Greece and Yugoslavia. The cost was considerable. Fifty-one LRDG men are known to have died during the war and at least 182 were captured. The LRDG Memorial Fund, a registered charity established by people with family connections to members of the unit, plans to erect a spectacular 5.8-metre-high sculpture of a scorpion — the LRDG’s emblem — at the Royal British Legion National Remembrance Gardens in Staffordshire. While many Second World War units are represented at the Gardens, the Long Range Desert Group is not currently among them. The memorial has been designed by internationally recognised British sculptor James Doran-Webb, renowned for his monumental animal sculptures.  At its centre will be a giant driftwood scorpion, surrounded by a three-metre stainless-steel ring with compass-style markings reflecting the LRDG’s navigational skills. The sculpture will stand on a plinth designed to trace the unit’s wartime journey from North Africa to the Aegean, Italy and the Balkans. The LRDG Memorial Fund is seeking donations from the public, military community and organisations towards its £150,000 fundraising target. Donations can be made at www.lrdgmemorialfund.org where there is a link to JustGiving. Meg Kennedy Shaw, daughter of Bill Kennedy Shaw, the LRDG’s intelligence officer, said: “Jack Mann's death this summer marked the passing of the last surviving member of the Long Range Desert Group. "With him, the final living link to this extraordinary group of men has gone. For those of us whose fathers and grandfathers served with the LRDG, it makes it all the more important that their story is not lost with their generation. “These men operated for almost five years across deserts, islands, mountains and coastlines, frequently deep behind enemy lines and in extraordinarily difficult conditions. "They showed exceptional courage, ingenuity and resourcefulness, yet their story remains relatively little known. “We believe the time has come to give the LRDG the permanent public recognition it deserves. The scorpion memorial will be a striking and lasting tribute to them, and a place where their families and future generations can remember what they did.” Sculptor James Doran-Webb added: “The scorpion gave us a powerful starting point because it comes directly from the LRDG’s own insignia. "I wanted the memorial to reflect the incredible ingenuity, endurance and navigational skill of the men who served, while creating something dramatic enough to stop people in their tracks and make them curious to discover who the LRDG were and what they achieved.”

metadata.title: Huntingdon Remembrance events to feature military parade and wreath-laying service
metadata.contentSnippet: A military parade and wreath-laying service will take place as part of Huntingdon’s annual Remembrance events.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Huntingdon Remembrance events to feature military parade and wreath-laying service
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A military parade and wreath-laying service will take place as part of Huntingdon’s annual Remembrance events. Residents are invited to join the commemorations, which honour those who have lost their lives in military conflicts. The Remembrance Sunday parade and service will be held on Sunday, November 8, with the annual Armistice Day service following on Wednesday, November 11. Cllr Patrick Kadewere, Mayor of Huntingdon, said: "Remembrance is an important opportunity for our community to come together and honour those who have served, sacrificed and given their lives in defence of the freedoms we enjoy today. 2Poppy drop during the Remembrance Sunday Service 2025 (Image: RAF Wyton) "Whether attending in person, listening from elsewhere in the town centre or joining us online, I encourage residents of all ages to take a moment to reflect on the service and sacrifice of generations past and present. "These acts of remembrance ensure that their legacy is never forgotten." Organised by Huntingdon Town Council in partnership with the Royal British Legion (Huntingdon Branch) and RAF Wyton, the events invite veterans, serving personnel, cadet organisations, and the wider community to reflect on the sacrifices made by servicemen and women. On Remembrance Sunday, the military parade will assemble in Princes Street car park before marching to Market Square, where the service will begin at 10.45am. The ceremony will include the Act of Remembrance, the two-minute silence, the Reveille, and the laying of wreaths by civic representatives, military organisations, and community groups. Remembrance Sunday Service 2025 (Image: RAF Wyton) A designated viewing area will be available for wheelchair users and those with mobility requirements, and British Sign Language interpretation will be provided. The Armistice Day service will take place at the War Memorial in Market Square on Wednesday, November 11, starting at 10.55am. It will include prayers, the Act of Remembrance, and the laying of wreaths. More details are available at www.huntingdontown.gov.uk/remembrance.
