metadata.title: 5 Huntingdonshire planning applications that you should know about
metadata.contentSnippet: Recent planning applications include a Ramsey traveller site, eight Warboys homes, Home Bargains Huntingdon plans and a St Neots redevelopment.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 5 Huntingdonshire planning applications that you should know about
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Planning committees across Huntingdonshire are busy as ever, with plenty of applications and appeals coming through. We've compiled a list of just some of the applications that are currently pending or have been approved in our areas. Here are some that might have gone under the radar. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. A statement accompanying the plans says: "Mr Reilly and his family are looking for a settled environment with a permanent base to call home." Plans have been submitted to create a new residential traveller site for a family near Ramsey (Image: Google Maps) Plans for a new eight-home development in Warboys have been approved despite objections from residents and the parish council. The proposal, from applicants Mr and Mrs Robinson, involves constructing eight detached homes on land between Heath Farm and Heath Pond, north of Heath Road in Warboys. The land is currently classed as agricultural. Five residents lodged complaints, with concerns ranging from highway safety due to the proximity of the site to the A141 junction, to the loss of agricultural land and countryside. Residents also fear the homes will put more pressure on the local GP surgery and primary school. Agricultural land on the edge of Warboys could become an eight-home housing development (Image: Google Maps) Plans to build four homes at a former kennels and cattery between Hilton and Fenstanton have been refused after a national planning policy change. The application sought permission to demolish the existing buildings at Fields View, Fenstanton Road, Hilton, and replace them with four detached single-storey homes. The scheme had previously been recommended for approval and was backed by councillors in August, subject to a review against a newly published National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF). However, planning officers later concluded that the development should be refused after reassessing it under the updated NPPF 2026. Officers told the council's development management committee that the plans would create "isolated homes" in the countryside outside a settlement boundary. Plans to build four homes on the site of a former kennels and cattery between Hilton and Fenstanton have been refused after a change in national planning policy (Image: HDC) Applicant TJ Morris Limited, which trades as Home Bargains, has lodged plans for a new retail unit on St Peters Road. If approved, the "comprehensive development" would also provide customer and service access, car parking and landscaping. According to the plans, the "high-quality" development would re-purpose the site, providing local people "with choice and quality of provision". The nearest Home Bargains store to Huntingdon is on Smithy Way, Great Cambourne (Image: Street View) Fresh plans have been submitted to turn a former RAF Association club into new homes after a previous application was refused. OTAA St Neots Property Ltd wants to convert the Grade II-listed building at 44-46 Huntingdon Street, St Neots, into eight homes and build a three-bedroom house at the rear. In February 2026, the council turned down proposals for the conversion of the building into seven homes, alongside the construction of two bungalows at the rear. The new plans would restore and convert the historic building into eight homes, with a detached house at the rear. There are also plans for landscaping works, parking facilities, cycle storage, and drainage improvements. The former RAFA club in St Neots could become new homes (Image: Emily Stevens)

metadata.title: ATM stolen from petrol station in ANOTHER Cambridgeshire ramraid
metadata.contentSnippet: An ATM was stolen from the BP petrol station on Wisbech Road in Littleport in the second Cambridgeshire ram raid this week.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: ATM stolen from petrol station in ANOTHER Cambridgeshire ramraid
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An ATM was stolen from a petrol station in the second Cambridgeshire ram raid this week. Police were called to the BP garage on Wisbech Road, Littleport, at 5.06am this morning (Friday November 6) after reports of a ram raid. Officers arrived 12 minutes later to find the cash machine gone and the telehandler used in the raid abandoned nearby. Police searched the area but found no suspects. Yesterday (Thursday November 5), the force were called at around 3am with reports of an attempted ram raid at the Nationwide building on Ramsey Road in Whittlesey. Police have not confirmed if the two incidents are related. Detective Chief Inspector Chris O’Brien said: "Ram-raids are likely to take place between September and January when the nights are darker. A search of the area was carried out but no suspects were found (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) "Our patrols have increased across the county. "We are committed to making it harder for ATM thieves to target our local shops and ATM machines and will be targeting areas we believe are at increased risk – but we can’t do it alone. "We need the public’s help to report anything suspicious or anything they see that might not seem quite right, no matter how small or insignificant it may seem. "One call could make all the difference and potentially stop a store or petrol station being targeted." Police want anyone with information, including dashcam or video doorbell footage, to contact them. They are also reminding the public to take extra precautions, including ensuring vehicles have working trackers, especially high-performance cars and heavy vehicles like transits and flatbeds that could be used in similar crimes. Other advice includes installing CCTV or video doorbells, and reporting any suspicious behaviour such as people tampering with number plates, appearing to study ATMs, or attaching fake "out of order" signs to machines. Concerns should also be raised about unfamiliar high-performance or heavy vehicles parked in the area, especially if they have been left for several days. Anyone with information about the Littleport incident is asked to contact police online quoting incident 52 of 6 November or Op ATMosphere. Those without internet access can call 101.

metadata.title: Care home resident, 79, rediscovers zest for life with day at the races
metadata.contentSnippet: A day at the races has helped a care home resident rediscover his zest for life in Huntingdon.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Care home resident, 79, rediscovers zest for life with day at the races
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A day at the races has helped a care home resident rediscover his zest for life in Huntingdon. Paul Austen, 79, enjoyed the special outing thanks to staff at The Chase care home, who learned about his lifelong passion for horseracing during a short respite stay. Paul, from the Cotswolds, had become withdrawn following a stroke last year that affected his mobility. The Chase - Enjoying the Day (Image: The Chase) Lauren Mair, general manager at The Chase, said: "When Paul first arrived, we could see that he had been through a very tough period. "Rather than pushing him too early, we took the time to get to know him, understand what mattered to him, and build a plan to help rebuild confidence at his own pace. "Once we discovered his love of horseracing, the idea of taking him to the races felt perfect. The Chase - Incredible Racehorse (Image: The Chase) "The change in him was wonderful to see. "He was excited, engaged, and couldn’t wait to get back out there again." Two members of staff accompanied Mr Austen to the races, and the home prepared a special lunch for him beforehand, complete with his favourite gin and tonic. His wife, Tina, said: "When I first heard about the trip, I had no words to describe how happy it made me. The Chase - Waiting for the Race (Image: The Chase) "I cannot thank the team enough – it was above and beyond anything we could possibly have wished for, and by far the best thing that had happened since Paul had his stroke. "I had happy tears hearing about it and couldn’t wait to hear all about his day. "Thank you all so much." Paul said: "A huge thank you from me and my family to everyone at The Chase for organising such an amazing day. "A few weeks ago, I couldn’t have imagined I’d be out at the races again, so it was wonderful and really refreshing to be out and about enjoying myself."

metadata.title: Russell Brand found guilty of charges of rape and sexual assault
metadata.contentSnippet: Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault after a court trial

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Russell Brand found guilty of charges of rape and sexual assault
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The actor was found guilty of raping a 21-year-old fan after meeting her at a 2009 stand-up show at the Hammersmith Apollo. Jurors also found Brand guilty of sexually assaulting a Capital Radio worker after encountering her in a corridor in 2005 and of sexually assaulting a Channel 4 worker during a forced massage in 2009. Brand, 51, was found guilty of groping another MTV worker during a party at a Soho bar in 2004, but not guilty of going on to orally rape her in a toilet. Russell Brand guilty of three charges of sexual assault and one of rape. He is told he is facing a 'lengthy custodial sentence.' He will be sentenced on Monday https://t.co/v5iH03L3UK — CourtNewsUK (@CourtNewsUK) November 5, 2026 Jurors found Brand not guilty on charges of raping a woman he met at a cabaret show on the fringes of the 1999 Labour Party conference in Bournemouth and of trying to drag an MTV worker into a toilet to indecently assault her in 2001. Speaking to Brand after the verdict was delivered, Mr Justice Bennathan said: “You’ve been convicted of a number of offences including rape. “The consequence of that is inevitably a significant custodial term. “My current view is that I therefore have to remand you into custody.” He added that the sentencing hearing would take place on Monday (November 9). Brand had been accused of seven offences against six women spanning 10 years of his showbiz career from 1999 to 2009, where he denied all allegations made. His trial began at Southwark Crown Court on October 12, with the jury hearing testimony from the complainants and witnesses, as well as Brand himself.

metadata.title: Minister responds to claims smoky bacon crisps could be banned in UK in new EU deal
metadata.contentSnippet: Angela Eagle told a Times Radio interviewer to "get a life" when asked about smoky bacon crisp labels and a UK-EU food deal.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Minister responds to claims smoky bacon crisps could be banned in UK in new EU deal
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cabinet minister told an interviewer to “get a life” over a question about smoky bacon crisps. Environment Secretary Dame Angela Eagle was asked whether closer alignment with the European Union could lead to restrictions on the crisps' labels. Speaking to Times Radio host Stig Abell, she compared the issue to the debate about EU rules on bananas during the Brexit referendum. She said: “Oh, Stig. I mean, really, we’ve had EU straight bananas, and now we’re talking about banning smoky bacon crisps, I think you should get a life.” (Image: Peter Byrne/PA) Dame Angela added: “If you want to obsess about smoky bacon crisps, I suppose that’s your choice.” The concerns relate to whether rules on the use of meat names for products without meat could affect flavour descriptions, rather than ban the crisps themselves. FoodNavigator reported that the European Snacks Association had raised the possibility that flavours such as smoky bacon could be caught by the rules. It also reported that an amendment had been proposed to exempt products including snacks from restrictions on flavour descriptions. The question comes ahead of a UK-EU summit in Brussels on November 20, where Prime Minister Andy Burnham is expected to seek agreements on food and farming, emissions trading and youth mobility. The proposed food deal is expected to align the UK with EU plant, animal and food trade standards to remove post-Brexit checks on exports. Dame Angela argued that reducing barriers would make it easier for farmers and food producers to trade with Europe. She said: “We’ve got huge potential growth in our economy if we allow our farmers and food producers to be able to export into Europe again without all the huge uncertainty and the costs and frictions that Brexit brought us.” “This will be a deal that improves that situation and it will enable this economy to grow and for us to have higher levels of prosperity than we’ve had before.” The minister declined to commit to giving farmers more time to adapt to the new trading arrangements, saying that removing barriers quickly would bring “huge economic benefits”. Asked on BBC Radio 4's Today programme about the Government's rejection of farmers' calls for a 24-month transition, she said ministers were listening to their concerns. She said: “The transition is a balance between getting and accessing those benefits as quickly as possible, but dealing with some of the transitional issues that you have to deal with whenever you’re moving from one system to another.” Mr Burnham has said the deals could raise GDP by 0.4%, compared with a previous estimate of 0.3%. Meanwhile, former EU Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier suggested the UK could negotiate to rejoin the bloc without being obliged to adopt the euro, but would have to accept freedom of movement and single market membership. He told Sky News: “If it is the choice of the UK to ask for a new negotiation to rejoin, it’s perfectly possible to begin such a negotiation without any kind of obligation to take part in the euro.” On the single market, Mr Barnier said: “There is no … possible negotiation on any kind of cherry-picking or the single market ‘a la carte’.” Mr Burnham has said the Government will “explore options” for a different long-term relationship with the EU after the summit. He has insisted voters would be “the boss” of any changes, amid questions about EU membership and freedom of movement.

metadata.title: Blue Badge drivers could face unexpected fines despite having a permit
metadata.contentSnippet: UK Blue Badges are recognised in many European countries, but rules and concessions vary, as experts explain.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Blue Badge drivers could face unexpected fines despite having a permit
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: UK Blue Badge holders heading to Italy have been issued a warning over a little-known driving rule that could land them with a fine of up to €335. British disabled drivers have been given a boost after the Department for Transport confirmed that UK Blue Badges will now be recognised in Italy. But motorists have been warned that being able to use their badge does not mean they can simply park or drive wherever they would be allowed to in Britain. Italy has its own regional parking restrictions and traffic rules, with one particular trap involving historic city centres potentially catching holidaymakers out. Letitia Smith, Head of Communications at AllClear Travel Insurance, said the change was welcome news but urged drivers to check local requirements before setting off. She said: “This is brilliant news for disabled drivers heading to Italy, but ‘recognised’ doesn’t mean the rules are the same as at home. Concessions vary from region to region, so don’t assume the parking rules will be the same as you’re used to in the UK. “The biggest thing to watch out for is Italy’s restricted traffic zones, or ZTLs, which cover many of the historic city centres. Your badge may give you access but check whether you need to register your number plate with local authorities first. Cameras log all car entries, and driving in without correct authorisation can mean a fine of between €84 and €335.” The warning is not limited to Italy. Disabled drivers planning to visit several countries should check the rules separately for each destination. Ms Smith said: “If you’re planning a wider European road trip, check each country's Blue Badge rules separately. Denmark and Switzerland require parking discs if you use time concessions, and in Spain recognition is decided by local authorities, so it can be different from one town to the next.” The Government has published guidance on using a UK Blue Badge in the European Union, including information for motorists planning trips abroad. UK Blue Badges are recognised in many European countries, but rules and concessions vary. Drivers should check local requirements before travelling. UK Blue Badges are recognised in: Countries with additional conditions or restrictions: Two important rules to remember: Italy's restricted traffic zones, known as ZTLs, operate in many historic city centres and limit which vehicles can enter. Blue Badge recognition may allow disabled motorists to access certain areas, but drivers could still need to register their number plate with the local authority before entering. Cameras monitor vehicles going into these zones, so motorists who drive in without the correct authorisation risk being fined between €84 and €335. The rules can vary between regions and towns, making it important to check the requirements for the specific destination rather than assume the same concessions apply everywhere. Recommended reading: AllClear has highlighted three things disabled drivers should consider before travelling to Italy. Check the local parking rules Look up the rules for the exact area you are visiting, including whether you need to register your vehicle or display a local notice alongside your UK Blue Badge. Take supporting documents Carry a translation of your Blue Badge and any relevant supporting paperwork, such as a doctor's letter. This may be requested in countries with stricter parking requirements. Check your hire car excess Blue Badges can be used in hire cars, but motorists should check how much they would have to pay if the vehicle is damaged. A car hire excess waiver through travel insurance could help avoid a hefty bill if the car is scraped or damaged, particularly on narrow streets.

metadata.title: Which? warning over common mistake that is making homes colder and bills higher
metadata.contentSnippet: Which? explains why it advises against drying washing on radiators, with alternatives and tips for reducing moisture indoors.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Which? warning over common mistake that is making homes colder and bills higher
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Drying clothes on radiators could leave homes colder and bills higher, Which? has warned. In a TikTok video, the consumer organisation advises households to stop putting wet washing directly on radiators and suggests using an airer instead. It says damp clothes can act as a barrier to heat, potentially leaving a room taking longer to warm up and increasing energy use. Which? also raises the risk of mould when moisture from drying clothes ends up in the air inside a home. Which? suggests putting washing on an airer near a radiator rather than covering it, allowing air to circulate around the room. For people who need another option, it suggests a heated airer for smaller loads or a tumble dryer. However, a heated airer does not make the moisture disappear, so the room still needs ventilation. In separate tests of indoor drying methods, Which? found that the cheapest option depends partly on the amount of washing. It says an unheated airer uses no electricity, while its tested heated airers took around four to five hours to dry a small cotton load. The organisation found a heated airer could save money compared with vented or condenser tumble dryers when a small load fits on it in one go. For larger loads that need several rounds on an airer, Which? says a tumble dryer is likely to be cheaper to run. Heat pump dryers have lower running costs than vented and condenser models, according to its comparison, although they can cost more to buy. Ventilation matters whichever indoor drying method is used: South Kesteven District Council advises drying washing outside if possible. If that is not possible, it recommends a heated, well-ventilated room, such as a bathroom with the door closed, and says not to put clothes on radiators. The council advises opening windows wider or using extractor fans where fitted when drying clothes, and keeping permanent vents clear. Energy Saving Trust says condensation forms when moisture in the air meets a cold surface, such as a window. Its advice notes that damp can have other causes too, including leaks, damaged guttering and faults that allow groundwater into walls. Signs of a problem can include persistent condensation, a musty smell, peeling wallpaper or mould, according to the trust. It says the underlying cause needs to be addressed, and leaks or signs of rising damp should be dealt with quickly.

metadata.title: British man with Ebola in DRC to be flown to UK for treatment
metadata.contentSnippet: A British healthcare worker has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo and is expected to be medically evacuated to the UK for treatment.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: British man with Ebola in DRC to be flown to UK for treatment
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A British man has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo. He is expected to be flown back to the UK for treatment following the diagnosis. A Government spokesperson said: "A British citizen currently in the DRC has tested positive for Ebola. "The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated." The patient, identified by Reuters as a healthcare worker, is expected to be medically evacuated to the UK, though the timing of the flight remains unclear. Only four cases of Ebola have ever been confirmed in the UK, including three involving health workers who responded to the outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015. Dr Damien Tully, associate professor at the Medical Research Council/Uganda Virus Research Institute and London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine Uganda Research Unit, said: "This case is a stark reminder of the risks faced by those responding to the outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the DRC. "However, it does not suggest that the virus has become more transmissible or that the threat to the UK has increased." Dr Tully described the infection as "deeply concerning, but it is not entirely unexpected." He said: "Healthcare workers are on the front line of these outbreaks, often treating severely ill patients under extremely challenging conditions. "Even with rigorous protective measures, accidental exposures can occur." He stressed that the risk to the British public "from this planned medical evacuation is extremely low" because Ebola is "transmitted primarily through direct contact with infected bodily fluids, and people are not generally infectious until they develop symptoms." The UK has two high-level isolation units equipped to handle such cases – at the Royal Free Hospital in London and the Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle. Dr Tully said: "These facilities are equipped with specialist isolation systems and staffed by highly trained infectious disease teams."

metadata.title: 'Enormous sadness' as beloved Hunts department store to close
metadata.contentSnippet: Beloved department store Townrow is set to close its store in St Ives, Huntingdonshire for good, insisting the decision was not taken lightly.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Enormous sadness' as beloved Hunts department store to close
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A beloved Huntingdonshire department store has announced with "enormous sadness" that it is set to close its doors for good. Townrow, a family department store business which opened in 1871, insisted the "difficult" decision to close its St Ives store was not taken lightly. Retailer Eaden Lilley went into administration in February 2009 and their 10,000 square foot St Ives store on Bridge Street was purchased by Townrow. The historic independent chain sells clothing, shoes, and kitchenware and also has stores in Maldon and Frinton-on-Sea in Essex. Managing Director Edward Townrow said: "Like many independent retailers, we have faced increasingly challenging trading conditions, rising operating costs and changes in shopping habits. "Despite exploring a number of alternatives, we have regrettably been unable to establish a financially sustainable future for the store in its current form. "What makes this decision particularly difficult is the extraordinary relationship we have with the people of St Ives. "Our customers have been nothing short of wonderful. "Over the years, we have been privileged to welcome generations of families through our doors. "We have shared in their everyday lives, celebrated special occasions with them and formed friendships that extend far beyond the shop floor. "Their kindness, warmth and loyalty have meant more to us than I can possibly express. "I want every customer to know how genuinely grateful we are for their support." Mr Townrow also paid tribute to the "remarkable" team at the St Ives store. He said: "They are the heart and soul of the store, and I could not be prouder of them. "Their dedication, professionalism and genuine care for our customers have made Townrow a very special place." The store will hold a closing-down sale in the coming weeks. Mr Townrow added: "Although this marks the end of a chapter for our existing St Ives store, we remain committed to our other stores and to the values that have defined Townrow for more than 150 years. "Finally, to our customers, our colleagues and the entire St Ives community: thank you, from the bottom of my heart. "It has been an absolute privilege to be part of your town."

metadata.title: MPs demand timeline for delayed Cambridgeshire special schools with 270 places
metadata.contentSnippet: A trio of MPs are demanding answers from ministers over delays to two long-promised special schools.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: MPs demand timeline for delayed Cambridgeshire special schools with 270 places
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A trio of MPs are demanding answers from ministers over delays to two long-promised special schools. The Cambridgeshire Liberal Democrats have launched a petition demanding a clear Government timetable for building the schools, left in limbo since the change of administration. Charlotte Cane (Ely and East Cambridgeshire), Pippa Heylings (South Cambridgeshire), and Ian Sollom (St Neots and Mid Cambridgeshire) said the Government has repeatedly failed to provide a timetable for the projects in Gamlingay and March, both of which were agreed before the general election and scheduled to open this September. The schools would create 270 places for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Ian Sollom (St Neots and Mid Cambridgeshire) pictured, Charlotte Cane (Ely and East Cambridgeshire), and Pippa Heylings (South Cambridgeshire), said the Government has repeatedly failed to provide a timetable for the projects in Gamlingay and March (Image: Ian Sollom) The MPs said: "Families were promised these schools and then left in the lurch as the planned opening dates for both schools passed without so much as a shovel in the ground. "And now ministers still refuse to say when they will actually be built. "That simply isn’t good enough." The future of the schools was cast into doubt when the Government revised its building plans. Cambridgeshire County Council had already secured a funding settlement and lobbied for the full amount needed, but despite this, there is still no clear timeline for opening the new special schools. Charlotte Cane (Ely and East Cambridgeshire) pictured, Pippa Heylings (South Cambridgeshire), and Ian Sollom (St Neots and Mid Cambridgeshire) said the Government has repeatedly failed to provide a timetable for the projects in Gamlingay and March. (Image: Charlotte Cane) The MPs warned that the delays are hitting children and families directly. They said: "Every child with special educational needs deserves the right support, in the right place, at the right time. "Parents are fighting tooth and nail just to find a place, while the County Council is forced to pour far more money into private placements. "Children and their families lose out and taxpayers foot the bill, nobody wins." They vowed to keep pressing ministers for action. The MPs said: "We will keep pressing ministers until these 270 places are delivered. "This Government is harming children with their dither and delay. They must publish a clear timeline now and give parents, carers and teachers the clarity they deserve. "Please sign and share our petition to tell the Government how important it is to build these new special schools." Cambridgeshire County Council is paying for places at private special schools, which cost an average of 2.5 times more than state provision. The MPs argue that years of underinvestment in SEND provision under both Conservative and now Labour administrations are letting down children, families, and professionals, while also risking higher long-term costs for social care and the NHS. The projects are known as Greensands Academy in Gamlingay and Lime Academy in March.

metadata.title: Almost 3,000 attend Huntingdon's record-breaking Halloween town trail
metadata.contentSnippet: Almost 3,000 people filled the streets of Huntingdon town centre for a Halloween event.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Almost 3,000 attend Huntingdon's record-breaking Halloween town trail
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Almost 3,000 people filled the streets of Huntingdon town centre for a Halloween event. The Trick or Treat Town Trail, organised by BID Huntingdon through its Discover Huntingdon brand, took place on Saturday, October 31 between 4pm and 6pm, drawing record crowds and transforming the town centre into a family-friendly Halloween hotspot. Paul Sweeney, chief executive officer of BID Huntingdon, said: "Halloween is without doubt my favourite event of the year, and seeing almost 3,000 people enjoying our Trick or Treat Town Trail was just fantastic. Families enjoyed free Halloween activities across Huntingdon town centre (Image: BID Huntingdon) "What makes this event so special is the opportunity to bring families into the heart of Huntingdon, creating wonderful memories while introducing children and their parents to shops and businesses they may never have discovered before. "These experiences are so important in building lasting connections between our community and our High Street, and I'm particularly proud that we can offer events like this completely FREE for everyone to enjoy." Families in costume filled the High Street, collecting treats from 20 participating businesses that stayed open late for the occasion. The event has quickly become a favourite in the town’s calendar, offering a safe and welcoming environment for children to enjoy trick-or-treating. A spooky soundtrack played through the town centre speaker system, adding to the festive atmosphere. Local businesses helped bring the annual Trick or Treat Trail to life (Image: BID Huntingdon) Earlier in the week, Discover Huntingdon hosted a pumpkin patch event on Tuesday, October 27, which featured a town-wide hunt for 27 handmade pumpkins hidden in shop windows. More than 400 pumpkins were given away during the event. Both activities are part of BID Huntingdon First’s ongoing efforts to promote the town centre through accessible, family-focused events that support local businesses and strengthen community ties. Mr Sweeney said: "A huge thank you to everyone who took part and helped make this year's celebrations our biggest yet."

metadata.title: Calls to cut state pension age to 65 and free up jobs for younger workers grow
metadata.contentSnippet: More than 112,000 people have backed a petition to cut the state pension age to 65, arguing it could free up jobs for younger workers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Calls to cut state pension age to 65 and free up jobs for younger workers grow
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A petition calling for the state pension age to be cut to 65 for everyone has passed 112,000 signatures, with the campaign now set to be considered for a debate in Parliament. The petition, created by Michelle Gill, argues that lowering the retirement age would allow people to retire with dignity, avoid hardship and potentially free up jobs for younger workers entering the labour market. It has attracted 112,304 signatures and remains open until March 16, 2027. The campaign comes as the state pension age is gradually increasing from 66 to 67, with the change having started in April 2026 and due to be completed by March 2028. However, the Government has already rejected the call to bring the pension age back down to 65, saying it has no plans to make the change. The petition says: "Reduce the state pension age to 65. We believe this could mean people can retire with dignity and avoid hardship. We also think it could free up jobs for younger workers. "Many aged 65–67 face poor health, caring pressures, and limited work options, which we think is unfair." The campaign passed the 100,000-signature threshold, meaning the Petitions Committee will consider it for debate in Parliament. An update published on October 24 confirmed that the petition would be considered for debate. It does not mean a debate has been scheduled or that the Government has agreed to change the rules. In its response, published on October 13, the Government said: "The Government has no plans to lower the State Pension age. "There are no plans to reduce State Pension age to 65." Ministers pointed to rising life expectancy and said pension age policy takes account of the fact that people are living longer and society is ageing. The Government cited Office for National Statistics projections showing that men aged 66 in the UK could expect to live a further 19.3 years on average in 2026, while women of the same age could expect to live another 21.9 years. By 2046, those figures are projected to increase by a further 1.6 years. The response also said increases to the state pension age had been in legislation since the Pensions Act 1995 and were intended to maintain fairness between generations and protect public finances. The Government confirmed that its Third State Pension Age Review is underway. The review will consider what state pension age is appropriate for future decades, taking into account a range of evidence, including life expectancy projections, findings from the Government Actuary, independent reports from Dr Suzy Morrissey and the Pensions Commission, and lessons from previous increases. The Government also acknowledged that people aged 50 and over can face barriers to staying in work or finding a new job. These include ill health, disability, caring responsibilities, menopause and outdated skills or qualifications. Ministers said support for older workers includes dedicated 50PLUS Champions, additional time with work coaches for new Universal Credit claimants aged over 50, and Midlife MOTs delivered in Jobcentres. The petition, which can still be signed here, argues that lowering the state pension age could free up jobs for younger people. In its response, the Government said it was investing an additional £2.5 billion by 2029 into the Youth Guarantee and Growth and Skills Levy. It said the investment would support almost one million young people and create up to 500,000 opportunities to earn and learn. The measures include expanded Youth Hubs, additional work experience and training, a £3,000 Youth Jobs Grant and a £2,000 apprenticeship hiring payment for employers. The Government also said it would provide a fully funded six-month job for long-term unemployed people aged 18 to 24. The petition remains open for signatures until March 16, 2027.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire firefighters tackle smoke-filled soft play rescue exercise
metadata.contentSnippet: On-call firefighters have been putting their skills to the test through a series of training exercises in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire firefighters tackle smoke-filled soft play rescue exercise
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: On-call firefighters have been putting their skills to the test through a series of training exercises in Cambridgeshire. Crews from Thorney and Ely have taken part in a range of scenarios as part of their regular weekly training, known as drill nights, to ensure they remain prepared for real-life emergencies. New firefighters at Ely practised safely pitching a large ladder, a task that requires a four-person team. At Thorney, crews tackled a mock incident involving hazardous materials and heavy smoke, wearing breathing apparatus to search for casualties and extinguish a simulated fire. A spokesperson for Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service said: "The soft play structure provided an excellent setting to test firefighters' ability to work through tight, restricted spaces while remaining calm under pressure. "Thank you to Play2Day Wisbech for hosting us." Training doesn’t always take place at stations, however. Thorney firefighters recently completed a confined space exercise at Play2Day Wisbech, a children’s soft play centre. Wearing full breathing apparatus and with vision deliberately obscured to simulate smoke, firefighters navigated the play structure to find and rescue training casualties. Paul Oliver, group commander and head of on-call for the service, said: "Being an on-call firefighter is a very exciting role. "Our crews take part in all kinds of training to help maintain their skills to keep them ready to respond to emergencies, whether its station based drills or larger exercises with other stations involving more complex scenarios. "It’s a great way to learn new skills and take on a challenge. "We are always looking to recruit more local people that can join stations as on-call firefighters. "We’d urge anyone living close to one of our on-call stations and can respond to emergencies around other commitments to visit our website to find out more about joining." More information is available on the Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service website.

metadata.title: Vintage 1960s train to take Cambridgeshire passengers on Christmas rail tour
metadata.contentSnippet: A vintage 1960s train is set to take passengers on Christmas rail tour from Peterborough and Huntingdon to Canterbury Christmas Market this winter.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Vintage 1960s train to take Cambridgeshire passengers on Christmas rail tour
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A vintage 1960s train is set to take Cambridgeshire passengers on Christmas rail tour to a historic city this winter. The Canterbury Christmas Cantata, organised by UK Railtours, will see the vintage train depart from Peterborough on Saturday, December 12, before heading to the walled city of Canterbury. It will stop at Huntingdon, Stevenage, Potters Bar, Finsbury Park and Kensington Olympia. Passengers will travel in classic Mark 2 carriages pulled by two 1960s Class 37 diesel locomotives, known to enthusiasts as "Tractors" for their distinctive engine sound. Travellers can choose between a six-hour stop in Canterbury to enjoy its cathedral and Christmas market or remain onboard for the 'Festive Tractor Trek' mini-tour through coastal Kent. The train will take passengers to the historic city of Canterbury to enjoy the Christmas market (Image: Supplied) Onboard refreshments will be available from 'The Railway Diners' Buffet Car. The train will depart from Peterborough at 6.33am, returning at 9.17pm, and depart from Huntingdon at 6.52am, returning at 9pm. Standard tickets begin at £129 for adults and £109 for juniors, with first-class non-dining at £229. The optional mini-tour costs an additional £30. Bookings can be made via the UK Railtours website.

metadata.title: Godmanchester Rovers’ winless run continues as Knowle strike late in fog
metadata.contentSnippet: Godmanchester Rovers’ winless league run continued as Knowle FC struck late to claim a hard-earned victory in worsening fog.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Godmanchester Rovers’ winless run continues as Knowle strike late in fog
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Godmanchester Rovers’ winless league run continued as Knowle FC struck late to claim a hard-earned victory in worsening fog. The league fixture took place on Saturday at the Peter Hodson Community Ground, in misty, gloomy conditions. Rovers had collected only one point from their previous six matches, while Knowle had taken two points from three after winning their opening eight games. The visitors began the afternoon second in the table, but neither side looked capable of imposing itself during a largely uneventful first half. Chances were scarce, although Zane Campbell cut inside from the left and forced a good save from Knowle goalkeeper Matt Horton. Just before the interval, referee Michael Dunkley dismissed the away side’s appeal for a penalty after a challenge involving Hayden Purves. The match changed shortly before the hour when Rovers full-back Alfie-Ray Turner stayed down following a challenge. Both benches called for play to be stopped, but the referee allowed the game to continue until the ball eventually went out. Matty Allan then received a ten-minute sin-bin punishment after voicing the home side’s frustration at the decision. Rather than pushing the visitors back, Rovers attempted to manage the game from deep and invited increasing pressure. Jack Mason produced an excellent save to keep the hosts level, but Knowle continued to threaten before taking the lead after 70 minutes. Captain Jack Duggan’s effort appeared to be heading wide, only for two deflections to send the ball looping over Mason and into the opposite corner. Rovers’ task became harder five minutes later when Tim Momodu, recently cautioned, committed another rash challenge and was shown a second yellow card. Seb Hayes introduced Declan Rogers and Micael Goncalves in a desperate attempt to rescue the contest, but Knowle saw out the remaining minutes as the fog thickened. Rovers now face successive away games against Lutterworth and Highgate United before hosting fellow strugglers FC Stratford on November 21.

metadata.title: Subway plans to open 70 new UK stores inside Asda supermarkets
metadata.contentSnippet: Subway plans to open up to 70 more restaurants in Asda stores over four years as part of a wider expansion.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Subway plans to open 70 new UK stores inside Asda supermarkets
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Up to 70 more Subway restaurants could open inside Asda supermarkets. The sandwich chain has expanded its agreement with the supermarket, with the new UK restaurants planned over the next four years. Subway said the deal would increase the number of its restaurants in Asda stores by more than 50 per cent. The company said Asda had expanded its portfolio to more than 120 Subway restaurants in the past year. The Asda partnership forms part of a wider plan to double Subway's restaurant footprint across Europe, the Middle East and Africa to 10,000 by 2031. That target also includes India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Pakistan, according to the company. Tracy Gehlan, president of Subway in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, said: “We’re building on a strong foundation across EMEA, with significant opportunities to grow in both existing and new markets.” She added: “Our ambition to double our footprint reflects our confidence in the brand, our development partners and the long-term potential across the region. “By expanding in the right locations and improving the experience for our guests and franchisees, we can continue bringing Subway to more guests in EMEA.” Over the past 18 months, Subway said it had signed six master franchise agreements across 14 countries in the region. These span Central Europe, Azerbaijan, the Nordics, Iberia and Qatar. From January 1, 2027, new and refurbished Subway restaurants across the region will use the company's Blueprint design and operating model. Subway said the model includes breakfast and coffee, grab-and-go options and an evening offering called Subway After Dark.

metadata.title: Channel 4 axes major series after 11 years amid 'serious allegations of wrongdoing'
metadata.contentSnippet: Channel 4 has cancelled Married At First Sight UK after an external review - season six and a UK/Australia spin-off will not be aired.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Channel 4 axes major series after 11 years amid 'serious allegations of wrongdoing'
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Channel 4 has cancelled Married At First Sight UK. The decision follows an external review prompted by "serious allegations of wrongdoing" involving the show. Earlier this year, two female participants alleged rape and a third claimed sexual misconduct by their on-screen husbands in a BBC Panorama documentary aired in May. In June, a cast member was arrested on suspicion of rape. All three men have denied the allegations. Chief executive of Channel 4, Priya Dogra, said: "Welfare across all our programmes is a primary concern. "Whilst the review praised the welfare protocols in place and made no findings that Channel 4 breached the Ofcom Code or that the format is inherently unsafe, I have to consider when is the right time for Channel 4 to move on from a format. "The recommendations are eminently sensible and feasible, but considering their wholesale implementation provoked fundamental questions about the editorial proposition of a show that, I believe, has now run its course over 10 years." She also addressed the women who made the allegations. Ms Dogra said: "I am very sorry for the distress those women have clearly felt. "I hope our actions – in swiftly commissioning the review and taking clear, decisive steps – demonstrate our commitment to the wellbeing of all contributors and our desire to relentlessly strengthen industry standards." The sixth season of Married at First Sight UK, filmed earlier this year, will not be aired. A planned spin-off series, featuring contestants from the UK and Australian versions, was also halted during the review. The external review was commissioned by Ms Dogra after the allegations surfaced. It was split into two parts: Channel 4 said the reviews did not attempt to judge the allegations, which remain a matter for the relevant authorities. Clyde & Co reviewed more than 31,000 documents and 20 hours of footage. Their findings concluded that Channel 4 and production company CPL had complied with the Ofcom Broadcasting Code and had not breached any regulations in handling the issues raised. However, the review identified isolated incidents where the welfare framework was not fully followed. One example involved participants breaking the code of conduct regarding "prohibited substances." They received a first and final warning instead of being removed from the show. Ms Heggessey’s review also found that some aspects of the programme could "implicitly put pressure on contributors to be intimate" and that participants could "become dependent on production and lose touch with reality," impacting their ability to make decisions. The review recommended improvements, including reducing the frequency of questions about couples’ physical relationships and discontinuing Intimacy Week and Partner Swap Week. It also suggested changing the show’s "leave or stay" mechanism. Currently, if one person in a couple chooses to leave but the other wants to stay, both must remain for another week. The review proposed allowing a participant to leave if they wish. Despite these concerns, the review described the welfare protocols as "extensive, extremely thorough and of a high standard." Ms Dogra said implementing the recommendations would require a "materially greater level of intervention, monitoring and supervision that would fundamentally alter the format and editorial proposition of the programme." She concluded that, given the maturity of the show and the required changes, ending the series was the right decision. Channel 4 said the budget for Married At First Sight UK will be redirected toward "bold, innovative new programmes from the UK independent production community." Production company CPL said it understood the decision and emphasised its commitment to contributor welfare. A spokesperson said: "CPL has always put contributor welfare at the heart of its programme making and will continue to do so. "CPL have worked closely with Channel 4 for many years and throughout the review process, and we look forward to working with them again in the future." Did you used to watch Married at First Sight UK? Let us know in the poll above.

metadata.title: Concern over refurbished venue’s projected doubling of average ticket prices
metadata.contentSnippet: Concerns have been raised as average ticket prices could double following a major Cambridge Corn Exchange refurbishment.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Concern over refurbished venue’s projected doubling of average ticket prices
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Concerns have been raised as average ticket prices could double following a major Cambridge venue’s refurbishment. The Corn Exchange is set to be redeveloped as part of the wider £95.7m Civic Quarter scheme to revitalise the city centre. The venue, considered the largest performance venue in the East of England, would see upgrades to the main auditorium, improvements to foyers and bar areas, improved seating, acoustics, sound quality and lighting. The wider plans also include work on refurbishing the Guildhall, Market Square and public spaces in-between. A report to Cambridge City Council ’s performance, assets and strategy overview and scrutiny committee said a revived Corn Exchange would act “as the catalyst for a renewed arts and culture scene in Cambridge drawing on its roots which saw it at the forefront of the changing trends in the UK’s music scene.” Sam Scharf, the council’s director of communities, said: “It’s already failed – I mean, last year it rained a bit and we had to cancel Tim Peake. “We then put a short-term remedy in with a bit of leading on top and that is not going to hold up – it’s not got any longevity.” Council officers said income from the venue will help fund the rest of the Civic Quarter scheme and project it will increase by a large amount after the refurbishment. Performances are estimated to increase from 180 a year to 340 and average ticket prices for council-run events from £24 plus VAT currently to £50 plus VAT in year five of the new venue’s opening. Officers said this only applies for events they self-promote and a larger amount of their income comes from hiring the venue out, when they don’t have control of ticket prices. Cllr Beth Gardiner-Smith said: “The business case also notes that the projection of event income is high compared to the benchmark venues. “I think it’s projecting a 43 per cent increase in attendance in year five and similar increases in performances. That feels big to me so I just want to make sure that we think that is robust. “What I don’t think we want to see, but maybe others would disagree, is that people across Cambridge are priced out of going to events on a regular basis at the Corn Exchange. “It’s a public venue for a purpose and it’s all part of this idea that we are creating a public realm and a civic space for our community and therefore we want tickets and events to remain affordable wherever possible.” Council officers said that the higher end of tickets is “growing exponentially” compared to lower-priced tickets which has driven up the average. Chair of the committee, Cllr Karen Young, said: “I’m hearing a lot of concern about the public not being priced out so we will pass that message onto cabinet.”

metadata.title: Cambs knifeman jailed after stabbing ex-girlfriend's new partner
metadata.contentSnippet: A St Neots knifeman has been jailed after stabbing his ex-girlfriend’s new partner during a confrontation at her home.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs knifeman jailed after stabbing ex-girlfriend's new partner
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire knifeman has been jailed after stabbing his ex-girlfriend’s new partner during a confrontation at her home. Matthew Beckett, 32, of Damson Crescent, St Neots, admitted wounding or inflicting grievous bodily harm without intent and possessing a knife in public. The attack took place less than two weeks after Beckett was ordered not to visit his former partner’s home as part of his bail conditions, after pleading guilty to harassing her in June this year. Beckett arrived at the property on June 29, argued with the woman’s new partner and left. He later returned, banging on the door while armed with a knife. When the man opened the door, Beckett lunged at him with the knife. The victim backed away as Beckett fled down the stairwell. The man chased him, but Beckett stabbed him in the chest through the stair railings and pinned him against a wall. Matthew Beckett previously pleaded guilty to harassing his ex-girlfriend (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) The victim was taken to hospital with serious but non-life-threatening injuries, while Beckett was arrested. He was sentenced to two years and three months in prison at Huntingdon Law Courts on Tuesday, November 3. Detective Constable Luke Currie said: "Beckett had been given clear bail conditions to stay away from his former partner’s home, but chose to ignore them. "Not only did he turn up at the address, but he also returned armed with a knife and this incident could easily have resulted in an even more serious outcome. "I hope this sentence provides some reassurance to the victim and others affected by Beckett’s actions."

metadata.title: The Cambridge Oven bakery opens in St Ives to queues out the door
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire food reviewer Lucy Melton shares her thoughts following a recent visit to The Cambridge Oven in St Ives.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: The Cambridge Oven bakery opens in St Ives to queues out the door
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire food reviewer Lucy Melton shares her thoughts following a recent visit to The Cambridge Oven in St Ives I had my eye on The Cambridge Oven ever since I heard it was coming to St Ives, so I made sure I headed there as soon as I could. I went on the first Saturday it was open and, unsurprisingly, there were people queuing out the door. It moved quickly though, and although a few things had already sold out, there was still a really good variety to choose from. Spinach and ricotta croissant (Image: Lucy Melton) The Cambridge Oven has been open in Cambridge since 2018 and has always been a must-stop when visiting, so I was really pleased to hear it was opening closer to home. I couldn't decide between sweet and savoury, so naturally I went for both. Starting with the spinach and ricotta croissant, I absolutely loved this. There was plenty of filling, the flavours worked really well together and the highlight was definitely the cheesy pastry, which added so much flavour. I then had the banana Danish, and the pastry was crispy, flaky and soft all at once. There was a lovely sugary coating which made it extra yummy, and I absolutely loved the banana crème in the centre. Banana Danish (Image: Lucy Melton) It had such a lovely flavour and went really well with the dried banana. I did wish there was a little more of the filling, but the pastry around it was tasty enough to make up for it. My brother-in-law went for the apple and almond Danish and really enjoyed it too. He particularly liked how light the pastry was and thought the filling was great. Overall, I was really pleased with everything I tried and will definitely be back to work my way through more of the menu. I love a visit to St Ives, so The Cambridge Oven will certainly be top of my list each time!

metadata.title: Award-winning Hunts pub features in Sidemen YouTube video watched by millions
metadata.contentSnippet: An award-winning pub, The Cock in Hemingford Grey, featured in a Sidemen YouTube video watched by millions.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Award-winning Hunts pub features in Sidemen YouTube video watched by millions
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An award-winning Huntingdonshire pub featured in a YouTube video watched by millions. The Cock in Hemingford Grey appeared in a video by the YouTube group Sidemen, titled 'SIDEMEN HOW FAR CAN YOU GET (ROAD TRIP EDITION)'. The video, posted on October 25, has racked up more than five million views and sees the social media stars split into pairs and try to drive as far across the UK as they can, completing challenges along the way. One challenge was 'take a selfie with a funny place name' and Sidemen members Ethan and Vik seized the opportunity when they arrived at The Cock. The village pub, which is the national dining pub winner twice, is renowned for its "great location and atmosphere". Oliver Thain, founder and owner of The Cock’s parent company Cambscuisine, said the appearance was "brilliant". Mr Thain said: "We had a bit of a laugh when we heard The Cock had made an appearance in a Sidemen video. "I'm not particularly familiar with the channel myself, but I gather they have a huge following, so it's brilliant to think that millions of people have now seen our little pub in Hemingford Grey. "Although the kitchen was closed when they arrived, the team were very welcoming and managed to rustle them up pork crackling, a great steak and chips and various other dishes. "You can see in the video how much they loved the food! "It was great to see the pub getting a bit of unexpected attention!" The Cock was named the Good Pub Guide's Pub of the Year in 2013, having also been named the best Dining Pub in Cambridgeshire.

metadata.title: Wetherspoon set to open up to 25 more pubs as sales jump higher
metadata.contentSnippet: JD Wetherspoon expects up to 25 further pub openings this financial year after sales rose 8.2 per cent over 14 weeks.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Wetherspoon set to open up to 25 more pubs as sales jump higher
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Up to 25 more Wetherspoon pubs could open this financial year. JD Wetherspoon estimates it could open a further five to 10 managed pubs and 10 to 15 franchised sites in the year ending August 1, 2027. That would be in addition to the six managed pubs and two franchises it has already opened this financial year. The expansion plans came as the pub group reported an 8.2 per cent rise in like-for-like sales in the 14 weeks to November 1, covering its first quarter and a further week. Chairman Tim Martin said: “The company has had a good start to the financial year. “There are still three quarters to go and profit forecasts are very dependent on the level of sales growth.” The six managed pubs opened so far are at Manchester Airport and Heathrow Airport, and in Crewe in Cheshire, Ferndown in Dorset, Dibden Purlieu in Hampshire and Kempston in Bedfordshire. Wetherspoon said it had sold one pub during the period and now had 797 trading managed pubs, alongside 25 franchises. Bar sales rose by 9.4 per cent over the 14 weeks, while food sales increased by 6.8 per cent. Like-for-like growth slowed to 7.5 per cent in the most recent five weeks, compared with 8.6 per cent in the first nine weeks of the quarter. Martin said the company was “comfortable” with market expectations once adjusted for the 53-week financial year. The company put the consensus profit estimate, compiled from seven analysts, at £76.4 million. In the previous 52-week financial year, pre-tax profit fell 28 per cent to £58.6 million as staff and other costs offset higher sales. The company also argued that labour cost increases affect pubs more heavily than supermarkets, estimating the labour cost of a pub pint at £1.68 compared with about 15p for a supermarket pint. Its calculation used an AI-derived estimate of the price of a supermarket pint and wage costs as a percentage of sales. The group argued that the effect had widened the price gap between pub and supermarket pints and reduced employment. Its next trading update is expected on January 20, 2027.

metadata.title: Thousands could unlock £2,600 savings after major government rule change
metadata.contentSnippet: Thousands of young disabled people could find it easier to access their Child Trust Funds under Government plans to simplify the process for parents and carers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Thousands could unlock £2,600 savings after major government rule change
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Thousands of young people who lack the mental capacity to manage their finances could find it easier to access money held in their Child Trust Funds under new Government plans. The proposed changes aim to remove a complicated legal hurdle that has left many disabled young adults and their families facing lengthy and costly court processes to release savings that belong to them. Under the reforms, parents and carers will be able to approach Child Trust Fund providers directly to access the money on behalf of young people who lack the mental capacity to make financial decisions. The Government said the changes could help between 63,000 and 126,000 young adults who have so far faced difficulties accessing their accounts. Child Trust Funds are long-term, tax-free savings accounts introduced for children born between September 1, 2002 and January 2, 2011. The accounts were designed to give young people a financial asset when they reached adulthood, with money becoming accessible at the age of 18. Justice minister Jake Richards said: “Young people who lack the mental capacity to make financial decisions should be able to access their savings as easily as possible – especially when this money was put aside by loved ones to help them take their first steps into adulthood. “This is simply an injustice that we’re finally putting right and as campaigners have argued for years, change is long overdue. “This legislation will ensure this group of young adults no longer face difficulty from accessing money that is rightfully theirs.” Economic secretary to the Treasury Lucy Rigby said the reforms would help tens of thousands more young people access their accounts. She said: “The changes that we’re introducing will help tens of thousands more young people to connect with their child trust funds - worth on average £2,600 each.” Recommended reading: The Government said it would work with others to develop the new process, including deciding who will be able to access the money, what evidence will be needed and what safeguards should be put in place to protect young people who lack mental capacity. Speaking in the Commons, Ms Rigby said: “The last Labour government introduced child trust funds with the intention that every child in this country could access a financial asset as they enter adulthood, and almost three million young people have already accessed their funds, currently containing an average of £2,600 each.” She added: “I am going to be bringing forward an amendment to the Financial Services Bill. The second reading of which is next week, which will enable the Ministry of Justice to make regulations to put this in action.” Anna Bird, chief executive of Contact, said families had faced unnecessary difficulties when trying to access the money. She said: “For too long, tens of thousands of young disabled people and their families have faced a complicated and costly process to access money that rightfully belongs to them.” The Court of Protection will remain available as an alternative route for protecting the financial interests of adults who cannot make financial decisions for themselves.

metadata.title: 'Arson' investigation ongoing after fire at derelict hotel in Cambs
metadata.contentSnippet: Police are investigating "arson" after a huge fire broke out at the derelict Station Hotel on Station Road in March, Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Arson' investigation ongoing after fire at derelict hotel in Cambs
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Police have launched an arson investigation after a huge fire broke out at a derelict hotel in Cambridgeshire. Around 20 firefighters tackled the blaze at the former Station Hotel on Station Road, March, at 12.48pm on Monday, November 2. Crews from March, Wisbech, Chatteris and Stanground, along with the north roaming fire engine, attended. Emergency services closed Station Road to all vehicles and nearby residents were advised to stay in their homes and keep doors and windows closed. Crews contained the fire and stopped it spreading to nearby properties. Emergency services rushed to Station Road in March on November 2 (Image: Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue) On November 3, a spokesperson for Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service said: "Crews have continued to make regular inspections to ensure the area is safe. "Due to the location of the fire and the building structure being unsafe to enter, the firefighting has continued to take place from the outside of building. "The cause of the fire has been determined as deliberate. "Anyone with information should contact police by visiting www.cambs.police.uk to submit an online report or call Crimestoppers on 0800 555111." On November 4, Cambridgeshire Police confirmed they were investigating arson. A spokesperson for the force said: "We are currently treating this as arson. "Work is continuing with the fire service and our investigation is ongoing; no arrests have been made at this time."

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire house with Chinese takeaway in garden goes viral
metadata.contentSnippet: A Peterborough house with a Chinese takeaway in its garden goes viral after influencer Housing Horrors featured the £180,000 Churchfield Road property.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire house has gone viral after a social media star spotted a Chinese takeaway in its back garden. "The outbuilding in the garden of the property is currently being used as a Chinese takeaway – giving the new buyer a fantastic opportunity to make something of their own," the listing reads. Dragon House has a 3.7 out of 5 rating on Google. (Image: Google Maps) "The house itself features two reception rooms, kitchen and downstairs shower room. Whilst upstairs offers two double bedrooms with an en-suite to bedroom one." Jack, who has more than 300,000 followers across his social media channels, highlights unusual homes listed on Rightmove. He encouraged his followers to share their experiences of the takeaway, asking: "If you are from the Peterborough area, what is this Chinese takeaway like? metadata.title: 'Dangerous' sex offender jailed after performing sexual act in front of 14-year-old
metadata.contentSnippet: A "dangerous" Peterborough sex offender who performed a sexual act in front of a 14-year-old girl has been jailed for more than two years.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Dangerous' sex offender jailed after performing sexual act in front of 14-year-old
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A "dangerous" Cambridgeshire sex offender who performed a sexual act in front of a 14-year-old girl has been jailed for more than two years. Paulius Grabauskas, 31, was on police bail for other offences when he approached the girl on Derby Drive, Dogsthorpe, Peterborough, at 9.30am on July 17. He took a sex toy from a bag and used it to perform a sexual act on himself in front of the child. Grabauskas was reported to police in April after exposing himself and touching himself in front of passengers on a Peterborough bus. In June, Grabauskas was reported again after he was seen performing an indecent act in a bush near a primary school in Orton Goldhay, Peterborough. Paulius Grabauskas used a sex toy to perform a sexual act on himself in front of a 14-year-old girl (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) Detective Sergeant Angus Cashman said: "Grabauskas is clearly a dangerous individual who has no control over his sexual urges. "His crimes will have a lasting impact on all of his victims – especially the 14-year-old girl who he targeted and subjected to a disturbing act for his own sexual gratification. "I am pleased he has now faced justice and I’m glad the sentence reflects the seriousness of his actions." Grabauskas, of Eastfield Road, Peterborough, was jailed for two years and three months at Cambridge Crown Court on Friday, October 30. He admitted two counts of exposure and one count of engaging in sexual activity in the presence of a child. He was also handed a 10-year sexual harm prevention order.

metadata.title: NFU calls Autumn Budget a ‘missed opportunity’ for Cambridgeshire family farms
metadata.contentSnippet: The Chancellor’s Autumn Budget has been criticised as a “missed opportunity” to support family farms in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: NFU calls Autumn Budget a ‘missed opportunity’ for Cambridgeshire family farms
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The Chancellor’s Autumn Budget has been criticised as a “missed opportunity” to support family farms in Cambridgeshire. Farmers and industry leaders say the plans offered little to boost business confidence or address the needs of food producers. The National Farmers’ Union (NFU) has called for investment to build resilience in the sector, arguing that a sustainable farming industry is crucial for the rural economy, environmental stewardship and food security. Tom Bradshaw, president of the NFU, said: "This was an opportunity for the government to act on the warm words it made over the summer. NFU Cambridgeshire County Chair Alison Morris (Image: Alison Morris) "It has failed to act and has left farmers and growers feeling abandoned. "The OBR (the Office for Budget Responsibility) has reflected that the food price inflation outlook is significantly higher than previous forecasts. "Yet the government has failed to link domestic food production to food-price inflation, has missed the opportunity to deliver on its commitment that 'food security is national security' and failed to give farm businesses the 'breathing space' that the Chancellor said this Budget was for." The government did announce the removal of tariffs on certain foods and fertilisers to help reduce costs. Chancellor John Healey prepares to deliver the Budget 2026 (Image: John Healey) However, the NFU said most fertiliser already arrives in the UK without tariffs, and any savings would depend on whether benefits are passed down the supply chain. Alison Morris, chair of the NFU Cambridgeshire, said: "This Budget has done nothing to help our farmers. "We need help now not words of we understand. "We urgently need support from the Keep Britain Growing Loan so that we can afford to harvest the crops still in the ground and plant next year’s crops. "Increasing the Annual Investment Allowance to at least £5m, including structures and buildings, scrapping the family farm tax would have gone some way to restoring much-needed confidence."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Nile Rodgers & Chic are set to headline a major night of music near Cambridgeshire. The legendary act will perform at Newmarket Racecourse’s July Course on Friday, July 30, 2027, as part of the popular Newmarket Nights summer concert series, which blends live music with an evening of racing. Nile Rodgers, the iconic co-founder of Chic, said: "Newmarket, we’ve missed you!" "We’re excited to return on Friday July 30th with our all-killer-no-filler set of hits and we can’t wait to turn the racecourse into one huge dancefloor." Nile Rodgers & Chic will headline Newmarket Nights at Newmarket Racecourse, on July 30, 2027. (Image: Jill Furmanovsky) Mr Rodgers is a multiple Grammy Award-winning songwriter, producer, and guitarist. He has penned and produced chart-topping hits with Chic including Le Freak and Good Times, and collaborated with musical legends such as Madonna, Diana Ross, David Bowie, Duran Duran, Daft Punk, Beyoncé, and Sam Smith. Sophie Able, managing director of Newmarket and Lambourn, said: "It’s a real honour to welcome the hitmaker himself back to Newmarket Nights next summer. "Nile Rodgers & CHIC bring an undeniable energy that lights up the July Course every single time. "They deliver the ultimate summer night out and we can’t wait to welcome them back." Ms Able described Newmarket Nights as the "ultimate summer night out," combining world-class racing with headline music performances and a vibrant festival atmosphere. "With a single ticket granting access to both world-class racing and live music, fans enjoy an unforgettable afternoon (and night out) at exceptional value." metadata.title: Cambs scientist named finalist in three Overt STEM Awards categories
metadata.contentSnippet: A Peterborough scientist who grew up in Somersham has been named a finalist in three categories at the Overt STEM Awards 2026.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs scientist named finalist in three Overt STEM Awards categories
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Peterborough scientist who grew up in Somersham has been named a finalist in three categories at the Overt STEM Awards 2026. Raewyn (Rae) Freestone, a registered scientist, has been shortlisted for DEI in STEM, Mentoring Excellence in STEM, and STEM Start-Up. The awards celebrate outstanding contributions to science, technology, engineering, and mathematics across the Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor. RaeBow STEM Outreach aims to make STEM more accessible and inclusive (Image: Raewyn (Rae) Freestone) Raewyn said: "Being a finalist in three categories is an incredible honour. "Having previously received a commendation in the Science Council's Registered Scientist CPD Award in 2021 and then winning in both 2022 and 2023, it is wonderful to receive further recognition for the different areas of STEM that I am passionate about." She currently works as a development technician at Linx Printing Technologies and is a member of the Institute of Science and Technology. With more than 25 years of experience across forensic science, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, research and engineering, Raewyn is committed to making STEM more accessible, inclusive, and visible. The Peterborough scientist is being recognised for her work in STEM (Image: Raewyn (Rae) Freestone) She said: "Throughout my career, I have benefited from people who shared their knowledge, encouragement and opportunities with me. "I believe strongly in giving something back and helping the next generation discover what they can achieve." Alongside her professional work, Raewyn mentors young people through Stemettes, a social enterprise supporting girls, young women, and non-binary individuals in exploring STEM careers. She also volunteers at Peterborough STEM Festival and supports STEM engagement events at Peterborough Cathedral. Rae’s work includes mentoring and community STEM engagement (Image: Raewyn (Rae) Freestone) Her STEM Start-Up nomination recognises RaeBow STEM Outreach, the initiative she founded to inspire the next generation through mentoring, community engagement, and positive role modelling. Raewyn said: "Whether that is through mentoring with Stemettes, volunteering at Peterborough STEM Festival and Peterborough Cathedral, or developing RaeBow STEM Outreach, I want to help more people discover STEM and believe that these opportunities are open to them too." The winners will be announced at a ceremony in Milton Keynes on November 3.
