metadata.title: 5 ways you can recycle your Halloween pumpkin after October 31
metadata.contentSnippet: If you're looking to recycle your pumpkin once Halloween is over, here's what you can do

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 5 ways you can recycle your Halloween pumpkin after October 31
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Millions of pumpkins are picked for carving every Halloween, becoming a staple decoration in homes and windows across the UK. However, once October 31 has been and gone, many people are left wondering what to do with their pumpkins. Around eight million are reportedly thrown away in the UK each year, despite there being several ways they can be reused or recycled instead. If you have a leftover pumpkin at home, there are plenty of ways to make the most of it before reaching for the bin. Millions of pumpkins usually end up being thrown away by Brits every year   (Image: PA) Pumpkins can be used for a variety of foods once they have been cleaned out. Dominique Delacour, dairy expert at CAMBOZOLA, shared: “The best way to recycle your pumpkin after Halloween is to cook with it - never throw it away! "Both the flesh, puplp and the seeds can be turned into something delicious. "Roasted pumpkin works beautifully with creamy cheeses in puff pastry parcels, pasta bakes or toasties, while the seeds can be washed, seasoned and baked until golden for a crunchy topping or snack. "It’s an easy way to cut down on waste and turn your Halloween leftovers into something comforting and indulgent for autumn.” Grating the pumpkin pulp you pull out when carving could also be ideal for use in a pumpkin loaf, pie or muffin. The fruit is high in vitamins A and C, as well as being a good source of fibre. Pumpkins don't just have to be used for food after Halloween, with several creative ways to give them a second life. One option is to turn your pumpkin into a seasonal candle. Clean out the inside before adding melted wax, spices such as cinnamon and ginger, and a wick to fill your home with autumnal scents. Leftover pumpkins can also be turned into planters. Remove the inside, add drainage holes and fill with potting soil and your choice of plants. Another option is to make a bird feeder by cleaning out the pumpkin, cutting openings into the sides and filling it with bird seed before hanging it outside. Pumpkins can be composted (PA)  (Image: PA) Using pumpkin in a DIY face mask can be beneficial. AHAs, or alpha hydroxy acids, are widely praised in the skincare world for their ability to help exfoliate and renew skin, and pumpkins are packed full of them. Josh Novell, Director of Polhill Garden Centre, has shared that pumpkins can be used in your garden once they have been cleaned out. He said: "Next, break the pumpkin up into small chunks. Large pieces take much longer to decompose. "Cutting them into fist-sized chunks or smaller helps them break down quickly and release nutrients evenly into the soil. “One of the biggest mistakes people make is scattering pumpkin pieces across the surface; that’s an open invitation for rats and slugs. "Always bury your pumpkin a few inches deep in the soil as this keeps pests away and helps the microbes get to work faster.” “If you’re digging pumpkins into borders or beds, mix in some dry garden materials like leaves, straw or old compost. "That stops the soil from getting too wet or slimy, and it balances out the carbon and nitrogen levels as the pumpkin breaks down.” If you do need to get rid of your pumpkin, then composting it would be the best option. Chris Taylor from Chris Taylor Gardening shared: "Pumpkins break down quickly and make great compost material. "Just remove any candle wax or decorations, chop it into smaller chunks, and add it to your compost heap. Recommended reading: "The high moisture content helps balance drier materials like leaves or cardboard." You could also offer it up to any gardeners or allotment owners who might be interested in taking it off your hands Aside from that, putting it in a food waste recycling bin also works. What do you do with your pumpkin once Halloween is over? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: I'm a personal finance writer - here are the 8 Budget changes I'm most pleased to see
metadata.contentSnippet: From £100 energy bill help to higher pensions, ISA savings and first-time buyer support, here's my personal finance writer's verdict on Budget 2026.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: I'm a personal finance writer - here are the 8 Budget changes I'm most pleased to see
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Budgets always have winners and losers, but this week there are some genuinely welcome bits of news for many people, and as a personal finance writer, I'm particularly pleased to see help for households facing rising energy bills, pensioners getting a boost, more money for workers and new support for people hoping to buy their first home. Chancellor John Healey has announced a package designed to give families, savers and businesses some breathing space during a challenging economic period. And while there's no magic wand to make the cost of living disappear overnight, I think there are some measures worth celebrating. From £100 landing in millions of bank accounts to a higher State Pension and a new scheme to help first-time buyers, here's what I'm taking away from the Budget – and what it could mean for your money. One of the biggest wins for families is the £100 energy support payment - and the fact that they have chosen to put it in people's banks and not give it directly to the energy companies. Around 20 million households in council tax bands A to D will receive £100 from the Government this winter, with the money expected to arrive directly in bank accounts from January - a time when most people will need it most. I particularly like that families will be free to spend the money however they choose. Whether it's going towards an energy bill, the weekly food shop or another household essential, it gives people a little more flexibility. Some may say it'll get frittered away, but I like the idea that billpayers get to choose - if that's a day out with the kids or new school shoes or even a drink with mates, a cash boost could help the economy as tills ring with a tiny bit more optimism. There's more good news for energy customers, too. The Government plans to move some of the cost of standing charges on gas bills into the unit rate. Around 60% of households are expected to save an average of £45 a year. The removal of VAT from electricity bills is also being extended until July 2031. Of course, households using more energy could end up paying more under the standing charge changes, so it's worth keeping an eye on how your own bill is affected. But overall, I welcome the focus on making energy costs more manageable. Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey delivering his Budget in the House of Commons, London. (Image: House of Commons/UK Parliament/PA Wire) There's some particularly good news for pensioners, with the State Pension set to rise to £13,036 a year from next April under the triple lock. For millions of people who rely on their State Pension to cover everyday essentials, this increase will be an important boost. I also think the announcement of a new tax allowance for pensioners on lower incomes is worth highlighting. The measure is designed to protect pensioners from being dragged into paying income tax simply because their State Pension has increased above the £12,570 personal allowance. This is particularly welcome for those who rely largely on the State Pension and don't have significant additional retirement income - the people who really need some help. Did you spot some good news for savers, too? The planned reduction in the annual cash ISA allowance from £20,000 to £12,000 has been scrapped. That's a big win for anyone who likes the flexibility and tax-free benefits of a cash ISA. It feels like trusting people to make the right choice with their own money rather than legislating where and how they can save. It means savers can continue to put away up to £20,000 a year across their ISAs, subject to the usual rules. I think this is particularly important at a time when people are trying to build emergency savings, put money aside for a deposit or simply earn a return on their hard-earned cash. However, there is a sting in the tail (when isn't there?). Tax on savings income is set to increase from April 2027. Basic-rate taxpayers will pay 24%, higher-rate taxpayers 44% and additional-rate taxpayers 49%. This makes making the most of tax-efficient savings options even more important. My advice is to review where your savings are held and check whether you're making full use of your available ISA allowance. One of the most interesting announcements for aspiring homeowners is the new £4.7 billion Your First Home scheme. The aim is to help around 70,000 households in England take their first step onto the property ladder. The scheme will offer first-time buyers 20% equity loans, potentially reducing the deposit and mortgage they need to find themselves. There will be household income limits of £110,000 outside London and £140,000 in London. For anyone who has been saving for years but struggling to get together enough money to buy a home, this could be a welcome opportunity. There's also a new First-Time Buyer ISA coming in April 2029, which will replace the Lifetime ISA. For eligible buyers, it's certainly an announcement worth watching. This is another announcement I'd put firmly in the positive column. The National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage will rise by 3.9% in April 2027. For workers aged 21 and over, the hourly rate will increase from £12.71 to £13.21. For those aged 18 to 20, it will rise from £10.85 to £11.27. Around 2.3 million workers are expected to benefit. For people on lower incomes, even a modest increase can make a difference to the monthly budget. With food shopping, transport and household essentials continuing to put pressure on finances, having more money coming in is certainly welcome. However, income tax thresholds remain frozen, meaning some workers could find more of their earnings falling into a higher tax bracket as their pay increases. It's a reminder that it's not just your headline pay rise that matters, but how much you actually take home. There's good news for motorists too, and goodness knows, we need it. The fuel duty freeze has been extended, keeping the rate at 52p a litre and cancelling a planned increase in January. For anyone who relies on their car, this is another welcome measure. There's also good news for people who use their own vehicles for work, with the higher tax-free mileage allowance of 55p being made permanent. That should provide some reassurance for employees who use their cars for business journeys and claim mileage expenses. With motoring costs adding up quickly, keeping these allowances in place is a positive step. Pensioners with income up to the value of the full new state pension (to be £13,040 from April 2027) will not pay tax. Mechanism not stated, I suspect there will be an effective increased pensioner allowance with a clawback for income above that. More when I know more. #Budget2026 — Martin Lewis (@MartinSLewis) October 28, 2026 I'm also encouraged by the business rates announcement. The threshold for small business rates relief for retail, hospitality and leisure businesses is increasing from £12,000 to £18,000. The Government estimates this will take around 70,000 additional businesses completely out of paying business rates. That's potentially a significant saving for independent shops, restaurants, cafés and other businesses that are the backbone of our local communities. For businesses trying to keep their prices competitive, invest in their premises or take on staff, reducing overheads could make a real difference. A thriving high street is good news for everyone, so I'm pleased to see measures aimed at supporting the businesses that keep our communities going. The global economic picture is undoubtedly challenging, particularly with the conflict in the Middle East putting pressure on energy prices. But there are some encouraging signs in the forecasts. The OBR has increased its growth forecast for 2026 from 1.1% to 1.2%. While growth for 2027 has been downgraded to 1%, the longer-term forecasts point towards growth of 1.6% in 2028, 1.8% in 2029 and 1.7% in 2030. There is still work to do, but I think it's important to look beyond the immediate economic headlines and recognise that there are opportunities for improvement. The big priority now must be making sure economic growth translates into better wages, more jobs and more money in people's pockets. Let's face facts - times are pretty tough. Most people are struggling - food and fuel cost far too much. But, for me, the biggest takeaway from this Budget is that there are some practical measures that could make a difference at different stages of our financial lives, and no big shocks to make matters worse. Whether you're a pensioner, a first-time buyer, a family with young kids, a saver or a small business owner, there is something in this Budget that could help. I'm particularly pleased to see the State Pension increase, the protection for lower-income pensioners, the decision to retain the £20,000 ISA allowance and the new support for first-time buyers. The £100 energy payment and minimum wage increases are also welcome measures for households feeling the squeeze. Recommended reading: Of course, there are still challenges ahead. Inflation, borrowing costs and weaker growth forecasts show that the economy isn't out of the woods yet. But I think it's important to recognise the positives too. My advice? Take a fresh look at your finances and make the most of any changes that could benefit you. Check your pension, review your savings arrangements, look at your ISA allowance and, if you're hoping to buy your first home, keep an eye on the new scheme. It's not a Budget that's going to change everyone's financial fortunes overnight, but there are some encouraging steps in the right direction. And with household budgets needing all the help they can get, that's certainly something worth celebrating.

metadata.title: Emmerdale and Corrie to face ITV schedule shake-up next week - when to watch
metadata.contentSnippet: ITV soaps Emmerdale and Coronation Street have often been moved or axed from the schedule due to live sport, with next week no different.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Emmerdale and Corrie to face ITV schedule shake-up next week - when to watch
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Both Emmerdale and Coronation Street will have a schedule shake-up soon, with ITV changing its plans due to sport. The popular ITV soaps have often been moved or axed from the schedule due to football matches, with next week no different. Here’s what the changes are and which episodes the TV schedule shakeup affects. Both soaps are being removed from the schedule on Friday, November 6, as Ireland face Argentina in the Nations Championship. The rugby match will be shown from 7.15pm to 10.30pm, with kick-off at 8.10pm. Mark Pougatch will present coverage of the opening match in the Northern Hemisphere leg of the tournament at Aviva Stadium. Emmerdale normally airs from 8pm to 8.30pm, followed by Coronation Street from 8.30pm to 9pm. Together, they form a weekday soap hour on ITV. ITV has not confirmed when the two episodes will be shown instead. They could be moved to the weekend, or viewers could see one fewer episode that week. Schedule changes linked to sport have affected the soaps before, particularly when football matches have been broadcast. Ireland's autumn campaign follows wins over Australia and Japan and a loss to New Zealand in July. Argentina lost to Scotland and England either side of a victory over Wales in the Southern Series. Andy Farrell's side will be aiming to begin its autumn campaign against the Pumas, who will travel to Dublin for the fixture. In other Coronation Street news, star Ryan Prescott is trading the cobbles for the capital in a brand new film role. Prescott, who plays Ryan Connor on the long-running ITV soap, is starring in the comedy-drama Waif, set in the heart of East London. The film explores a world of skateparks, guitar shops, and art openings, and sees Prescott take on the role of Noah, a "drifting art curator" who is trying to make a life for himself. Filming began in London in mid-October, and Prescott has already shared a glimpse of life on set. The Corrie star posted a behind-the-scenes photo on Instagram, posing with writer-director Rocky Rodriguez Jr and actor Jason Flemyng, who plays Miles in the film. In the post, Mr Prescott said: "We are rollllliiiing, first week into the WAIF shoot and loving it, thank you all for the amazing energy on set!" Other photos from the shoot show him alongside Band of Brothers actor Dexter Fletcher, who plays Judge Rodney Bax QC. The cast also includes newcomer Helen Foster as Clem, a "freewheeling single mum." According to the film’s synopsis, "with social services watching, this community of slackers must grow and not give in." No release date has yet been announced. Mr Prescott remains a regular presence on Coronation Street, where he has played Ryan Connor since 2019. He is the third actor to take on the role. In 2023, his character briefly left the show after his affair with Daisy Midgley was exposed. He later returned as part of a major storyline involving steroid addiction. Recently, Ryan has been supporting Dylan Wilson (Liam McCheyne), who is struggling with guilt after a sexual encounter with Betsy Swain (Sydney Martin) led to her having a stroke. Things look set to become even more complicated, however, after Ryan discovers a pregnancy test belonging to his love interest, Bethany Platt, played by Lucy Fallon. Who is your favourite character on Coronation Street? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Legal expert reveals your rights if trick-or-treaters disturb you on Halloween
metadata.contentSnippet: A legal expert has revealed your rights if you are disturbed by trick-or-treaters on Halloween or if anyone causes damage to your property during the holiday.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Legal expert reveals your rights if trick-or-treaters disturb you on Halloween
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Halloween is an exciting time for many families who will be dressing up and trick-or-treating this weekend. Many houses will be decorated with pumpkins and will be handing out chocolates and sweets to children. However, some people are not a fan of this holiday and will be keeping their doors shut during the evening. A property law expert has revealed what homeowners can do if they want to avoid being disturbed on Halloween. If you do not decorate your house, it indicates to people that you do not want to be disturbed. (Image: Getty) Janet Lane, a property law expert from Rogers and Norton, has shared a few steps that homeowners can take to indicate to trick-or-treaters that they do not want to be disturbed. She said: “There is generally an implied permission for somebody to walk up the usual route to your front door and knock, which is why a delivery driver, neighbour or other caller does not normally need express permission first. “But homeowners can make it clear that they do not want Halloween callers. “A locked gate, or a simple and prominent ‘no trick-or-treaters’ notice on the door, gate or window is one of the clearest ways of communicating that visitors are not invited to approach.” Legal action or police involvement is only necessary if the situation escalates into criminal damage, harassment, or anti-social behaviour. Throwing things at a property like eggs, flour, rocks, and silly string or damaging walls, windows, and vehicles falls under criminal damage, according to the Criminal Damage Act 1971. The Public Order Act 1986 states that using abusive, threatening or insulting words or behaviour that causes alarm or distress is also an offence. Lane added: “There is an important difference between a child innocently knocking on the wrong door and behaviour which becomes intimidating or destructive.” “A single knock is one thing. “Repeatedly banging on somebody’s door after being asked to leave, damaging their property or throwing objects at their home is something very different and should never be dismissed as simply part of Halloween.” Janet says that using a clear sign that says ‘no trick-or-treaters please’ and not putting out pumpkins or decorations will signal to people that you do not want to be disturbed. You should also keep gates closed and make sure any signs are visible before people reach your front door. Do you love Halloween or will you be keeping your door closed this year? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Thief jailed for stealing £1,000 of goods in two-week spree
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridge thief Lisa Bradley jailed for 20 months after stealing more than £1,000 from M&S, Superdry, Next and a home during a two-week crime spree.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Thief jailed for stealing £1,000 of goods in two-week spree
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A thief who stole more than £1,000 worth of goods in a two-week crime spree has been jailed. Lisa Bradley. of Chesterton Road, Cambridge, targeted businesses across Cambridge and a home between September 29 and October 11. The 42-year-old stole a £140 case of M&S chocolate from BP in Teversham before going on to steal a backpack from Typo and hundreds of pounds worth of clothing from Superdry. She also stole two duvets worth £150 from Next and a parcel containing 84 pouches of cat food, worth £82, from outside a home in Molewood Close. Bradley appeared at Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on Friday, October 23 and was sentenced to one year and eight weeks in prison after pleading guilty to five counts of shop theft and one count of theft. PC Laura D’Urso, of Cambridgeshire Constabulary's spree offender team, said: "Bradley repeatedly stole from businesses across Cambridge, taking more than £1,000 worth of goods in less than two weeks. “Shop theft is not a victimless crime and we know the impact repeated offending can have on businesses and their staff. We will continue to target those who steal from businesses.”

metadata.title: Council-owned developer may not be able to pay back loans
metadata.contentSnippet: This Land, which is owned by Cambridgeshire County Council, could face a shortfall of as much as £7.7m in March 2029, against its loan obligations.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Council-owned developer may not be able to pay back loans
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A council-owned developer has said they may face a multi-million pound cash shortfall as the housing market faces an “economic squeeze”. This Land, which is owned by Cambridgeshire County Council, could face a shortfall of as much as £7.7m in March 2029, against its loan obligations. A report said the company may not be able to pay back the loans and interest it took from the council under the current forecasts. Michael Hudson, the council’s executive director of finance, told a meeting of the shareholder sub-committee this was not an “immediate insolvency event”. He said that “national market factors” were increasing risks of cash shortages for housing developers and other businesses “as the economic squeeze hits harder and harder”. Set up by the county council in 2016 to build homes and sell land to other developers across Cambridgeshire, the company currently owes the council £58m and a further £22.5m in interest. The report said they expect losses of around £2.7m, around £400,000 worse than planned, by the end of the 2026/27 financial year partly driven by delayed sales at Eddeva Park. Approved in 2021, the development just south of Cambridge of up to 230 homes is a mix of detached, terraced and apartments, with 40 per cent marked as affordable. Rob Williams, chief executive officer of This Land, said that “sales are taking a bit longer at the moment” and “things are slow” in both house building and the wider economy. He said: “The planning system is getting slower if anything. “I think the raft of improvements that have come from central government, whilst they are positive, are taking time to embed and for planning authorities to get their heads around.” The report said council officers are working with This Land “to assess options to protect the council’s position and address the 2029 cashflow risk”. These include “close management of the principal receipts, potential rephasing of disposals, management of loan and interest timing and consideration of the company’s future operating model”.

metadata.title: Bar Hill Christmas tree grant approved despite concerns over heatwave maintenance
metadata.contentSnippet: Bar Hill Community Association has been given funding for a permanent Christmas tree – though concerns were raised over its ability to survive a heatwave.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Bar Hill Christmas tree grant approved despite concerns over heatwave maintenance
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. A Cambridgeshire village has been given funding for a permanent Christmas tree – though concerns were raised over its ability to survive a heatwave. Bar Hill Community Association applied to plant the Christmas tree on land owned by the parish council ahead of the lights switch-on scheduled in November. They told South Cambridgeshire District Council that the scheme would be a “long-term community asset” and help “enhance community cohesion”. The report said it would cost a total of £2,807.20 with £1,000 funded by the parish council and asked the district council for a grant to cover the rest. This was broken down into £1,129.20 for the lighting and electricity, £1,278 for the tree and installation, £150 for a banner and £250 for Christmas presents. William Scantlebury, ward councillor for Bar Hill, wrote in support of the application and said it would be a “simple but meaningful addition, helping to bring residents together and add some festive spirit to the heart of Bar Hill”. Cllr Dr Richard Williams, vice chair of South Cambs Council’s grants advisory committee, said it’s “a lovely thing to have” but the costs “jump out a bit”. Cllr Eileen Wilson, of Cottenham, said: “The one thing that came to my mind when I was reading about this was the ongoing maintenance after the heatwaves that we had this summer. “Have they got provisions in place to maintain the tree, to keep it watered if we have a heatwave, because seeing the example of the trees along the A14 that have perished, it does take quite a lot to keep trees going when they have these very big heatwaves.” Emma Dyer, development officer with the communities team, said she’d check the tree management policy but assumes that would be covered. She said: “I think it’s something that they want to keep as an asset so I should imagine they would take a lot of care and look after it.” Cllr Farhan Hussain, of Shelford, said he grew up in Bar Hill and it is “quite an isolated village”. He said: “I think it’s quite a good, community spirit thing to have and I know a lot of villages are isolated at the moment. “Having that in place might actually help out a lot of low disposable income families. You know, things are quite tough at the moment. “I think this is a nice way to do it, but I think it would be very good to just clarify the detailed cost of how they’ve come to that price.” Councillors decided against delaying the application for more details about the pricing as it would mean it wouldn’t be decided until after Christmas. Cllr Williams said: “I think it’s a lovely idea, I really wouldn’t like to delay it and then miss Christmas”. The grant was approved unanimously.

metadata.title: The stunning Cambridgeshire walk with incredible views and riverside tea room
metadata.contentSnippet: The St Ives and Hemingfords Walk in Cambridgeshire is one of the county's best-kept secrets.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: The stunning Cambridgeshire walk with incredible views and riverside tea room
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: For those looking to escape the crowds and discover a quieter side of Cambridgeshire, the St Ives and Hemingfords Walk is one of the county's best-kept secrets. Beginning at Houghton Mill, this picturesque route follows the banks of the River Great Ouse through water meadows and historic villages. The five-mile circular walk is largely flat, making it accessible for most abilities, and offers a constantly changing landscape. Walkers pass through the peaceful Ouse Valley and enjoy long stretches beside the river before reaching the charming villages of Hemingford Grey and Hemingford Abbots. Along the way are postcard-worthy cottages, medieval churches and waterside views that feel a world away from nearby towns and cities. Those with time to spare can visit Holt Island Nature Reserve in St Ives, explore the town's historic centre or stop by the Norris Museum before continuing through the meadows. The route starts and finishes at Houghton Mill, the National Trust's historic working watermill, where visitors will find a gift shop and a popular riverside tea room. Further refreshments can be found in the nearby villages, including traditional pubs that make ideal stopping points on a warm afternoon. What makes this walk so special is its sense of tranquillity. Even during the summer months, there are stretches where the only sounds are birdsong, rustling reeds and the gentle flow of the river. For anyone seeking a hidden riverside route packed with scenery, wildlife and heritage, this walk is certainly a rewarding day out. Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: Channel 4 reveals shocking twist to new £1m game show hosted by Bradley Walsh
metadata.contentSnippet: Bradley Walsh hosts Channel 4’s Million Pound Shot from November 1, where contestants risk their own cash to win £1 million, amid charity criticism.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Channel 4 reveals shocking twist to new £1m game show hosted by Bradley Walsh
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Bradley Walsh is set to host a new game show with a high-stakes twist. Million Pound Shot will launch on Channel 4 on Sunday, November 1, and will see contestants gamble their own money for the chance to win a life-changing sum. The 66-year-old presenter has teased a “big twist” in the format, revealing that players must risk their own cash to compete for the top prize. Mr Walsh said: "This programme is unlike anything we’ve seen on British TV before, and when I heard about this format I thought it was one of the most original and surprising quiz shows I’d ever encountered. "They’re going to have to be willing to take big risks, and back themselves right to the very end. "This is not a game for the faint-hearted." Contestants will bring their own bank cards and bet cash based on how confident they are in their answers to general knowledge questions. Correct answers earn them Bet Balls, which hold a monetary value. Players can either take the money or risk firing the Bet Balls into the Million Pound Shot Machine for a shot at winning £1 million. Mr Walsh said: "This game is all about confidence and bravado. "Putting your money where your mouth is will not be simple when it’s your own cold hard cash. "So the contestants are going to have to be cool, calm, and willing to take a risk. "The game is always in their control." However, the show has drawn criticism from anti-gambling charities. Nick Harvey, a spokesperson for the Coalition to End Gambling Ads (CEGA), said: "This sounds like nothing more than gambling dressed up as a gameshow. "Despite millions being harmed in the UK every year, gambling has become so normalised that someone at a tv channel thought this was a good idea. I just hope that – unlike the gambling industry itself – they’re prioritizing the contestant’s welfare and mental health." Channel 4 has been contacted for a comment. Will you be watching Million Pound Shot? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Major change heading to more than 230 Aldi stores as part of huge investment
metadata.contentSnippet: Aldi will invest £17.5m in installing solar panels at 230 more UK stores between 2027 and 2031.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Major change heading to more than 230 Aldi stores as part of huge investment
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Aldi has announced a multi-million-pound investment in renewable energy. The supermarket chain will spend £17.5 million installing solar panels at 230 additional UK stores between 2027 and 2031. This latest commitment will enable Aldi to generate more of its own renewable electricity, with each installation providing up to 30 per cent of a store’s annual energy needs. Jonathan Neale, managing director of national real estate at Aldi UK, said: "We have plenty of space on our store roofs, so it makes sense to use it. "We want solar power to become a normal part of how we run our stores, and this investment will help us bring it to even more locations over the coming years. "By generating more of our own electricity, we can reduce our reliance on the grid and make our stores more sustainable." The new scheme expands on Aldi’s existing £8.4 million programme to fit solar panels on 100 additional stores during 2025 and 2026. By the end of 2026, more than 500 Aldi stores are expected to have solar panels installed. Mr Neale said: "By generating more of our own electricity, we can reduce our reliance on the grid and make our stores more sustainable." The solar panel programme is part of Aldi’s wider investment in UK stores. Earlier this year, the retailer announced plans to invest more than £300 million in upgrading and extending existing stores in 2026. Nearly 30 new Aldi stores will open across the UK before Christmas. The supermarket chain has revealed the full list of locations opening or relocating over the next 10 weeks. Shoppers in communities across England, Scotland and Wales will see 24 new branches open alongside three site relocations. Do you shop at Aldi? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Sir David Attenborough issues heartfelt message as he thanks the public
metadata.contentSnippet: Sir David Attenborough thanks the public as Wildlife Trusts complete £30m purchase of 9,500-acre Rothbury Estate in Northumberland to support nature recovery.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Sir David Attenborough issues heartfelt message as he thanks the public
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Sir David Attenborough has thanked the public after the successful purchase of a 9,500-acre estate in north-east England. The Rothbury Estate in Northumberland, acquired by The Wildlife Trusts and Northumberland Wildlife Trust following a two-year fundraising campaign and priced at £30 million, marks the largest land purchase in England in decades. Sir David, president emeritus of The Wildlife Trusts, said: "The Wildlife Trusts called for your support and you answered in your thousands. "The appeal to secure the future of the Rothbury Estate in Northumberland has been successful and now the opportunity to bring the vision of a landscape where nature and people thrive side by side can become a reality. "This will be a place where nature, community, farming and heritage can combine to create something very special for generations to come. "Thank you very much." The project will focus on nature-friendly farming, restoring bogs, and enhancing wildlife across the estate. Sir David’s early backing generated more than £1 million in donations within a week. The scheme received around £1.9 million from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, as well as £5 million from the National Lottery Heritage Fund. Public donations totalled £17 million, with contributions from more than 25,000 people across 50 countries. Eilish McGuinness, chief executive at The National Lottery Heritage Fund, said: "By working with local communities to develop new approaches to land management, this transformational project has the potential to deliver nature recovery at a grand scale, helping to reconnect people to the unique natural and cultural heritage of this remarkable and nationally significant landscape." Mike Pratt, chief executive of Northumberland Wildlife Trust, described it as a "remarkable achievement." Mr Pratt said: "The completion of the Rothbury Estate purchase is a defining moment for Northumberland and the North East. "Opportunities of this scale and significance are incredibly rare. "By securing this extraordinary landscape, we’ve the potential to create a flagship for nature recovery supported by sustainable farming, whilst delivering lasting benefits for wildlife, local people and the rural economy for generations to come." Portions of the estate have already been secured, and initial work is under way to survey wildlife, landscapes, and historical features. Sir David has previously praised the estate’s remote beauty, where visitors can explore crags and prehistoric rock art.

metadata.title: Fake beauty products found to contain mercury, lead, nicotine and methanol
metadata.contentSnippet: Counterfeit beauty products seized by Trading Standards contained mercury, lead and methanol, prompting warnings over dangerous fake cosmetics across the UK.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Fake beauty products found to contain mercury, lead, nicotine and methanol
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Counterfeit beauty products containing mercury, lead and methanol are putting consumers at risk, following testing of hauls seized by Trading Standards. The toxic chemicals were found in fake cosmetics, skincare and perfumes seized during recent investigations, with four in 10 seized cosmetics found to contain potentially harmful substances. Among the most alarming discoveries was a skincare product containing 13,200 parts per million of mercury, as well as high levels of lead in lipsticks, eyeshadows and contour products. Nicotine was also found in some counterfeit perfumes, and one fake fragrance was made up of approximately 80 per cent methanol. The Intellectual Property Office has issued warnings. (Image: IPO/Press Association) Rani Ghosh, an independent toxicologist, said: "When you hear that mercury has been found in face cream, lead in make-up or nicotine in perfume, it raises serious questions about what is going into these products and how they are being made. "Some reactions to unsafe cosmetics may be visible, such as irritation, swelling or changes to the skin. "But what concerns me as a toxicologist is what you might not see. "Substances such as mercury and lead can affect the body internally, and those effects may not be immediately obvious. "Counterfeit beauty products can look incredibly convincing. "You cannot tell from the packaging what chemicals are inside, how the product has been made, or what risk it might pose. "That is why knowing where your beauty products come from matters." The Intellectual Property Office’s (IPO) latest Counterfeit Goods Tracker revealed that one in five 18 to 24-year-olds who bought beauty products last year knowingly bought counterfeits, up from six per cent in 2023. In July, the Police Intellectual Property Crime Unit and Greater Manchester Police seized 1,666 counterfeit hair products, including extensions, shampoos and conditioners, from a warehouse in Manchester. A separate raid in Bolton uncovered £2 million worth of fake goods. This included perfume, cosmetics, clothing and vapes. The IPO’s Face the Fakes campaign is working with content creators and the beauty industry to raise awareness of the potential harms of counterfeit beauty products. Helen Barnham, head of enforcement engagement at the IPO, said: "These findings show why counterfeit beauty products can pose such serious risks to consumers. "Products can look remarkably convincing, but behind the packaging they can contain dangerous substances that have no place in the cosmetics people use every day, and can be made in appalling, unhygienic conditions. Counterfeit manufacturing equipment. (Image: IPO/Press Association) "Counterfeiters exploit the names and reputations of brands that consumers know and trust, while bypassing the rigorous safety standards that legitimate businesses work hard to meet. "With our latest research showing a sharp rise in counterfeit beauty buying among young adults, we want to make sure people understand the potential risks and know how to protect themselves. "Our Face the Fakes campaign is giving consumers practical advice to shop more safely, including checking who is actually selling a product and choosing trusted sources." Dr Emma Meredith, director-general of the Cosmetic, Toiletry and Perfumery Association, said: "There is a rigorous safety framework behind every legitimate cosmetic product sold in the UK. "Ingredients are carefully controlled, products have to be made in clean and hygienic conditions, and they must undergo a safety assessment. "Companies have clear legal responsibilities for the products they place on the market."

metadata.title: Ryanair confirms luggage rule change impacting thousands of travellers
metadata.contentSnippet: Ryanair has announced it will be reducing the amount of time passengers will have to drop off their checked luggage at the airport.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Ryanair confirms luggage rule change impacting thousands of travellers
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Ryanair has confirmed it will be making a major change to its luggage rules, and it is set to be enforced next month. The change is expected to affect millions of people who fly with Ryanair. If you are taking a trip soon and are flying with Ryanair, it is worth keeping up to date with the airline’s policies to avoid being caught out at the airport. Ryanair has confirmed it will be changing its rules around airport check-ins and bag drops. From November 10, the airline will be giving passengers less time to drop off their luggage before their flight. The new rule means Ryanair will close all of its airport bag drop desks and physical check-in counters 60 minutes before the flight’s departure time. Previously, the airline allowed passengers to drop off their luggage up to 40 minutes before their flight. The change is hoped to give passengers more time to clear airport queues, such as security checks and passport control queues, before their flights. The airline has said the extra 20 minutes will help to run operations more smoothly. Ryanair has said the change should help reduce the number of travellers who miss their flights because of delays at the airport. The rule impacts anyone with checked luggage or those who require physical check-in assistance at the airport. If you have either a 10kg or 20kg checked bag, you must make sure it has gone through the bag drop at least an hour before your scheduled flight time. Ryanair CMO, Dara Brady, said: “From Tues, 10 Nov, bag drop services at all Ryanair airports will close 60 minutes before scheduled departure, instead of the current 40 minutes. “This small change will give the 20% of Ryanair passengers who check in a bag, more time to clear airport security and passport control queues and get to their departure gate before boarding begins, particularly during busy travel periods when airport queues can be longer. Recommended reading “We remind passengers using airport bag drop services to arrive at the airport in good time and ensure they have checked in and dropped their bags before check-in and bag drop closes 60 minutes before departure. “The remaining 80% of passengers who check in online and do not check in a bag are unaffected by this change.” Do you think Ryanair’s rule change will make travelling easier? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Disabled Huntingdonshire tenant raises asbestos fears over deteriorating floor
metadata.contentSnippet: A disabled tenant fears his Needingworth home is unsafe because its asbestos-containing floor is deteriorating, but his housing association, Places for People, says a survey found it poses a “very low risk”.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Disabled Huntingdonshire tenant raises asbestos fears over deteriorating floor
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A disabled tenant fears his Huntingdonshire home is unsafe because its asbestos-containing floor is deteriorating, but his housing association says a survey found it poses a “very low risk”. Michael Cook moved into the Places for People property in Chapel Close, Needingworth, in June, and says the bitumen floor should have been sealed and covered first. He says the bitumen is now breaking up and becoming sticky in places, with residue transferring onto his belongings, clothes and the paws of his dog, Spike. Places for People tenant Michael Cook says flooring in his flat contains asbestos and is a health risk, however the landlords say surveys show it is 'low risk'. (Image: Michael Cook) Places for People disputes claims that the deterioration poses an asbestos risk. A Places for People spokesperson said: “We take concerns about the safety and condition of our customers’ homes seriously, and we’re sorry for the worry and frustration Mr Cook has experienced. “Our survey confirmed the presence of asbestos in the adhesive beneath the floor, but it is encapsulated and very low risk, with no evidence of fibres being released into the home. Places for People tenant Michael Cook says flooring in his flat contains asbestos and is a health risk, however the landlords say surveys show it is 'low risk'. (Image: Michael Cook) “The surveys identified no risk requiring emergency action, and there is no requirement to stop vacuuming, sweeping or mopping, or to avoid laying laminate flooring.” Mr Cook and his advocate, his mum Ilya Kennard, say surveys carried out in 2026 found chrysotile asbestos in the bitumen adhesive beneath floors in several rooms. Mr Cook says the deteriorating floor has left the material inadequately protected and should have been sealed and covered before he moved in. Places for People tenant Michael Cook says flooring in his flat contains asbestos and is a health risk, however the landlords say surveys show it is 'low risk'. (Image: Michael Cook) Mr Cook has also reported plumbing and drainage problems, including flooding in the wet room. Mr Cook also says he was told not to vacuum, sweep or mop the affected floor because it could be disturbed. Places for People disputes this and says its surveys found no need for such restrictions. Concerns have also been raised about how the case was handled and communicated to Mr Cook, who is disabled and takes morphine and pregabalin for a broken back. Places for People acknowledged shortcomings in its communication with Mr Cook and his advocate and said work would now be undertaken at the property. The spokesperson added: “While the reported deterioration of the floor is not causing asbestos fibres to become airborne, we have assessed the property and are laying new flooring throughout. “There were, however, shortcomings in our communication with Mr Cook and his appointed advocate. “We apologise for the stress this may have caused and will ensure appropriate support is in place in future.”

metadata.title: Hunts council leader slams latest 'deeply disappointing' LGR delay
metadata.contentSnippet: Huntingdonshire District Council's executive leader, Cllr Sarah Conboy, has slammed the latest update on Local Government Reorganisation, calling it "deeply disappointing".

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hunts council leader slams latest 'deeply disappointing' LGR delay
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A council leader has slammed the latest government update on Local Government Reorganisation, calling the lack of action "deeply disappointing". Sarah Conboy, leader of Huntingdonshire District Council, criticised the update, which confirmed that no final decision had been made on Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. LGR would see the two tier system of county and district councils in Cambridgeshire replaced with a number of unitary authorities across the county. An announcement on the form this would take was expected in July, but the Secretary of State for Local Government at the time, Steve Reed, delayed the decision until October. On October 29, Jim McMahon MP, Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Local Government, Devolution and Regional Growth, announced in Parliament that only five of the 14 areas under review would be proceeding. Cambridgeshire and Peterborough was not included in the five. Cllr Conboy said: "Today's announcement is deeply disappointing for Huntingdonshire and the wider Cambridgeshire and Peterborough area. "After months of work developing and assessing proposals, we had hoped the Government would provide certainty about the future of local government in our area. "Instead, residents, businesses and councils are being asked to wait longer for a decision. "We will continue to work constructively with our partners while seeking greater clarity from Government on the next steps and timescales." The Government says it expects to make a final decision by early next year. In the meantime, HDC will continue to work with regional partners to assess the implications of the announcement and plan for the next phase of the LGR programme. The council confirmed there will be no immediate changes to council services, which will continue to be delivered as normal while councils await further details. The Government said all options would remain under consideration, with a further update due by Christmas and outcomes for every area expected early next year.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Plans have been submitted to create a new residential traveller site for a family near Ramsey. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. Applicant Christopher Reilly is seeking permission for the development to provide a permanent home for his family, who are members of the Gypsy and Traveller community. A statement accompanying the plans says: "Mr Reilly and his family are looking for a settled environment with a permanent base to call home." It adds that having a fixed address would help the family access schooling, medical services and other local amenities. The supporting statement says there are already a number of similar developments in the area and claims the proposed design and layout would be in keeping with its surroundings. The application describes the 0.15-hectare site as currently vacant and "derelict ground". Documents submitted with the plans indicate that the proposed day room would be constructed using red facing brick with smooth grey concrete roof tiles. Post-and-rail timber fencing is proposed around the site, while the hardstanding would have a permeable surface. The applicant has stated that there are no trees or hedges on the development site or neighbouring land which could influence the scheme. The application also indicates that no new or altered vehicle or pedestrian access from the public highway is proposed. It is claimed the development would not increase flood risk elsewhere, while the application form indicates surface water would be dealt with through a sustainable drainage system. The applicant argues that the usual Biodiversity Net Gain condition would not apply because the development involves an existing hard-surfaced area of less than 0.2 hectares. The plans will now be considered by Huntingdonshire District Council before a decision is made. In March 2026, Huntingdonshire District Council approved eight retrospective traveller-site applications in Ramsey Heights, after officers said a district-wide survey found insufficient authorised pitches to meet demand.

metadata.title: We visited Cambs garden centre’s new pottery studio - here's what we thought
metadata.contentSnippet: Nestled into Huntingdon Home & Garden’s spacious restaurant area is its newest attraction – The Potting Shed Studio.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: We visited Cambs garden centre’s new pottery studio - here's what we thought
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Nestled into Huntingdon Home & Garden’s spacious restaurant area is its newest attraction – The Potting Shed Studio. Immediately after walking through its doors, the sage green interior decor gives an instant feeling of calmness. It really is a place to unwind and let your imagination takeover. The staff – a small team led by studio manager Sophie – are equally as welcoming, leading us to the well-stocked display. It can be tricky deciding what to paint due to the vast selection, but don’t worry as they have every age covered. From cute little animals to small plates, platter plates, jugs and photo frames, the £1 booking fee per person is redeemable against the price of your pottery. Though it’s not quite as well equipped as some of the longer established pottery studios – for example Center Parcs – this can be forgiven as the studio only opened its doors in late March. Nonetheless, we as a family loved our experience; our two young children had great fun mixing the different squeeze paints together in their palette and getting creative. It’s worth noting, however, that they were not provided with or offered aprons, but we have been assured that the paint comes off very easily in the wash. Something else to bear in mind is that the turnaround is up to two weeks, so you will have to make a return visit for collection — though this isn’t really a problem as Blue Diamond has its customers covered. The Potting Shed Studio has been open for around two weeks (Image: Ben Jolley/Newsquest) Visitors can get topped up on your fresh fruit and veg, browse the clothing range, enjoy a cuppa and a slice of cake, and even refresh your fish tank by popping into Maidenhead Aquatics. Overall, The Potting Shed Studio is a great addition not only to the garden centre – which gave out a complimentary glass of bubbly upon entry to celebrate one year of being open – but for the wider Cambridgeshire area. Alongside being great for families, it would make for a quirky few hours out to get the girls together or even for part of a date day. And, with plans to run exciting events in the future, make sure to keep your eyes peeled on their socials.

metadata.title: Why Hamerton Zoo Park is one of Cambridgeshire’s best attractions
metadata.contentSnippet: Here’s why Hamerton Zoo Park near Sawtry is one of Cambridgeshire’s best attractions.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Why Hamerton Zoo Park is one of Cambridgeshire’s best attractions
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: When it comes to a day out at the zoo, the UK’s biggest are likely the first ones that spring to mind. But, much closer to home, there’s a more local alternative that’s equally worth visiting: Hamerton, near Sawtry, between Huntingdonshire and Peterborough. What began its life as a private collection when it first opened its doors to the public in June 1990, has since grown into a park that is home to many rare and unusual animals. Fast forward 35 years, and not only has the number of distinct breeds massively increased, the entrance area has had a makeover and there’s a brilliant new park (Treetop Adventure Play) that has just as much to occupy children as it does adults. Tree Tops Adventure Play(Image: Newsquest) This includes an obstacle course in the sky that’s connected with ladders and ropes, a great zipwire, plenty of slides and a disorienting Rubix cube-like climbing puzzle that’s sure to challenge parents. Onto the zoo’s main attraction, and there are countless stunning animals to see and learn about: from cute common marmosets that would fit in the palm of your hand to swinging lemurs, to tiny dik-dik deers, hopping white wallabys and adorable lettuce-munching tortoises of all sizes. Though acclimatised to living in dark, the sloths are equally mesmerising to watch, clinging to branches and ropes while somehow managing to eat upside down. It’s entrancing to witness them move along at such a slow pace, especially in such close proximity. The same can be said for the reptile and rodent house, which has all manner of rare lizards and snakes. It’s worth noting that all the enclosures are incredibly well kept and presented, especially in the bird area (a highlight of which is the strikingly colourful Scarlet Ibis). The flamingos(Image: Newsquest) The meerkat enclosure, meanwhile, has had an upgrade with two new bubble head viewing platforms that provide a great photo opportunity - little ones are sure to want to go through the tunnel on repeat, and they may even be able to snap a selfie with a meerkat. A word of warning, though: it might be a bit tiring for adults - especially those who are taller. As if all that isn’t enough, there are also swimming otters, miniature donkeys, zebra, massive camels, several tigers and, if you’re lucky like we were, one or more of the Syrian Brown Bear family might pop out to say hello. The animal-spotting doesn’t stop there, though, as even while enjoying a tasty panini and delicious cake, there are opportunities to spot some impressive aquatic species. The viewing platforms inside the meerkat enclosure(Image: Newsquest) With all this and more for an affordable price - £19.99 an adult, £15.99 a child, free for under threes and carers - it’s a great value experience. Undoubtedly one of Cambridgeshire’s best attractions, you can easily spend the whole day at Hamerton Zoo Park, and its annual pass option makes for a perfect family gift that’s guaranteed to create lots of special memories. To book, visit https://hamertonzoopark.com

metadata.title: We visited bird sanctuary in Cambridgeshire and here’s what we thought
metadata.contentSnippet: Here's why you should visit The Raptor Foundation in Woodhurst, Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: We visited bird sanctuary in Cambridgeshire and here’s what we thought
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Ben Jolley reports back from a visit to The Raptor Foundation in Woodhurst, Cambridgeshire It’s more important than ever to support local attractions - especially ones that are making a real difference. A registered charity for over 30 years and situated at its current site for the same amount of time, visiting The Raptor Foundation is not only fun for all ages but you'll be supporting a crucial cause too. Having started its life in Ramsey St Mary, before moving to its current, bigger premises in the late 1990s, the sanctuary is home to around 170 birds of prey, including between 35 and 40 different species. The Buzzard Lawn (Image: Newsquest) As the majority of these have come from a rescue background, money spent (entry is very affordable at £8 for adults, £5 for children and free for under threes) goes towards rescuing, rehabilitating and then returning native birds of prey back to the wild. Open to the public all year round, and currently appealing for builders to help create new aviaries, time spent at the foundation is both exciting and educational. The bird of prey displays - which feature rare owls and falcons soaring overhead - are thrilling to watch. If you’re lucky, some may even decide to perch on the seat next to you, which takes the phrase up close and personal to a whole new level. Action from the bird of prey display (Image: Newsquest) Having trained the birds inside out, the keepers and handlers are incredibly knowledgeable, informative and able to answer any question posed to them. This extends to the talks and feeding sessions throughout the day which offer further meet and greet opportunities; a parrot might even land on your shoulders. It’s not just birds, however, as the reptile house is home to a gigantic tortoise (and many smaller ones), as well as lizards and snakes. Beyond animals, there is also a play area and pond that will amuse younger children and a tearoom serving food and drink. The foundation also runs experience days which, ranging from one-to-one handling to junior keeper days, would make for a perfect Christmas present. It also hosts photography tours and is an ideal venue for birthday parties. As if that wasn't enough, there is also the option to stay overnight, at either the Falcons Nest guest accommodation or the caravan site. Whilst we didn’t spend the whole day at The Raptor Foundation (largely due to the weather), there's no question that it is one of Cambridgeshire's most treasured gems.

metadata.title: Jailed in October for crimes including sexual assault and child abuse images
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire offenders jailed for sexual assault, drink-driving, false imprisonment, burglary and child abuse image offences in Cambridge and Peterborough courts.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Jailed in October for crimes including sexual assault and child abuse images
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: These are some of the offenders sentenced by courts in and around Cambridgeshire for crimes including violent assault, dangerous driving, burglary and child abuse image offences. Bradley Warby, 41, of Caldecote Close, Peterborough, followed a 16-year-old girl through King’s Cross railway station before targeting her again on a train to Peterborough. Warby sat next to the teenager, made sexual comments towards her and repeatedly sexually assaulted her. A concerned passenger reported the incident to British Transport Police, and detectives later identified Warby through CCTV. He pleaded guilty to three counts of sexual assault and was jailed for one year and two months at Cambridge Crown Court on October 5. Samiul Islam, 25, of Pipe Lane, Peterborough, was driving at speed along the A1307 in Huntingdon when he crashed into a stationary Mercedes in August 2024. The Mercedes driver was paralysed and one of Islam’s passengers suffered a fractured spine and collarbone. Islam’s roadside breath test measured 42 microgrammes of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath, above the legal limit of 35. The collision forced the Mercedes almost 30 metres down the road, despite its handbrake being on, and Islam was banned from driving for five years and 10 months. He was jailed for two years and six months at Peterborough Crown Court on October 2. Zoe Smith and Shane Rowe, both 39, barricaded a man with mobility problems inside his Cambridge flat for more than 12 hours. They blocked the door with a table, repeatedly punched him in the face and stopped him leaving before he escaped for help. Both were convicted of false imprisonment and theft after a trial, while Rowe was also convicted of assault by beating. The pair took the victim’s wallet and phone, and he told police he lived in fear of them. Rowe was jailed for eight years and Smith for five at Cambridge Crown Court on October 9. Both were given indefinite restraining orders banning contact with the victim. Anthony Lamb, 51, of Church Street, Gamlingay, smashed up his ex-partner's home in Histon and attempted to attack her with a hammer. She escaped to a neighbour’s home and called police. Officers found a fire burning near her front door. Lamb admitted two counts of criminal damage and breaching a restraining order. He was jailed for three years and six months at Peterborough Crown Court on October 1. Richard Kemp, 57, of no fixed abode but from the Huntingdon area, sexually assaulted a woman who had gone to check on his welfare in May 2023. Kemp, who was drunk, became verbally abusive before attacking the woman as she tried to leave. He was convicted following a trial of two counts of assault by penetration. He was jailed for five years at Peterborough Crown Court on October 8 and placed on the sex offenders’ register. Jack Wilmot, 29, of no fixed address, admitted a series of burglaries, thefts and assaults committed across Cambridge during a two-week crime spree. He targeted shops, stealing cigarettes, alcohol, perfume and meat, and assaulted staff twice. He also broke into Dorringtons Bakery, stealing a charity box, and Milton Road Pharmacy. He was jailed for one year at Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on October 2. Aaron Strachan, 26, of Robertson Way, Sapley, Huntingdon, was found with 17,147 indecent images of children on his phone after a police investigation. The children’s gymnastics coach initially denied knowing about the material but pleaded guilty on the day of his trial to making three indecent images of children and distributing one indecent image or video. He was jailed for three years and four months at Cambridge Crown Court on October 16.

metadata.title: Sir David Attenborough issues heartfelt message as he thanks the public
metadata.contentSnippet: Sir David Attenborough thanks the public as Wildlife Trusts complete £30m purchase of 9,500-acre Rothbury Estate in Northumberland to support nature recovery.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Sir David Attenborough issues heartfelt message as he thanks the public
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Sir David Attenborough has thanked the public after the successful purchase of a 9,500-acre estate in north-east England. The Rothbury Estate in Northumberland, acquired by The Wildlife Trusts and Northumberland Wildlife Trust following a two-year fundraising campaign and priced at £30 million, marks the largest land purchase in England in decades. Sir David, president emeritus of The Wildlife Trusts, said: "The Wildlife Trusts called for your support and you answered in your thousands. "The appeal to secure the future of the Rothbury Estate in Northumberland has been successful and now the opportunity to bring the vision of a landscape where nature and people thrive side by side can become a reality. "This will be a place where nature, community, farming and heritage can combine to create something very special for generations to come. "Thank you very much." The project will focus on nature-friendly farming, restoring bogs, and enhancing wildlife across the estate. Sir David’s early backing generated more than £1 million in donations within a week. The scheme received around £1.9 million from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, as well as £5 million from the National Lottery Heritage Fund. Public donations totalled £17 million, with contributions from more than 25,000 people across 50 countries. Eilish McGuinness, chief executive at The National Lottery Heritage Fund, said: "By working with local communities to develop new approaches to land management, this transformational project has the potential to deliver nature recovery at a grand scale, helping to reconnect people to the unique natural and cultural heritage of this remarkable and nationally significant landscape." Mike Pratt, chief executive of Northumberland Wildlife Trust, described it as a "remarkable achievement." Mr Pratt said: "The completion of the Rothbury Estate purchase is a defining moment for Northumberland and the North East. "Opportunities of this scale and significance are incredibly rare. "By securing this extraordinary landscape, we’ve the potential to create a flagship for nature recovery supported by sustainable farming, whilst delivering lasting benefits for wildlife, local people and the rural economy for generations to come." Portions of the estate have already been secured, and initial work is under way to survey wildlife, landscapes, and historical features. Sir David has previously praised the estate’s remote beauty, where visitors can explore crags and prehistoric rock art.

metadata.title: Fake beauty products found to contain mercury, lead, nicotine and methanol
metadata.contentSnippet: Counterfeit beauty products seized by Trading Standards contained mercury, lead and methanol, prompting warnings over dangerous fake cosmetics across the UK.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Fake beauty products found to contain mercury, lead, nicotine and methanol
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Counterfeit beauty products containing mercury, lead and methanol are putting consumers at risk, following testing of hauls seized by Trading Standards. The toxic chemicals were found in fake cosmetics, skincare and perfumes seized during recent investigations, with four in 10 seized cosmetics found to contain potentially harmful substances. Among the most alarming discoveries was a skincare product containing 13,200 parts per million of mercury, as well as high levels of lead in lipsticks, eyeshadows and contour products. Nicotine was also found in some counterfeit perfumes, and one fake fragrance was made up of approximately 80 per cent methanol. The Intellectual Property Office has issued warnings. (Image: IPO/Press Association) Rani Ghosh, an independent toxicologist, said: "When you hear that mercury has been found in face cream, lead in make-up or nicotine in perfume, it raises serious questions about what is going into these products and how they are being made. "Some reactions to unsafe cosmetics may be visible, such as irritation, swelling or changes to the skin. "But what concerns me as a toxicologist is what you might not see. "Substances such as mercury and lead can affect the body internally, and those effects may not be immediately obvious. "Counterfeit beauty products can look incredibly convincing. "You cannot tell from the packaging what chemicals are inside, how the product has been made, or what risk it might pose. "That is why knowing where your beauty products come from matters." The Intellectual Property Office’s (IPO) latest Counterfeit Goods Tracker revealed that one in five 18 to 24-year-olds who bought beauty products last year knowingly bought counterfeits, up from six per cent in 2023. In July, the Police Intellectual Property Crime Unit and Greater Manchester Police seized 1,666 counterfeit hair products, including extensions, shampoos and conditioners, from a warehouse in Manchester. A separate raid in Bolton uncovered £2 million worth of fake goods. This included perfume, cosmetics, clothing and vapes. The IPO’s Face the Fakes campaign is working with content creators and the beauty industry to raise awareness of the potential harms of counterfeit beauty products. Helen Barnham, head of enforcement engagement at the IPO, said: "These findings show why counterfeit beauty products can pose such serious risks to consumers. "Products can look remarkably convincing, but behind the packaging they can contain dangerous substances that have no place in the cosmetics people use every day, and can be made in appalling, unhygienic conditions. Counterfeit manufacturing equipment. (Image: IPO/Press Association) "Counterfeiters exploit the names and reputations of brands that consumers know and trust, while bypassing the rigorous safety standards that legitimate businesses work hard to meet. "With our latest research showing a sharp rise in counterfeit beauty buying among young adults, we want to make sure people understand the potential risks and know how to protect themselves. "Our Face the Fakes campaign is giving consumers practical advice to shop more safely, including checking who is actually selling a product and choosing trusted sources." Dr Emma Meredith, director-general of the Cosmetic, Toiletry and Perfumery Association, said: "There is a rigorous safety framework behind every legitimate cosmetic product sold in the UK. "Ingredients are carefully controlled, products have to be made in clean and hygienic conditions, and they must undergo a safety assessment. "Companies have clear legal responsibilities for the products they place on the market."

metadata.title: New DWP bank checks begin for people claiming three benefits
metadata.contentSnippet: New DWP bank checks begin for people claiming three benefits have begun as part of a major crackdown on fraud and error.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: New DWP bank checks begin for people claiming three benefits
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: New bank checks targeting people claiming three benefits have begun as part of a major Department for Work and Pensions crackdown on fraud and error. The DWP has issued its first Eligibility Verification Notice, requiring banks and other financial institutions to check information relating to some benefit-receiving accounts. The new system can be used in relation to Universal Credit, Pension Credit and Employment and Support Allowance (ESA). It is designed to identify cases where someone may have savings which affect their entitlement or has remained abroad for longer than benefit rules allow. However, the DWP has stressed that the powers do not give officials access to people's bank accounts, transactions or information about their spending habits. Instead, financial institutions will be asked to check relevant benefit-receiving accounts against specified eligibility rules and flag cases where further investigation could be required. A flag will not itself mean somebody has committed benefit fraud or done anything wrong. The Government also says no decision about a person's benefit entitlement can be made solely using information provided through the new system. Undeclared savings and the amount of time claimants spend outside the country are two of the areas the Government hopes the checks will help identify. The DWP estimates fraud and error involving undeclared savings and time spent abroad in relation to Universal Credit and Pension Credit cost taxpayers £1.5 billion in 2025-26. The Eligibility Verification Measure is expected to generate £1.2 billion in savings by 2030-31. Minister for Innovation, Fraud and Debt Lilian Greenwood said: “Benefit fraudsters should be looking over their shoulder. These new powers will help us crack down on those who deliberately abuse the system, while ensuring people receive the right support at the right time. “We are not interested in where people do their weekly shop or how much they’re spending on new clothes. Banks will simply be asked to identify if somebody may no longer meet the rules for the benefits they receive, allowing us to investigate further where necessary. “With £1.2 billion in savings expected by 2030/31, this is a major step forward in tackling fraud and error, protecting public money and ensuring support goes to those who genuinely need it.” Being flagged through the system will not automatically result in someone's benefits being stopped. The DWP says a flag does not establish fraud or wrongdoing and further enquiries would have to be made. The measure is initially being introduced through a "test-and-learn" phase and will be subject to independent oversight before any wider rollout. The powers were introduced through the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 and form part of the Government's wider efforts to reduce fraud and incorrect benefit payments. Further measures are also planned, including 2,000 additional anti-fraud specialists being deployed to Jobcentres and tougher checks involving Universal Credit claims from people who have gone abroad. The Government says its broader package of measures is intended to save taxpayers £14.6 billion over the next five years.

metadata.title: Care home resident returns to drums after 60 years for private jam session
metadata.contentSnippet: A care home resident in St Ives has rediscovered his rhythm with a long-awaited return to the drums.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Care home resident returns to drums after 60 years for private jam session
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A care home resident in St Ives has rediscovered his rhythm with a long-awaited return to the drums. Robert McPhee, 79, who lives at Care UK’s Field Lodge on London Road, hadn’t played in more than 60 years but recently told staff he’d love the chance to play again and relive his rock ’n’ roll youth. In his teens, he was a drummer in a band that practised every Sunday in a room above the bus station in Whitley Bay. Robert said: "I can’t believe it’s been over 60 years since I dusted off the drumsticks. "It brought back fun memories of playing in the band." To help him reconnect with his musical past, the Field Lodge team arranged a private jam session with a local drummer named Alex. The experience was organised through the care home's Wishing Tree initiative, which encourages residents to share personal wishes—whether it’s revisiting a favourite hobby or trying something new. Linda Martinez, home manager at Field Lodge, said: "When Robert expressed a desire to play the drums again, we were eager to help make it happen. "Our Wishing Tree initiative is a wonderful way for residents to share their ambitions and it’s hugely rewarding to be able to make these a reality. "Robert clearly enjoyed playing again, and it was lovely to see him rekindle his passion—he hasn’t lost his sense of rhythm." She extended her thanks to those who helped bring Mr McPhee’s wish to life. Linda said: "I’d like to say a big thank you to everyone who helped us to make Robert’s wish come true and proved that the rock ’n’ roll spirit belongs to all ages."
