metadata.title: Home Bargains hot water bottle warning after customer's horror burns
metadata.contentSnippet: Megan Shannon describes surgery after a hot water bottle bought at Home Bargains spilled on her

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Home Bargains hot water bottle warning after customer's horror burns
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A woman needed surgery after a hot water bottle spilled on her. Megan Shannon said she suffered first- and second-degree burns when the long bottle she bought from Home Bargains leaked in June 2025. She said she had wrapped the £7.99 Home Collections bottle around her waist to ease period pains and heard a pop after about 10 minutes. She said: "I just heard a pop, and felt the hot water trickle down my stomach, my legs, my thighs, my pelvis." Megan said the water was boiling hot and ran down her legs when she stood up. Megan was rushed to Whiston Hospital in Prescot, Merseyside (Image: Kennedy News/@meg.shann) Her boyfriend called an ambulance while she used cold water in the shower to cool her burns. She said: "It's the worst physical pain I've ever been in, it's like having my skin unpeeled multiple times in the same area." Megan, from Liverpool, was taken to Whiston Hospital in Prescot, where she said a team of plastic surgeons, doctors and nurses assessed her injuries. Megan said her groin, upper thighs and lower abdomen had first- and second-degree burns. Three days after the incident, she underwent a treatment called Recell, which she described as a skin graft treatment. She said: "It was petrifying. I had to have surgery, a treatment called Recell, it's a skin graft treatment. They take skin from somewhere in my body and spray it back on to me." Megan said doctors treated blisters and it took weeks before she could walk comfortably. She said: "To be comfortable walking it took weeks and because of the area I wasn't even able to wear underwear. My mental health went so down after that." She said the burns had mostly healed but marks remained and had left her feeling self-conscious. Megan said she would not use a hot water bottle again, adding that doctors had recommended a microwaveable wheat bag to her. Home Bargains said it was sorry to hear about her experience and encouraged her to get in touch so it could look into the incident. A spokesperson said: "We take the safety of our customers extremely seriously, which is why all our hot water bottles are stringently tested to ensure they meet the relevant safety standards and are labelled with appropriate safety warnings." The spokesperson added: "Hot water bottles can pose a risk of burns if they are not cared for or used correctly, which is why it is important that customers follow the safety instructions provided." NHS Scotland advises people not to use boiling water when filling a hot water bottle, and to let the water cool for a few minutes first. It also recommends filling the bottle no more than two-thirds full, carefully squeezing out the air and using a cover to protect the skin. The NHS says burns and scalds should be held under cool running water for 20 minutes as soon as possible, within three hours of the injury. It advises calling 999 or going to A&E for a very large or deep burn, or one affecting the face, genitals or bottom.

metadata.title: JD Wetherspoon customers banned from wearing this item in all 800 UK pubs
metadata.contentSnippet: Meta Glasses (and other smart glasses) are now banned from all JD Wetherspoon pubs in the UK.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: JD Wetherspoon customers banned from wearing this item in all 800 UK pubs
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Meta Glasses are now banned at all JD Wetherspoon venues across the UK. Customers can no longer wear Meta glasses, or any other smart glasses, at any of its more than 800 pubs. The devices, which can record video, photos and audio, have raised privacy concerns due to their ability to film without drawing attention. The ban, announced in August, follows growing reports of people secretly recording strangers and sharing footage online. A JD Wetherspoon spokesperson, explaining the ban, said: "Like many hospitality companies, Wetherspoon has CCTV cameras for security reasons, but their use is strictly controlled by data legislation. "Apart from that, the general code that applies in our pubs, and most pubs, is that you can’t film customers or employees without their permission. "Meta glasses seem to breach this code, and common sense, by enabling surreptitious surveillance, so our instinct is to say turn off the cameras. "This is akin to our efforts to stop audible playing of videos in our pubs, which also invades people’s space." Meta reassured people that their glasses have a light that turns on to let people know when a photo or video is being taken. A spokesperson for the company added: "People use our glasses because they're helpful and help them stay in the moment, from listening to music to live translation or hands-free calls. "They also provide critical new technology for people who are low-sighted or hard of hearing and limiting how people can use this technology would be a major step backwards. "Naturally some places shouldn't be filmed at all and that's reasonable but rules should be applied consistently." Around 88% of Wetherspoon customers agree with the Meta Glasses ban. (Image: Patrick Glover) We asked readers whether they agreed with the Meta Glasses ban in Wetherspoon pubs, with 88% (4243 people) saying 'yes'. Around 9% (441) of people didn't agree with the ban, while 3% (141) said they weren't sure. Wetherspoon also recently banned customers from playing music out loud or taking calls on speaker at its UK pubs. While Meta Glasses, playing music out loud, and taking calls on speaker are all banned at Wetherspoon venues across the UK, poppies are not. The confirmation comes after customers at The Star, a JD Wetherspoon pub in Gosport, were denied entry on Sunday (October 25) for wearing poppies. The incident occurred during a day of demonstrations in the town, and among those turned away were veterans and members of the public, including Reform UK councillor George Madgwick. Cllr Madgwick said they were denied entry after door staff told them wearing poppies breached company policy. JD Wetherspoon has confirmed that poppies are not banned in its UK pubs. (Image: Getty Images) JD Wetherspoon has since insisted there is "no ban on poppies" in its pubs and apologised for the incident. A Wetherspoon spokesperson said: "Wetherspoon has been a long-standing supporter of the Royal British Legion Poppy Appeal, with poppies for sale in our pubs, including the Star. "There is no ban on poppies in Wetherspoon pubs. "However, there were some standard security measures in place today, as a result of demonstrations in the town. "Unfortunately, some members of the public, including some wearing poppies, did not gain entry to the pub. "The pub closed to all customers, on advice of the police, at 5pm and remains closed today. "We apologise to any regular customers who have been inconvenienced by today’s events and look to forward to welcoming everyone back tomorrow." Do you agree with the new Meta Glasses ban at Wetherspoon pubs? Let us know in the poll above or in the comments below.

metadata.title: Budget 2026 what to expect from John Healey as Chancellor prepares major announcement
metadata.contentSnippet: John Healey will deliver his first Budget as Chancellor today, October 28, with households and businesses waiting to see whether he will announce further help with the cost of living.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Budget 2026 what to expect from John Healey as Chancellor prepares major announcement
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: John Healey will deliver his first Budget as Chancellor today, October 28, with households and businesses waiting to see whether he will announce further help with the cost of living. Andy Burnham's Chancellor faces a difficult economic backdrop, with pressure on public finances compounded by higher borrowing costs linked to turmoil in international markets following the Iran war. Ministers have already unveiled a series of measures aimed at easing everyday costs, including changes to Carers’ Allowance, mileage payments and food tariffs. Further announcements are expected on energy bills, fuel duty, wages and public spending. But with the Government facing tight financial constraints, the Chancellor will also have to balance support for households against his commitment to meeting the fiscal rules. Here is what to expect from the Budget 2026, including the measures already announced and the policies reportedly under consideration. There's been much debate about how the state pension and personal allowance issue will be resolved, and given that the state pension is tipped to rise above the income tax threshold in April, today is likely to be the day that's finally sorted. In a post on social media, Martin Lewis highlighted that the full new State Pension is expected to rise to around £13,040 a year from April 2027, while the Income Tax personal allowance remains frozen at £12,570. Martin pointed out that John Healey has said the Government will honour former Chancellor Rachel Reeves' promise that pensioners whose only income is the State Pension will not pay Income Tax. He questioned whether that protection could create a cliff edge for those with even a small amount of extra income. “An important question for @JohnHealey_MP,” Martin wrote. He continued: “So the full new State Pension would normally attract tax. Yet you've said you'll honour former Chancellor Rachel Reeves' promise that those whose ONLY income is the State Pension won't pay tax. But will that be a cliff edge?” Of course, many would like to see the HMRC Personal Allowance increase for everyone. As Alex Beavis, Interim Director of Banking at LHV Bank, says, it's particularly key for savers. He's calling on the Chancellor to raise the allowance: "The biggest tax rise facing savers won't make the Budget headlines. It's already happening to your hard-earned cash, year after year. "The Personal Savings Allowance hasn't moved since 2016. With savings tax rates due to rise by two percentage points from April, more people will be taxed twice on the same money." Measures to ease pressure on household budgets are expected to feature prominently in the Budget. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has asked the Chancellor and Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh to examine whether standing charges on gas bills could be scrapped. Ministers are also looking at whether to break the link between wholesale gas prices and electricity bills, despite gas accounting for only a proportion of total electricity generation. Fuel duty is another key issue for motorists. Mr Healey is expected to cancel a planned January increase, keeping fuel duty frozen at 52p per litre for a 16th consecutive year. The reported move follows concerns about rising petrol and diesel prices and the impact of the Iran war. These include: The Prime Minister has said further measures will be announced on Wednesday to give families and businesses more “breathing space”. The Chancellor is expected to announce an increase in the minimum wage. The national living wage is set to rise by nearly 4%, from £12.71 to £13.20 an hour. The reported plans would also end the trend of increasing the minimum wage for workers aged 18 to 20 by a larger percentage than the rate for older workers. Instead, the younger age group's minimum wage would rise at roughly the same rate as the national living wage, according to the report. The details remain subject to confirmation in the Budget. The Treasury estimates that reducing paperwork and other administrative requirements could save businesses around £800million. The proposals form part of efforts to reduce the burden on firms and support economic growth. Mr Healey has ruled out increasing capital gains tax in the Budget. The tax is charged on profits made when people sell certain assets, such as shares or second homes. Some Labour figures have called for capital gains tax rates to be brought closer to those applied to earnings, but the Chancellor has rejected a rise. A potential increase in the tax surcharge on banks is reportedly under consideration. The surcharge, currently set at 3%, could rise to 8%, reversing a reduction introduced by former chancellor Jeremy Hunt. The Trades Union Congress, which supports the proposal, said the increase could raise £2.25billion a year from banks' “bumper profits”. However, representatives of the financial sector have warned that a higher tax could discourage investment in Britain. It remains to be seen whether the Chancellor will include the proposal in his Budget. Mr Healey has promised to fill a £4.7billion shortfall in Britain's defence investment plan. The plan, one of Sir Keir Starmer's final major announcements as prime minister, promised an additional £15billion for the UK defence sector but allocated only £10.3billion, leaving the Chancellor to find the remaining funding. The additional spending would help raise defence expenditure to 2.7% of the economy by 2027. The Government's longer-term path towards NATO's target of 3.5% of gross domestic product by 2035 is due to be set out at next year's spending review. Mr Healey previously resigned as defence secretary in a dispute over funding, arguing that the Government needed a plan to reach 3% of GDP in 2030. The OBR estimates that reaching that level would cost an additional £17.3billion in 2029/30. More than £600million is set to be committed to projects supporting the development and safe use of artificial intelligence. The planned funding includes: The investment is intended to support the development of AI while strengthening safeguards against potential threats. A £7million fund will be used to examine the feasibility of a potential future bid to host the Olympic and Paralympic Games in northern England. The funding would support a study into whether such a bid could be viable. It does not mean a bid to host the Games has been confirmed. An initial £285million is set to be allocated as part of plans to give mayors and regional leaders in England greater funding and powers. The aim is to allow local leaders to invest in projects in their areas and have more control over regional priorities. More than £1billion is set to be allocated to social and affordable housing. The funding forms part of the Government's wider plans to address housing needs and increase the availability of affordable homes. The Budget is also expected to include an additional £432million for the rough sleeping programme in England. The aim is to help get people off the streets by Christmas. Mr Burnham has said he wants “every single person” sleeping rough to receive an offer of help by the end of the year. The funding was disclosed ahead of the Budget, with the Government expected to set out further details as part of its spending plans. The state of the public finances will be a central issue in Mr Healey’s first Budget. The Chancellor has retained the fiscal rules established by his predecessor, Rachel Reeves. These require day-to-day spending to be funded by tax receipts rather than borrowing by 2029/30, while public debt as a share of the economy must also be falling in the same year. In March, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) forecast that the Government had around £24billion of headroom against its fiscal rules. However, higher borrowing costs could significantly reduce that buffer. The Resolution Foundation estimates that headroom may have fallen to around £12billion, while the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) believes it could still stand at approximately £20billion. The figures highlight the uncertainty facing the Chancellor as he considers how much additional support he can afford to offer households and businesses. The Chancellor say not, but some experts advise that it should. Antonia Medlicott, Founder and Managing Director of financial education specialists Investing Insiders, says: “I wouldn’t like to pay more income tax, and I’m sure nobody else would. But a transparent income tax rise is much better than a dozen smaller, stealthy tax grabs that sneak up on ordinary people and increase financial pressure on them. “The chancellor doesn’t have much headroom, and he has made a mistake by ruling out rises in income tax, employee national insurance, and VAT for working people. All three raise serious money. “The easiest of those to raise is the basic rate of income tax. A rise from 20 per cent to 21 per cent would raise about £8bn a year from 2027-28, according to HMRC. That’s about £224 a year for someone earning £35,000, or about £74 for a pensioner on £20,000. “Raising VAT would feed straight into inflation in the middle of an energy shock, while employee national insurance falls only on earnings, so the whole burden lands on workers. Income tax reaches pension income and rental income too, which spreads the load across a much wider base.” Recommended reading: John Healey will deliver the Budget on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Households will be watching for announcements affecting wages, fuel costs, energy bills and benefits, while businesses will be looking for details on tax, regulation and investment. Although several measures have already been announced, other proposals remain based on reports ahead of the Chancellor's statement and should not be treated as confirmed until the Budget is delivered.

metadata.title: Martin Lewis celebrates end of 'energy poll tax' as £108 Standing Charge axed
metadata.contentSnippet: Martin Lewis welcomes the planned abolition of the £108 gas standing charge in 2027, calling it an unfair energy poll tax after years of campaigning.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Martin Lewis celebrates end of 'energy poll tax' as £108 Standing Charge axed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Martin Lewis is celebrating the Government's decision to scrap the £108 gas standing charge, declaring an end to what he has branded an “energy poll tax”. The Money Saving Expert founder said he was “very pleased” after meeting Chancellor John Healey, who confirmed the fixed charge will be removed in 2027. The move marks a major victory for Mr Lewis, who said he had campaigned against standing charges for around six years. Standing charges are added to gas bills regardless of how much energy a household uses, meaning customers can face costs even when they make efforts to cut consumption. Mr Lewis has long argued that the system unfairly penalises people who use less gas, including those trying to keep their bills down. Announcing the news, he said: “I have confirmation that the standing charge on gas bills is to be scrapped in 2027. I've been campaigning on this for about six years, so I am very pleased to hear it.” He added: “It is a moral hazard. It disincentivizes people from cutting their bills. It's a poll tax on energy, if you like.” The typical gas standing charge costs around £108 a year, according to Mr Lewis. Under the planned changes, the charge will be removed and the costs shifted into the unit rate customers pay for each kilowatt hour of gas they use. Mr Lewis said he did not yet know the final increase to unit rates, but estimated it could be just under 1p per kilowatt hour. The changes could come into effect with the October 2027 energy price cap, although January 2028 is another possibility. The exact timing has yet to be confirmed. For households that use very little gas, scrapping the fixed fee could mean no longer paying the same daily charge as a much heavier user simply for having a gas supply. The reform is expected to benefit around 60% of households, with the Treasury estimating an average annual saving of £45 for those who gain. Although Mr Lewis welcomed the announcement, he warned that the change would not mean every household pays less. Because the costs will be transferred to unit rates, people who use more gas could end up paying more. He estimated the dividing line could be around 12,500 kilowatt hours of gas a year, although the final figure will depend on the rates eventually set. Around 40% of households could pay more under the new structure, according to his estimate. Mr Lewis also cited research by Nesta suggesting the majority of people in income groups below £100,000 would be better off following the change. He said vulnerable households with high energy use may need additional support if energy prices remain elevated when the reform comes into force. The gas announcement could also be the first step towards a wider shake-up of energy bills. Mr Lewis said Mr Healey would speak to Ofgem about how electricity standing charges could be removed, too. However, he said the Chancellor had described this as “trickier” and indicated it would take longer. For now, the confirmed plan relates to gas standing charges, with no timetable announced for electricity. The reform will primarily affect standing charges under the energy price cap. Suppliers will still be able to offer different pricing structures on other tariffs. Recommended reading: Mr Lewis also reassured people who already have a fixed energy tariff, saying the planned changes should not alter the rates they have agreed to pay. He said: “As for those on fixes: if you get a fix now, the rate of your fix is fixed, so this should not affect it. You will pay what you pay and if it has standing charges they will continue.” For millions of households, the end of the fixed gas fee will be a welcome move away from paying a charge that stays the same regardless of how much gas they use.

metadata.title: John Healey tipped to reverse one of Rachel Reeves' most unpopular Budget cuts
metadata.contentSnippet: John Healey is reportedly considering reversing plans to cut the annual ISA allowance from £20,000 to £12,000, in a potential Budget boost for savers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: John Healey tipped to reverse one of Rachel Reeves' most unpopular Budget cuts
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Chancellor John Healey is reportedly preparing to reverse plans to cut the annual ISA allowance from £20,000 to £12,000 in a potential boost for savers. The Chancellor is said to believe reducing the amount people can save tax-free was the wrong way to encourage more Britons to invest in stocks and shares, according to the Financial Times. Instead, Mr Healey is reportedly considering focusing on educating savers about the benefits of investing in the stock market. UNCONFIRMED: Reports in FT 2027 cash isa reduction for under 65s to £12,000 to be scrapped so it will stay at £20,000. — Martin Lewis (@MartinSLewis) October 28, 2026 The reported U-turn would reverse a decision announced by former chancellor Rachel Reeves at last year's autumn Budget. The proposed cut, which would apply to savers aged under 65, is due to come into force in April 2027. Individual Savings Accounts (ISAs) allow people to save or invest without paying tax on interest, dividends or capital gains within the account. The annual ISA allowance currently stands at £20,000, meaning eligible savers can put up to that amount into ISAs each tax year without paying tax on the returns. ISAs remain one of the UK's most popular savings products, with HM Revenue and Customs figures showing that around £135.7billion was paid into adult ISAs in the 2024/25 tax year. That was an annual increase of £32.7billion, with much of the growth coming from cash ISAs. Cash ISA subscriptions rose by 37.5%, an increase of £26.1billion, while subscriptions to stocks and shares ISAs increased by 19.7%, or £6.1billion. Lifetime ISA subscriptions also rose, increasing by 20.1%, equivalent to £472million. The figures suggest that cash ISAs accounted for much of the growth in ISA subscriptions, despite government efforts to encourage more people to invest. Recommended reading: The reported rethink would be a boost for savers who want to retain the flexibility to put up to £20,000 a year into tax-free accounts. It could also be welcomed by banks and building societies, which rely on savings deposits to help fund lending to households and businesses. The reported ISA U-turn would offer some relief to the banking sector ahead of today's Budget, with banks widely expecting the Chancellor to announce higher taxes on the industry. However, the ISA change has not been formally confirmed. The £12,000 limit remains a proposed change unless and until the Government announces otherwise.

metadata.title: Gas standing charges to be scrapped in major Budget energy bill shake-up
metadata.contentSnippet: Gas standing charges costing typical households around £108 a year are set to be scrapped from 2027, with the Treasury estimating 60% could save £45 annually.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Gas standing charges to be scrapped in major Budget energy bill shake-up
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Millions of households are set to see gas standing charges scrapped from 2027, in a major shake-up that could save some families money on their energy bills. The Treasury has announced that Chancellor John Healey will ask energy regulator Ofgem to remove the fixed daily fees “in 2027 or as soon as possible after”. Standing charges are added to gas bills regardless of how much energy a household uses. They cover the cost of delivering gas to homes and businesses and currently cost a typical household around £108 a year. The change is expected to affect around 23 million homes, with the Treasury saying the move could save 60% of households an average of £45 a year. However, the charges will not simply disappear from the energy system. Instead, the fixed costs will be transferred to the unit rate customers pay for each unit of gas they use. This means households that use less gas could benefit, while those that use more may face higher costs per unit. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: “Abolishing gas standing charges is about basic fairness and giving people more control over their bills. “I am determined to reform our broken energy market, so it better serves the public interest.” Simon Francis, coordinator of the End Fuel Poverty Coalition, said: "Removing the gas standing charge will bring real relief to many low-income households who use very little energy and for prepayment customers it could stop debt building up in the summer months. "It's also welcome that the Chancellor acknowledges that wider measures are needed to bring down bills and we will wait to see if he matches these words with more action in the Budget later." Mr Healey added: “Gas standing charges are unfair and outdated so I am scrapping them to give millions of households a bit of breathing space. “My Budget will draw a line in the sand on an energy policy that has failed British billpayers for years, letting extra costs on bills pile high and leaving households even more exposed to global shocks.” Recommended reading: The announcement comes as Mr Healey prepares to deliver his first Budget in the Commons on Wednesday afternoon. The Chancellor said the change would give families “breathing space” while making the energy system fairer. The precise timing of the change will depend on Ofgem, which has been asked to implement the reform from 2027 or as soon as possible afterwards.

metadata.title: Celebrity asks to block sexual misconduct claims, citing 'potentially fatal' impact
metadata.contentSnippet: An unnamed celebrity is seeking a High Court injunction to stop ITN and Guardian GNM from reporting sexual misconduct allegations.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Celebrity asks to block sexual misconduct claims, citing 'potentially fatal' impact
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A celebrity has asked the High Court to block publication of sexual misconduct allegations, arguing it could have "potentially fatal" consequences. The unnamed public figure is seeking an injunction to prevent ITN and Guardian News and Media (GNM) from revealing claims that he used his status over many years to pursue "inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women". The man denies all allegations, according to the BBC, including suggestions that he abused his position to contact and form relationships with teenagers and young women for sexual purposes. ‘Well-known individual’ suing two news outlets to halt publication of claims linked to 'inappropriate sexual activities' https://t.co/phZU4JS2oE — LBC (@LBC) October 28, 2026 Sara Mansoori KC, representing the celebrity, told the court that publication would carry a "potentially fatal impact," citing evidence of severe mental health risk. Ms Mansoori said: "The only reason they would not be fatal is because the claimant would be locked up and prevented from his desire to end his life. "This is not a case where an individual has spuriously raised 'mental health' concerns in the face of an impending publication that they do not wish to occur. "The claimant has attempted suicide twice as a result of these matters, been hospitalised for months, been the subject of involuntary detention and been examined by multiple – now more than 10 – doctors." She told the court that the man had already made one suicide attempt after receiving letters from the news organisations seeking his response to the allegations, and later attempted to take his own life a second time after absconding from hospital. The claimant, who is referred to in court as PPT, "has no intention of returning to public life," Ms Mansoori said. A medical report submitted to the court stated that inpatient treatment could offer "significant, but not complete mitigation of the risk," and that treatment, perhaps for months, had "a realistic potential to reduce the risk". Mr Justice Nicklin, who is presiding over the case, emphasised the public interest in the proceedings but warned against speculation or attempts to identify the individual. He said: "The existence of online speculation, however confidently expressed or widely repeated, does not authorise anyone to identify, or purport authoritatively to identify, PPT in connection with these proceedings. "Nor does repetition transform speculation into established fact." The judge clarified that the case is not about determining the truth or accuracy of the allegations, but rather whether they can be lawfully published. Gavin Millar KC, representing the news organisations, argued that there was a strong public interest in publishing the allegations, which he said formed a "pattern of behaviour." Mr Millar said "numerous allegations" had been gathered during a "wide-ranging and rigorous investigation", with reporters having spoken to more than 100 people. He told the court that "many of the women have been traumatised by the claimant's alleged conduct and have suffered mental health crises and mental illness as a result". Mr Millar acknowledged the seriousness of the suicide risk but argued that "the state may have a responsibility to protect life," but doing so in this case would require the state to "intervene in lawful journalistic activities to prevent an autonomous act by the claimant himself." He suggested that the risk could be mitigated and that there was "no proper basis to restrain the publication of public interest journalism." Justice Nicklin described the matter as "a difficult and important case" and said the court would determine the outcome "fairly, on the evidence and legal submissions." He confirmed that his decision would focus solely on whether the allegations can be published, not on their truth or accuracy.

metadata.title: 12 ways John Healey’s Budget 2026 plans could affect your money
metadata.contentSnippet: Find out what John Healey’s Budget 2026 means for your money, from £100 bank payments and pension tax changes to cash ISAs, fuel duty and savings.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 12 ways John Healey’s Budget 2026 plans could affect your money
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Chancellor John Healey has unveiled a series of measures aimed at easing the cost of living, supporting pensioners and helping households manage their finances. From £100 energy payments and changes to pension tax to a freeze on the cash ISA allowance and new help for first-time buyers, the Budget contains several announcements that could affect what people pay, save and receive. Here are 12 key changes and what they could mean for your money. Around 20 million households in council tax bands A to D will receive a £100 payment directly into their bank accounts this winter to help with rising energy bills. The Government said the scheme would cost £2.6billion and provide support during the coldest months. The Chancellor also extended the cut to VAT on electricity until July, which he said would take £50 off the annual price cap. Pensioners whose income is no higher than the value of the full new State Pension will not pay income tax under the Government’s new pension tax allowance during this Parliament. The measure is intended to protect pensioners receiving the full new State Pension from income tax as payments rise. However, pensioners with additional private pensions, earnings or savings interest could still need to consider their total taxable income. More than 13 million State Pension recipients are set to receive a 3.9% increase from April next year under the triple lock. The increase will provide a boost to pensioners’ regular income, although the amount each person receives will depend on their entitlement and whether they receive the new or old State Pension. The Chancellor also promised that every penny of the pension fund surplus for ex-mineworkers would go to miners, alongside a commitment to continue working towards the full transfer of the guarantor’s fund. Martin Lewis said the Chancellor had told him that gas standing charges would be scrapped in 2027. The MoneySavingExpert founder said the charge currently costs around £108 a year, but warned that the cost would be shifted to unit rates. That means households would pay more for each unit of gas they use instead. Mr Lewis estimated that around 60% of people could pay less, while 40% could pay more, depending on their consumption. The Chancellor is also expected to discuss removing electricity standing charges with Ofgem, although this is considered more complicated. Motorists will continue to benefit from the 5p-a-litre fuel duty cut until July 2027. The Chancellor said the extension would help households, hauliers and farmers amid continued pressure on fuel prices. He also announced that the higher mileage allowance for people using their cars for work would increase from 25p to 35p per mile. The increase to the standard mileage rate introduced earlier this year will also become permanent. Savers will be able to continue putting up to £20,000 a year into a cash ISA without paying tax on the interest. The Chancellor abandoned a planned reduction to the tax-free cash ISA limit, saying the allowance would remain unchanged for people of all ages. He also announced plans to work with the sector to create a new Starter ISA aimed at rewarding first-time investors. The decision will be welcome news for savers who want to keep their money in cash while protecting the interest they earn from tax. The Chancellor announced £4.7billion in Government-backed lending for a new Your First Home equity loan scheme, due to launch next spring. The scheme is intended to help first-time buyers who do not have financial support from family. He also announced plans for a new First Time Buyer ISA to replace the Lifetime ISA. In addition, the Government will end the Lifetime ISA penalty for people buying homes costing more than £450,000. Those affected will get back at least what they paid in, according to the Chancellor. The changes could be significant for aspiring homeowners struggling to save a deposit or facing property prices above the existing Lifetime ISA limit. The National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage will increase by 3.9%, benefiting 2.3 million of the lowest-paid workers. The Chancellor said the increase was intended to help people manage everyday costs, including the weekly shop. The actual benefit will depend on the rate each worker currently receives, their age and the number of hours they work. The Government will change Carer’s Allowance rules so people no longer lose their entire benefit because they earn just a penny above the earnings limit. The Chancellor said the cliff edge would be removed, allowing carers to keep some support as their earnings rise. The change is intended to make it easier for people to combine paid work with caring responsibilities without risking the loss of their entire allowance over a small increase in income. The Government is suspending tariffs on more than 100 supermarket products in an attempt to keep prices down. The Chancellor said the move was intended to help households with the cost of the weekly shop. The impact on individual shoppers will depend on how retailers pass on any savings, so it does not guarantee that every affected product will become cheaper. The Chancellor announced changes to how self-assessed income tax is collected, with affected taxpayers expected to make smaller, more regular payments rather than facing large bills that can be harder to pay. The changes could help people manage their cash flow and budget for tax more consistently. However, the announcement concerns the timing of payments rather than an automatic reduction in the amount of tax owed. The Chancellor also announced that the tax-free trading allowance for people earning money from a new venture would rise from £1,000 to £3,000. Self-employed fathers and partners will become eligible for paid parental leave for the first time. The Chancellor described the announcement as a first step towards wider change, saying he had listened to calls from MPs about paternity leave. The measure could provide additional financial support to eligible self-employed parents following the arrival of a child. The announcement did not set out all the detailed eligibility rules or payment arrangements, so further information will be needed to establish exactly who qualifies and how much they will receive. Recommended reading: The biggest immediate help announced by the Chancellor includes the £100 energy payment for eligible households, the extension of the electricity VAT cut and the continued fuel duty reduction. Pensioners will also be watching the new pension tax allowance and the 3.9% State Pension increase, while savers have been given certainty that the cash ISA allowance will remain at £20,000. Other measures, including the gas standing charge changes and new first-time buyer support, will take longer to come into effect.

metadata.title: Budget 2026 - what John Healey has promised pensioners and what it means for you
metadata.contentSnippet: The State Pension rise is part of a wider pledge from the Government to improve support for older people

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Budget 2026 - what John Healey has promised pensioners and what it means for you
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The State Pension rise is part of a wider pledge from the Government to improve support for older people, with the Chancellor setting out a vision for a new settlement for pensioners and their families. He said: "A new settlement for older generations, a rising state pension, and a national care service that is there when older people need it, taking the burden off families, taking the burden off our NHS." The comments put the focus on more than the annual State Pension increase, with access to care also featuring in the Government's plans for older generations. For pensioners, the key questions are how the expected 3.9% State Pension rise will affect their weekly income, whether changes to tax thresholds will leave more people paying income tax on their pension, and what a proposed national care service would mean for people who need support in later life. Money Saving Expert founder Martin Lewis said the announcement meant pensioners with income up to the value of the full new State Pension would not pay tax, but warned that the precise mechanism had not yet been explained. He said: “Pensioners with income up to the value of the full new state pension (to be £13,040 from April 2027) will not pay tax. Mechanism not stated, I suspect there will be an effective increased pensioner allowance with a clawback for income above that. More when I know more.” The full new State Pension is expected to rise to around £250.70 a week from April 2027, taking annual payments above £13,000 for the first time if the projected increase is confirmed. However, the amount each person receives will depend on their National Insurance record, while the wider impact of the Budget will also depend on the detail of any tax and social care measures announced.

metadata.title: Coffee sold at TK Maxx recalled over mould toxin above legal limit
metadata.contentSnippet: A batch of Bialetti caramel ground coffee sold at TK Maxx has been recalled. Check the batch code, best-before date and refund advice.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Coffee sold at TK Maxx recalled over mould toxin above legal limit
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A batch of ground coffee has been recalled over a mould toxin. Bialetti's Perfetto Moka caramel-flavoured coffee, sold at TK Maxx, contained ochratoxin A above the permitted limit, according to recall notices from the retailer and manufacturer. The recall applies to 250g packs with batch code LC5 BD149T and a best-before date of May 29, 2027. TK Maxx said the coffee was sold in its stores between July and November 2025. An urgent recall has been issued for the Bialetti Perfetto Moka Ground Coffee Flavoured with Caramel after it was found to contain levels of Ochratoxin A above the permitted limit (Image: Kennedy News & Media) Customers with the affected coffee are being told not to consume it and to return it. In its recall notice, TK Maxx said: "This product is being recalled because testing identified levels of Ochratoxin A above the permitted limit." The retailer said the coffee could be returned to any TK Maxx or Homesense store for a full refund or replacement. Bialetti said customers returning the affected batch to the point of purchase would receive a full refund even without a receipt. Ochratoxin A is a naturally occurring toxin produced by certain moulds, according to the Food Safety Authority of Ireland, which also issued an alert about the batch. The authority said consuming the affected product does not pose an immediate health risk, but continuous consumption over a long period may pose a potential risk. It advised consumers not to use the affected batch and said exposure to the toxin should be minimised. Bialetti said in its notice: "If you have a package from this batch at home, please do not consume it and return it to the point of purchase." Customers with questions can contact Bialetti at product.recall@bialettigroup.com.

metadata.title: Nine-mile walk from Northstowe to Landbeach raises funds for homeless people
metadata.contentSnippet: A sponsored walk from Northstowe to Landbeach has raised funds and awareness for people experiencing homelessness in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Nine-mile walk from Northstowe to Landbeach raises funds for homeless people
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A sponsored walk from Northstowe to Landbeach has raised funds and awareness for people experiencing homelessness in Cambridgeshire. The approximately nine-mile walk was organised by TU Cleaning Service in support of Emmaus Cambridge and took place on October 10 to mark World Homeless Day. Thana, director and founder of TU Cleaning Service, said: "We're still feeling amazing about the walk and the incredible support and donations we received. "It was such a rewarding experience for us as a team and we're really proud of everyone who took part and helped make it happen. "As a cleaning business, we believe everyone deserves somewhere clean, safe, and dignified to call home. "Together, we're walking to make a difference." Sponsored walk for homelessness charity Emmaus Cambridge is a step in the right direction for World Homeless Day (Image: Emmaus Cambridge) The team set off from Northstowe and finished at the Emmaus Cambridge site in Landbeach, raising funds and collecting essential items for the charity’s residents along the way. Donations included toiletries and household goods for the Emmaus Cambridge charity shop. Emmaus Cambridge supports people who have experienced homelessness by providing a 45-bedroom community home. The charity offers tailored support, training, and work experience to help people move forward. Supporters can contribute to the fundraiser by visiting gofundme.com/f/world-homeless-day-walk. More information about the charity and its work can be found at emmaus.org.uk/cambridge.

metadata.title: LNER train passengers 'ran for their lives' in 'sheer terror', court hears
metadata.contentSnippet: The prosecution told Anthony Williams’ trial the passengers "ran for their lives" in "sheer terror" amid a knife attack on board an LNER train last year.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: LNER train passengers 'ran for their lives' in 'sheer terror', court hears
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The prosecution told Anthony Williams’ trial the passengers "ran for their lives" in "sheer terror" amid a knife attack on board an LNER train last year. Several people were injured on an LNER train from Doncaster to London King's Cross on November 1, 2025 which was forced to make an emergency stop in Huntingdon. Anthony Williams, 33, denies 14 counts of attempted murder: ten of them in relation to the LNER train, three said to have happened in Peterborough and one at Pontoon Dock DLR station in London. Earlier this month, Williams pleaded guilty to 10 counts of wounding with intent relating to the incident on the LNER train, the wounding with intent of a man at Pontoon Dock DLR station in the early hours of November 1 and to the wounding with intent of a 14-year-old boy in Peterborough on October 31, as well as a number of other offences. His trial opened at Cambridge Crown Court this morning (October 28). Prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC told the court: "To the many people he encountered, the defendant Anthony Williams posed a dangerous threat, marauding through towns and cities, on streets and trains alike, armed with a knife." He told the court that Williams was "striking out at them when they were defenceless and in fear". Mr Paxton told the court: "In sheer terror, passengers ran for their lives. "They could go no further, they were trapped on a moving train." The court heard that the victims were "no threat to the defendant, nor were any others he encountered on that train". He added: "We the prosecution say that when he attacked those with a knife, he had intention to kill." The trial continues.

metadata.title: £100 energy bill support to be sent directly to bank accounts for 20 million people
metadata.contentSnippet: John Healey has announced a £100 energy payment for 20 million households in council tax bands A to D, with money paid directly into bank accounts this winter.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: £100 energy bill support to be sent directly to bank accounts for 20 million people
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Chancellor John Healey has announced a £100 energy payment for 20 million households in England in council tax bands A to D, with the money paid directly into bank accounts to help with rising energy bills this winter. The £2.6billion scheme is designed to give families breathing space during the coldest months, as households face pressure from energy costs and the impact of conflict in the Middle East. Announcing the measure in his Budget, Mr Healey told MPs: “Madam Deputy Speaker, let me say this to families at home: I know that with the conflict in the Middle East, rising energy bills are a real worry. “I know that people look to government at times like this not to solve all their problems, but to give them a bit of breathing space. “So today, I'm taking one further step. This winter, for 20 million households in council tax bands A to D, I'm announcing a £100 energy payment for households, paid directly into people's bank accounts to deal with rising energy bills. “That's a £2.6 billion scheme to take the pressure off in the coldest months and see people through to the spring.” The Chancellor said the Scottish, Welsh and Northern Ireland governments would receive their share of the funding, and urged them to introduce similar support for households in their nations. He added: “Madam Deputy Speaker, 50 pounds off VAT, 100 pounds off council tax, for this winter two tax cuts for next year fairer bills, and for the long term radical reform of the energy market to produce cheaper power.” The payment is intended for households in council tax bands A to D, with the money paid directly into bank accounts. The announcement sets out a £100 payment for eligible households this winter, but further details on how payments will be administered and when the money will arrive have not been provided in the statement quoted above. The Chancellor said the devolved governments would receive funding to support households in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, but called on them to take their own action to provide similar help. Households should wait for further official guidance on eligibility and payment arrangements before assuming they will receive the money automatically. The energy payment is part of a wider Budget package that Mr Healey said would support working people while maintaining the Government's commitment not to raise taxes on “working people”. The Chancellor told MPs that the Budget was designed to provide breathing space on the cost of living and the cost of doing business, support businesses and growth, and tackle longer-term challenges including energy, national security, public services and housing. Recommended reading: He said the Government had £15billion of fiscal headroom in 2029 to 2030, rising to £22billion in 2030 to 2031. Mr Healey also said the Budget would put the public finances on course to eliminate the current budget deficit within three years. “That is what a buffer is for, use it when you need it, rebuild it when you can,” he said. “And so despite the global challenges, this Budget puts us on track to eliminate the current budget deficit and get Britain’s finances into the black within three years.”

metadata.title: Minimum wage to increase to £13.20 an hour as John Healey announces Budget pay boost
metadata.contentSnippet: Chancellor John Healey has announced a 3.9% rise in the National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage, affecting 2.3 million of the lowest-paid workers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Minimum wage to increase to £13.20 an hour as John Healey announces Budget pay boost
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Chancellor John Healey announced he will increase the national minimum wage and national living wage by 3.9%, taking the over 21 rate from £12.71 to £13.20 an hour. He said: "For 2.3 million of our lowest paid workers, I am increasing both the national minimum wage and the national living wage by 3.9%.” Mr Healey opened his Budget statement by saying it is for “the working people of Britain, for British businesses, big and small”, built on “fiscal discipline”. He said: “First, by giving Britain some breathing space on the cost of living and the cost of business, “Second, backing the enterprise of British business to unleash innovation and growth in every postcode “And third, by tackling the big challenges on energy, on national security, on public service transformation and on housing.” The real Living Wage and the Government’s National Living Wage are often confused, but they are different pay rates with different purposes. The National Living Wage is the legal minimum employers must pay eligible workers aged 21 and over. The real Living Wage is a voluntary rate calculated independently to reflect the cost of living, with a separate, higher rate for London. The real Living Wage currently stands at £14.10 an hour across the UK and £15.45 in London. The key difference is that the Government’s rates are legal minimums, while the real Living Wage is a voluntary benchmark based on the cost of living. Recommended reading: The real Living Wage is a voluntary employer commitment that covers workers aged 18 and over. Nearly 17,000 employers, including IKEA, KPMG and LUSH, have signed up to pay it, according to the Living Wage campaign. The movement says almost half a million workers receive a pay increase each year as a result. However, workers do not automatically have a legal right to the real Living Wage. They are entitled to the statutory minimum that applies to them unless their employer has committed to a higher rate or their contract provides for one.

metadata.title: Train stabbings accused used stolen Stevenage knives to attack man, court hears
metadata.contentSnippet: The man accused attempted murder following the Huntingdon train stabbings used knives he stole from Stevenage to attack a man in London, a court has heard.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Train stabbings accused used stolen Stevenage knives to attack man, court hears
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The man accused attempted murder following the Huntingdon train stabbings used knives he stole from a Stevenage store to attack a man in London, a court has heard. Anthony Williams, 33, denies 14 counts of attempted murder: 10 of them in relation to the LNER train, three for offences in Peterborough and one in London, with his trial beginning today (October 28). Several people were injured on an LNER train from Doncaster to London King's Cross on November 1, 2025. The train made an emergency stop in Huntingdon. In the early hours of November 1, Williams is accused of stabbing a man at at Pontoon Dock DLR station, with Cambridge Crown Court court hearing the knife he used in the attack was stolen from a store in Stevenage. Prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC said that after a person was seen jumping onto train tracks and leaving Stevenage station, Williams was spotted at Asda. Williams went there with the "sole purpose of stealing a large knife”, and took a "pack of four kitchen knives which he puts down his trousers before walking out of the store". "As he does so he can be seen drinking from a bottle,” he said, adding that Williams has pleaded guilty to stealing the pack of knives. Mr Paxton said that "some hours later the defendant Mr Williams discards, throws away, this same empty pack of knives close to some bins in Old Castle Street in the city of London". He said that one of the knives “which was the largest knife was kept by the defendant who used it to stab" a man at Pontoon Dock DLR station in London. Earlier this month, Williams pleaded guilty to 10 counts of wounding with intent relating to the incident on the LNER train, the wounding with intent of a man at Pontoon Dock DLR station in the early hours of November 1 and to the wounding with intent of a 14-year-old boy in Peterborough on October 31, as well as a number of other offences. The trial continues.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire council pledges £2m to tackle EHCP assessment delays
metadata.contentSnippet: Long waits for vital education, health and care plan (EHCP) assessments could finally be addressed as part of a new funding push in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire council pledges £2m to tackle EHCP assessment delays
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Long waits for vital education, health and care plan (EHCP) assessments could finally be addressed as part of a new funding push in Cambridgeshire. Up to £2 million has been pledged by Cambridgeshire County Council to tackle the long waiting times for families applying for Education, Health & Care Plan (EHCP) assessment in Cambridgeshire. The funding was approved at a meeting of the council’s children and young people committee on Tuesday, October 20. Cllr Edna Murphy, chair of the committee, said: "We know that the council’s performance on EHCP assessments has not been good enough. "While service delivery has improved significantly over the last year, these improvements have been outstripped by a continued unprecedented increase in demand. "I want to apologise to the families who have been kept waiting, in some cases far beyond the statutory deadline, and reassure them that improving the timeliness and quality of the EHCP processes is an absolute priority for us. "We’re working hard to provide fair opportunities and the best possible start in life for all Cambridgeshire’s children and young people, regardless of need – so I’m really pleased we have today supported additional investment that aims to tackle the long waiting times for assessments. "We will be carefully and closely monitoring the impact of this new programme, which I fully expect will prove to be a decisive turning point for the waiting families across our county." Under current law, assessments must be completed within 20 weeks, but rising demand has led to significant delays in Cambridgeshire. The additional investment will fund a 12-month recovery programme, prioritising the longest-waiting and highest-risk cases, subject to final approval by the council’s strategy and resources committee.

metadata.title: Hunts train attack victim asked 'am I going to die today?', court hears
metadata.contentSnippet: A train passenger who was stabbed in an attack on board an LNER train at Huntingdon asked medics “am I going to die today?”, a court heard.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hunts train attack victim asked 'am I going to die today?', court hears
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A train passenger who was stabbed in an attack on board an LNER train asked medics “am I going to die today?”, a court heard. Several people were injured on an LNER train from Doncaster to London King's Cross on November 1, 2025, and the train was forced to make an emergency stop in Huntingdon. Anthony Williams, 33, denies 14 counts of attempted murder: ten of them in relation to the LNER train, three said to have happened in Peterborough and one at Pontoon Dock DLR station in London. He has pleaded guilty to 10 counts of wounding with intent relating to the LNER incident, but denies the 10 attempted-murder charges concerning those passengers. Jonathan Gjoshe boarded the London-bound train at Doncaster before he saw a man dressed all in black pull out a knife, prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC said at Williams' trial today (October 28). Mr Gjoshe believed Williams was following him and told other passengers: “Please make sure he's not following me”, the court heard. Jurors heard that Mr Gjoshe screamed at other passengers: “Just run, just run, there’s a guy with a knife. I’ve been stabbed. I’ve been stabbed”. Mr Paxton told the court that Mr Gjoshe asked medics: “Am I going to die today or not?” when he was taken to hospital after the attack. The trial will continue on October 29.

metadata.title: Royal Mail sets Christmas 2026 posting dates for UK parcels, cards and gifts

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Royal Mail sets Christmas 2026 posting dates for UK parcels, cards and gifts
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Royal Mail has revealed their deadlines for Christmas post. Christmas cards sent Second Class should be posted by December 18. That is Royal Mail's last recommended date for Second Class and Second Class Signed For items travelling within the UK in time for Christmas 2026. First Class senders have until Monday, December 21, while the last recommended date for Special Delivery Guaranteed is Wednesday, December 23. Royal Mail advises posting as early as possible and says its published dates are subject to change. The company's last posting dates for UK inland services are: Saturday, December 19 is also the last posting date for Royal Mail Tracked Returns 48 to arrive back with the sender before Christmas. The Post Office says parcels must be received before a branch's final acceptance time, which varies between branches, and advises customers to check before posting. For Parcelforce Worldwide UK services, the last posting date is Monday, December 21 for express48 and express48large. The deadline for express10, expressAM and express24 is Tuesday, December 22. People sending cards and parcels overseas are advised by Royal Mail to post as early as possible, particularly for international deliveries. Its Christmas page directs customers to its country guides for published international delivery aims rather than listing individual Christmas deadlines for each destination. Separate dates apply to mail sent from the UK to British Forces Post Office addresses around the world. For Operations and HM Ships, the last posting date from the UK is November 17, with November 24 the last arrival date at BFPO. The last UK posting date for Static Firm Base/PJOBs was October 24, with October 30 listed as the last arrival date at BFPO. For mail returning to the UK from BFPO locations, including HM Ships, Royal Mail says the target deadline is Wednesday, December 16, to allow time for delivery before Christmas.

metadata.title: Budget 2026 5 changes that could affect your money before Christmas
metadata.contentSnippet: Five Budget measures have been revealed ahead of Wednesday, including mileage allowance changes, cheaper food, parental pay and support for carers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Budget 2026 5 changes that could affect your money before Christmas
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Ahead of the Budget 2026 tomorrow Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey have announced five “everyday fixes” covering work-related travel, food prices, parental pay and support for unpaid carers, alongside plans to make sending and returning parcels easier. The measures are expected to feature in Wednesday’s Budget, with Mr Burnham promising further action to help families and businesses. Millions of employees and self-employed people who drive for work are set to benefit from changes to the tax-free mileage allowance. The Government will make the existing 55p-a-mile rate permanent for the first 10,000 business miles. For mileage above that threshold, the rate will increase from 25p to 35p per mile. The Government expects the overall package to help around three million workers. Shoppers could save money on their food bills after ministers announced plans to remove tariffs on more than 100 products. Popular items including baked beans, chocolate and gherkins are among the goods covered by the changes. The Treasury estimates the tariff cuts will save households around £21 on food shopping over the course of a year. The changes are also intended to reduce costs for farmers by cutting tariffs on fertilisers, while households that use kerosene for heating could benefit from a separate tariff reduction. More than 150,000 parents a year are expected to benefit from an extension to parental pay. The changes will include self-employed fathers who have previously missed out on the support. The measure is intended to give more parents financial support during the early weeks of their child's life. Further details are expected as the Budget measures are set out. The Government has promised to end the controversial Carers’ Allowance earnings cliff edge. Under the current system, unpaid carers can lose their entire benefit if they earn even a few pence above the weekly earnings limit. The Government plans to introduce a taper instead, reducing the benefit by £1 for every £1 earned above the limit. The change is intended to prevent carers from suddenly losing all their support when they take on extra paid work. The Government is also rolling out hundreds of additional Post Office drop boxes. The aim is to reduce the number of people who have to queue at counters to send or return parcels. The extra facilities are expected to be particularly useful in the run-up to Christmas, when parcel volumes typically rise. The Prime Minister said the Government wanted to address everyday financial pressures alongside its wider economic plans. He said: “We are taking on the big challenges facing the country. But that doesn’t mean losing sight of the everyday problems that cost people money or simply aren’t fair. “If you’re a nurse driving for work, a parent spending those precious first weeks with your new baby, or an unpaid carer picking up an extra shift, these changes will make life a little easier and put more money back in your pocket. “And at Wednesday’s Budget, we’ll go further to give families and businesses the breathing space they need today, while we build a stronger economy, transform our country and bring down cost for people long-term.” Chancellor John Healey said the measures were only a small part of the Government's plans to ease pressure on household budgets. He said: “Today’s everyday fixes are just a small part of what we are doing to give families a bit of breathing space. “Conflict in the Middle East and Europe is hitting families here at home through higher everyday costs. “We can’t control global events, but we can act where we can make a difference.” Recommended reading: The Budget is also expected to deliver a £432million boost to help get homeless people off the streets by Christmas. Mr Burnham said he wanted to ensure “every single person” sleeping on the streets received an offer of help by the end of the year. The Prime Minister has indicated that further measures to support families and businesses will be announced in Wednesday’s Budget.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Some retailers have seen a dramatic increase in sales of essential goods after the government urged households to be prepared in the event of periods of disruption. This advice was given as part of the Be Ready campaign to help families cope if storms or heatwaves knock out power, water, phones, or broadband. Advice focuses on actions taken in advance, including keeping bottled water and non-perishable food at home. Officials said winter storms and summer wildfires demonstrated how conditions disrupt essential networks. Guidance recommending preparations for three days of disruption follows approaches already in place in countries such as France, Ireland and the Netherlands. The rise in sales came after Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said that people should stockpile goods to prepare for an emergency such as a cyber attack or an extreme weather event. The government’s checklist of nine essential items includes: Some retailers have reported increases in sales of essential goods following the government’s advice. A spokesperson for supermarket chain Iceland told BBC Newsnight: "It's clear consumers have listened to the government's message as we have seen a 40% increase in sales of tinned products over the weekend and strong sales of bottled water too. "Our supplies of these products remain healthy." Maplin saw sales of radios rise by 92%, torches by 284%, and power banks by 106%. Ollie Marshall, managing director at Maplin, said: "Within hours of the Be Ready announcement we saw people reach for the basics – a torch, a wind-up radio, a power bank. "Torch sales nearly quadrupled and radio sales almost doubled in three days. "These are simple, affordable products that keep a household connected and informed when the power goes out, and it's encouraging to see people taking the advice seriously." Recommended reading: Robert Dyas reported a 160% increase in radio sales compared with the previous week. Some independent retailers also reported a spike in sales of goods. metadata.title: Poundland could collapse as owners push for insolvency with jobs at risk
metadata.contentSnippet: Poundland could be broken up as owner Gordon Brothers weighs bids for parts of the discount retailer from Wilko, The Range, Poundstretcher and others.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Poundland could collapse as owners push for insolvency with jobs at risk
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Discount retailer Poundland could be broken up as its owners consider offers for parts of the business. Gordon Brothers, which acquired the chain for £1 last year, is currently evaluating multiple bids for the company. A spokesperson for Gordon Brothers said: "While Martin Property Group had been identified as the preferred bidder by Poundland’s management team, attention must now turn to other active bids. "As well as interest from buyers for the whole business, the sale process has also surfaced a number of formal and indicative offers for significant viable parts of the business from established retail operators. "These options will now be objectively evaluated, with a view to minimising uncertainty for Poundland’s people and all relevant stakeholders." A sales process for the business began last month following turnaround efforts that included a series of store closures. Irish real estate firm Martin Property Group was named as the preferred bidder by management earlier this month. Gordon Brothers is therefore assessing a number of other bids, largely from retail rivals, which would involve buying parts of the Poundland business and ultimately see the company enter insolvency. Wilko and The Range owner CDS Superstores, Poundstretcher owner Fortress and TG Jones owner Modella are all among companies interested in buying parts of the retailer. It comes after Trade Union Usdaw shared that it was concerned Gordon Brothers is risking workers' jobs. Usdaw has said that it is worried that Gordon Brothers may decide to pull out and put the company into administration. In a statement put out on Usdaw's website, Bally Auluk – Usdaw national officer said, "With thousands of jobs on the line, it is an absolute disgrace that Gordon Brothers has failed to engage with us to seek a secure future for the business." Usdaw added: "We found it difficult to understand why Poundland was being described as struggling, after the company recently announced they had returned to like-for-like sales growth and staff were being thanked for their ‘amazing efforts’." Poundland currently operates around 600 stores across the UK and employs approximately 12,000 workers. How do you feel about Poundland potentially being broken up? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Care Network celebrates 40 years after helping thousands across Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: A charity is celebrating 40 years of changing lives and strengthening communities across Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Care Network celebrates 40 years after helping thousands across Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A charity is celebrating 40 years of changing lives and strengthening communities across Cambridgeshire. Care Network Cambridgeshire marked the milestone with an event at the William Collyn Community Centre in Girton on Tuesday, October 6, bringing together staff, volunteers, clients, and supporters to reflect on its journey and future plans. Since becoming an established charity in 1986, Care Network has supported thousands of people across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, helping them overcome loneliness, rebuild confidence, access essential services and maintain their independence during challenging times. Sheila Stephenson, founder of Care Network, said: "I am over the moon as to where things have got to." CNC client Alisha (left) and CNC employee Sandra (right) (Image: CNC) One of the most moving moments of the event came when Alisha, a woman in her 20s, shared how Care Network supported her after major brain surgery. Living alone in a new area, she faced isolation, financial hardship, and health struggles. With help from the charity, she accessed financial support, improved her safety at home, and began building connections in her community. Alisha’s story highlighted that care and support are not just for older people—life’s challenges can affect anyone, regardless of age. Care Network began as a small project in Comberton in the 1970s and has since grown into a countywide charity offering services such as Help at Home, RISE, and Community Support. In 2025, it supported 2,479 people, with 94 per cent saying they felt less isolated and 90 per cent reporting improved independence. CNC event with attendees, employees, volunteers and trustees (Image: CNC) Lynda Phillips, chief executive of Care Network Cambridgeshire, said: "One of the things that we are really good at is that we build the support around the individual needs." The charity plans to expand its volunteer network and raise awareness of its services to reach even more people in the years ahead. It remains committed to supporting individuals, strengthening communities, and keeping people at the heart of everything it does.

metadata.title: St Ives landmark lit up as 68 babies remembered during Baby Loss Awareness Week
metadata.contentSnippet: A historic landmark was illuminated as part of a heartfelt tribute to bereaved families in St Ives.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: St Ives landmark lit up as 68 babies remembered during Baby Loss Awareness Week
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A historic landmark was illuminated as part of a heartfelt tribute to bereaved families in St Ives. The town’s medieval bridge and chapel, one of only four of its kind in the UK, was lit up during Baby Loss Awareness Week to raise awareness and offer a space for remembrance. It formed part of the third annual Ribbon Memorial Display, organised by town councillor Laura Thompson and held outside St Ives Methodist Church, who once again supported the memorial by providing use of their fencing. The memorial gave families a space to remember their babies (Image: Baby Loss Awareness Week) Cllr Thompson said: "I wanted to give parents the opportunity to talk about their baby and offer a physical act of remembrance. "I end the week with a roll call of names on the Facebook page, it is so important that parents hear their baby's name spoken aloud." This year, 68 babies were remembered during the week, with nearly 4,000 people viewing the roll call video online. The display was visited by the High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire, who shared his personal connection to the cause. He said: "My wife and I lost a baby very early in a pregnancy, so I feel very connected to this cause. The town’s Bridge and Chapel were illuminated for the awareness week (Image: Baby Loss Awareness Week) "The mayor, Cllr Alex Thompson, and I went to join in on the first day. "By the time we got to the memory wall – only an hour or so after it had opened – over a dozen ribbons had already been tied to the fence, many with loving messages and a child’s name." Eight businesses in St Ives also showed their support by decorating their windows in pink and blue. Cllr Thompson said: "My Facebook page, St Ives Baby Loss Support and Awareness – Cambridgeshire, was viewed over 67,000 times during Baby Loss Week. "These are huge figures and I will keep driving awareness in our town and giving people space to remember."
